paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
original_question: If G is a torsion-free group and H is a soluble normal subgroup of G with G/H a periodic Engel group, then can every G-invariant order on H be extended to make G an o-group?
self_contained_problem:
Definitions and setup. A group $G$ is called an o-group (orderable group) if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ that is two-sided invariant, i.e. $a \le b$ implies $xay \le xby$ for all $x,y \in G$. Given a normal subgroup $H \trianglelefteq G$, a total order $\le$ on $H$ is called $G$-invariant if it is preserved under conjugation by every element of $G$: $a \le b$ implies $g^{-1}ag \le g^{-1}bg$ for every $g \in G$ and $a,b \in H$. We say a $G$-invariant order on $H$ extends to make $G$ an o-group if there is a two-sided invariant total order on $G$ whose restriction to $H$ coincides with the given order.

A group is periodic if every element has finite order. A group $Q$ is called an Engel group if for every pair of elements $x,y \in Q$ there exists an integer $n = n(x,y) \ge 1$ such that the iterated commutator $[x,{}_n y] := [[\dots[[x,y],y],\dots],y]$ (with $y$ appearing $n$ times) is trivial. A group is soluble if it has a finite derived series ending in the trivial subgroup, and torsion-free if it has no nontrivial element of finite order.

Question. Suppose $G$ is a torsion-free group and $H$ is a soluble normal subgroup of $G$ such that the quotient $G/H$ is a periodic Engel group. Must every $G$-invariant total order on $H$ extend to a two-sided invariant total order on $G$ (so that $G$ becomes an o-group)?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an unsolved problem attributed to A. H. Rhemtulla in a compilation of open questions on ordered and orderable groups. No subsequent published resolution was found via search; status remains unverified.

paper_title: Some open problems related to stability
original_question: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and individual queues in front of the servers, where each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest queue or chooses among tied shortest queues at random. Under what conditions, if any, do the queue-length or workload distributions converge weakly or in total variation to stationarity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-server queue (for concreteness, take two identical servers) fed by a stationary and ergodic marked point process $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$, where $t_n\in\mathbb R$ are the arrival epochs of customers (with $t_n<t_{n+1}$) and $\sigma_n\ge 0$ is the service requirement of the $n$-th customer. Each server has its own dedicated queue, served in FIFO order. The routing discipline is join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ): upon arrival, customer $n$ instantaneously enters the queue with the smallest current queue length; if several queues are tied for the minimum length, the customer chooses one of them uniformly at random (independently of everything else).

Let $Q(t)=(Q_1(t),Q_2(t))$ denote the vector of queue lengths at time $t$ and $W(t)=(W_1(t),W_2(t))$ the vector of workloads (residual service times) at time $t$.

Determine general conditions on the stationary ergodic input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ — in particular, conditions beyond the i.i.d. or Markovian setting and not relying on monotonicity or Loynes-type constructions — under which the distribution of $Q(t)$ (or of $W(t)$) converges, as $t\to\infty$, weakly, or in total variation, to a stationary distribution. Equivalently, identify (or rule out the existence of) natural sufficient conditions guaranteeing such convergence to stationarity for the JSQ multi-server queue with general stationary ergodic input.
category_tag: Queueing theory / stability of stochastic networks
status_search_result: Although stability and ergodicity of join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) systems have been extensively studied under i.i.d. or Markovian assumptions (e.g., Foley–McDonald 2001, and various works on JSQ in the Halfin–Whitt regime and JSQ orbit queues), the question of weak or total-variation convergence to stationarity for multi-server JSQ queues with fully general stationary ergodic input remains, to the best of available evidence, open. The model lacks monotonicity and is not amenable to Loynes-type constructions, and no general result giving such conditions has been located in the literature.

paper_title: Open problems: Descending cohomology, geometrically
original_question: For a smooth projective threefold X over Q whose Tate-twisted third cohomology is expected to have a phantom abelian variety J(X)_Q, can this intermediate Jacobian or phantom abelian variety be constructed as, or at least in terms of, the Albanese variety of a Hilbert scheme that is geometrically attached to X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consider the third $\ell$-adic cohomology with Tate twist $H^3(X_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\mathbb{Q}_\ell(2))$, viewed as a Galois representation, and assume that there exists an abelian variety $J(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ — a so-called phantom abelian variety — whose $\ell$-adic Tate module realizes this Galois representation (so that, over $\mathbb{C}$, $J(X)_{\mathbb{C}}$ corresponds to the algebraic part of the Griffiths intermediate Jacobian of $X_{\mathbb{C}}$).

Question: Does there exist a Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_P(X)$ of subschemes of $X$ (for some choice of Hilbert polynomial $P$, or more generally a moduli space of subschemes geometrically attached to $X$ in a functorial way), defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that $J(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ can be constructed as the Albanese variety $\mathrm{Alb}(\mathrm{Hilb}_P(X))$, or as a quotient or factor of such an Albanese variety, with the construction recovering the expected identification of Tate modules with $H^3(X_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}},\mathbb{Q}_\ell(2))$?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this construction problem was located. The classical analogue (intermediate Jacobian of a cubic threefold realized as the Albanese of its Fano surface of lines) is known, but the general question of a uniform Hilbert-scheme/Albanese construction of a "phantom" abelian variety descending the algebraic part of $H^3$ to $\mathbb{Q}$ does not appear to have a known answer; it is posed as an open problem.

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
original_question: For all integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, does there exist an integer h(k, ℓ) such that every planar point set of at least h(k, ℓ) points contains either ℓ collinear points or k mutually visible points?
self_contained_problem:
Two distinct points p and q in a finite set S of points in the Euclidean plane are said to be mutually visible (with respect to S) if the open line segment joining p and q contains no other point of S. A subset C ⊆ S is called a visible clique if every pair of distinct points in C is mutually visible. A subset of S is called collinear if all its points lie on a common straight line.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every pair of integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, there exists an integer h(k, ℓ) such that every finite set S of at least h(k, ℓ) points in the Euclidean plane contains either ℓ collinear points or a visible clique of size k.
status_search_result: The big-line-big-clique conjecture remains open in general for finite planar point sets. It is known to hold for k ≤ 5 (the case k = 4 was established by Kára–Pór–Wood, and k = 5 by Abel et al.), and trivially for ℓ ≤ 3. The conjecture is open for all k ≥ 6 with ℓ ≥ 4. The infinite analogue was disproved by Pór and Wood (2010), and a strengthened "visible islands" variant was disproved in 2022.

Abel et al. verified the conjecture for k = 5 ... open for all k ≥6 and ℓ≥4", "claim": "Conjecture verified for k ≤ 5; open for k ≥ 6, ℓ ≥ 4."}, {"title": "The Big-Line-Big-Clique Conjecture is False for Infinite Point Sets", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2988", "snippet": "The infinite analogue is false", "claim": "Infinite version disproved."}, {"title": "Big Line or Big Clique in Planar Point Sets — Open Problem Garden", "url": "http://garden.irmacs.sfu.ca/op/big_line_or_big_clique_in_planar_point_sets", "snippet": "Open problem on visibility in planar point sets", "claim": "Listed as an open problem."}]

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
context_brief: Hamiltonian circuits in embedded segment visibility graphs
original_question: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle that becomes a non-self-intersecting Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph?
self_contained_problem:
Let S = {s_1, s_2, ..., s_n} be a finite set of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane in general position (no three segment endpoints collinear). The segment visibility graph G of S is the graph whose vertices are the 2n endpoints of the segments in S, and in which two vertices u and v are joined by an edge if and only if either (i) u and v are the two endpoints of the same segment in S, or (ii) the open segment uv does not meet any segment of S (i.e., u sees v among the obstacles S). The embedded segment visibility graph G' is the straight-line drawing of G obtained by drawing every edge of G as the corresponding straight line segment between its endpoints in the plane.

A Hamiltonian cycle in G is a cycle visiting each of the 2n vertices exactly once. Such a cycle is said to correspond to a (non-self-intersecting) Hamiltonian circuit in G' if, when its edges are drawn as straight line segments, no two of these segments cross each other.

Prove or disprove: for every finite set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in general position in the plane, the segment visibility graph G of S contains a Hamiltonian cycle that corresponds to a non-self-intersecting Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph G'.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved affirmatively by Hoffmann and Tóth, who proved that every segment visibility graph (for any finite family of pairwise disjoint segments in general position) contains a Hamiltonian cycle realizable as a non-self-intersecting straight-line Hamiltonian circuit, and gave an O(n log n) algorithm to construct it, building on a result of Bose, Houle, and Toussaint.

paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
context_brief: Alternating paths in embedded segment visibility graphs
original_question: In the embedded segment visibility graph G′ of a set S of n disjoint segments, is there always an alternating path containing at least O(log n) segments of S?
self_contained_problem: Let S be a set of n pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane in general position (no three segment endpoints collinear). The embedded segment visibility graph G' of S is the geometric graph whose vertices are the 2n endpoints of the segments of S, and whose edges consist of (i) the n segments of S themselves and (ii) all open visibility edges, i.e. pairs of endpoints p, q (belonging to possibly different segments) such that the open segment pq does not meet any segment of S. An alternating path in G' is a simple path whose edges alternate between segments of S and visibility edges. Prove or disprove: there exists a constant c > 0 such that for every such S of n disjoint segments, G' contains an alternating path that uses at least c log n segments of S.
status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to Urrutia, was proved by Hoffmann and Tóth: every set of n disjoint segments in general position admits an alternating path through Ω(log n) segments in its embedded segment visibility graph.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let S be a finite set of points in P^N. Suppose there exists m such that a(S,m)/m = (a(S,1)+N-1)/N, where a(S,m) is the least degree of a divisor vanishing to order at least m on S. Must S then either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration? More generally, if the Waldschmidt constant satisfies e(S) = (a(S,1)+N-1)/N, must the same conclusion hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a finite set of points over an algebraically closed field. For a positive integer $m$, define
$$\alpha(S,m) = \min\{\deg F : F \in k[x_0,\dots,x_N] \text{ is a nonzero homogeneous form vanishing to order } \geq m \text{ at every point of } S\},$$
and write $\alpha(S) := \alpha(S,1)$. Define the Waldschmidt constant of $S$ by
$$\widehat{\alpha}(S) = \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m} = \inf_{m \geq 1} \frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m}.$$

A star configuration of points in $\mathbb{P}^N$ is the set of points obtained as the pairwise intersections (codimension-$N$ flats) arising from a collection of hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^N$ in general linear position; equivalently, given $s \geq N$ hyperplanes meeting properly, $S$ is the set of points each of which is the intersection of exactly $N$ of these hyperplanes.

The Chudnovsky lower bound states that $\alpha(S,m)/m \geq (\alpha(S)+N-1)/N$ for all $m \geq 1$, hence $\widehat{\alpha}(S) \geq (\alpha(S)+N-1)/N$.

Question 1. Suppose there exists $m \geq 1$ such that
$$\frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m} = \frac{\alpha(S)+N-1}{N}.$$
Must $S$ either be contained in a hyperplane of $\mathbb{P}^N$ or be a star configuration?

Question 2. Suppose $\widehat{\alpha}(S) = (\alpha(S)+N-1)/N$. Must the same conclusion hold (i.e., $S$ is contained in a hyperplane or is a star configuration)?
status_search_result: Active research surrounds Chudnovsky's conjecture, Waldschmidt constants, and star configurations (e.g., proofs of Chudnovsky-type bounds for very general points, monomial ideals, and stable Harbourne–Huneke containments). However, no source found directly resolves the equality-case characterization asked here, so the status of the precise question appears unknown/open based on available evidence.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at points p1, ..., pr, and let D = dH - m1E1 - ... - mrEr. Assume that D is special, meaning that D is effective and h^1(X,D)>0. Must every positive multiple nD with n>1 also be special?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the blow-up of the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $r$ distinct (possibly general) points $p_1,\dots,p_r$, with exceptional divisors $E_1,\dots,E_r$, and let $H$ denote the pullback of the hyperplane class on $\mathbb{P}^2$. For integers $d, m_1,\dots,m_r$, consider the divisor
$$D = dH - m_1 E_1 - \cdots - m_r E_r$$
on $X$. Call $D$ special if $D$ is effective and $h^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X(D)) > 0$. Equivalently, the linear system of plane curves of degree $d$ with multiplicity at least $m_i$ at $p_i$ is non-empty and has dimension strictly greater than the expected dimension $\max\{-1, \binom{d+2}{2} - 1 - \sum_i \binom{m_i+1}{2}\}$.

Question: If $D$ is special, must $nD = ndH - nm_1 E_1 - \cdots - nm_r E_r$ also be special for every integer $n > 1$?
category_tag: linear systems on blow-ups of P^2
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this stability-of-speciality-under-multiplication question for linear systems on blow-ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. The problem is closely tied to the Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz conjecture and remains discussed in the literature on linear systems on rational surfaces, but no clear proof or counterexample to this specific multiplication question was located.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
context_brief: Cohomology of monomial subschemes on surfaces
original_question: With the same notation, let Y be a general subscheme of a smooth projective surface S corresponding to a monomial ideal I, and let D be a divisor on S. Find conditions on S, I, and D that determine or constrain the cohomology of I_Y ⊗ O_S(D), ideally giving criteria that force h^0(I_Y ⊗ O_S(D)) = max{0, h^0(O_S(D)) - n}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, and let $I \subset \mathcal{O}_S$ be a sheaf of ideals that is locally monomial: at every point $p \in S$ where $I$ is non-trivial, there exist local coordinates $(x,y)$ on $S$ at $p$ such that the stalk $I_p$ is generated by monomials $x^a y^b$. Let $Y \subset S$ be a general subscheme of the corresponding type, defined by the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_Y = I$, and write $n := \dim_k H^0(\mathcal{O}_Y) = \mathrm{length}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ for its colength. Let $D$ be a divisor on $S$ and consider the twisted ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D)$, fitting in the short exact sequence
$$0 \to \mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D) \to \mathcal{O}_S(D) \to \mathcal{O}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D) \to 0.$$
The naive expected value of $h^0(\mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D))$ is $\max\{0,\, h^0(\mathcal{O}_S(D)) - n\}$, corresponding to the conditions imposed by passing through $Y$ being independent on $|D|$.

Find geometric and numerical conditions on the triple $(S, I, D)$ that determine, or at least constrain, the cohomology groups $h^i(\mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D))$ for $i = 0, 1, 2$. In particular, give criteria on $(S, I, D)$ that force the equality
$$h^0(\mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D)) = \max\{0,\, h^0(\mathcal{O}_S(D)) - n\}.$$
category_tag: Linear series and ideal sheaves on surfaces
status_search_result: The question is a general open problem in the theory of linear series on surfaces, closely tied to interpolation problems (e.g., Nagata-type and SHGH conjectures for fat points, which are special cases of monomial subschemes). No general criteria forcing the expected value of $h^0$ for arbitrary monomial subschemes on arbitrary surfaces are known; the problem remains open in this generality, though partial results exist for specific surfaces (e.g., $\mathbb{P}^2$, blow-ups, abelian surfaces) and specific monomial ideal types.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group and let L be an ample line bundle on X. Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite étale cover p: X'→X such that either (1) the Seshadri number of p^*L at every point of X' is greater than N, or (2) the Seshadri number of p_e^*(p_1^*L \otimes p_2^*L) along the diagonal in X'	imes X' is greater than N? If not in general, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees such a positive answer?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective manifold and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Recall that the Seshadri constant of $L$ at a point $x \in X$ is
$$\varepsilon(L;x) \;=\; \inf_{C \ni x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\mathrm{mult}_x C},$$
where the infimum runs over all irreducible curves $C \subset X$ passing through $x$. For a smooth subvariety $D \subset X$, the Seshadri constant of $L$ along $D$ is
$$\varepsilon(L;D) \;=\; \sup\{\,t > 0 : \mu^*L - tE \text{ is nef}\,\},$$
where $\mu : \widetilde{X} \to X$ is the blow-up of $X$ along $D$ with exceptional divisor $E$.

Say that the algebraic fundamental group $\widehat{\pi}_1(X)$ is large if for every closed positive-dimensional subvariety $Z \subset X$, the image of $\pi_1(\widetilde{Z}) \to \widehat{\pi}_1(X)$ is infinite, where $\widetilde{Z} \to Z$ is a resolution of singularities.

Assume that $\widehat{\pi}_1(X)$ is large. For every real number $N > 0$, address the following:

(1) Does there exist a finite étale cover $p : X' \to X$ such that $\varepsilon(p^*L; x') > N$ for every $x' \in X'$?

(2) Letting $p_1, p_2 : X' \times X' \to X'$ be the two projections, does there exist a finite étale cover $p_e : Y \to X' \times X'$ (with $X' \to X$ a finite étale cover) such that the Seshadri constant of $p_e^*(p_1^*L \otimes p_2^*L)$ along the preimage of the diagonal $\Delta_{X'} \subset X' \times X'$ is greater than $N$?

(3) If the answer to (1) or (2) is negative or unclear in general, identify a condition on $\pi_1(X)$ that guarantees an affirmative answer.
status_search_result: Part (1) was answered affirmatively by G. Di Cerbo and L. F. Di Cerbo (arXiv:1411.1033, 2014; published 2019): if the algebraic fundamental group of X is large and L is ample, then Seshadri constants of pullbacks of L can be made arbitrarily large by passing to a finite étale cover, confirming a conjecture of J.-M. Hwang. Analogous statements hold under residual finiteness of π₁(X) and for big and nef line bundles outside the augmented base locus. Related work on moving Seshadri constants for varieties of maximal Albanese dimension also provides affirmative results in that setting. The diagonal version (2) is closely connected and follows in the cases treated, though the literature focuses on (1).

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let (R,m) be a regular local ring of dimension n and let I⊂R be an ideal of big height e. Determine whether the strengthened symbolic-power containments listed in Problem 2.8.2 hold, namely whether I^(m) is contained in m^{rn-r}I^r for m≥rn, in m^{rn-r-(n-1)}I^r for m≥ rn-(n-1), in m^{re-r}I^r for m≥re, and in m^{re-r-(e-1)}I^r for m≥ re-(e-1).
status_search_result: These strengthened containments (associated with the Harbourne–Huneke conjectures) remain open in general. A "stable" version, asserting the containments for all sufficiently large r (depending on I), has been established in various cases, and special cases (monomial ideals, generic points in P^2 and P^3, star configurations, characteristic-p settings) are known. However, counterexamples to some Harbourne-type strengthenings exist for certain radical ideals, so the full conjecture is not expected to hold uniformly. Overall, the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let f:Y→B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. Fix an integer g>0. Is there a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C contained in a fiber, with geometric genus g, satisfies C^2 ≥ -b(Y,g), where self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f \colon Y \to B$ be a surjective morphism from a smooth complex projective threefold $Y$ to a smooth projective curve $B$, and assume that the general fiber of $f$ is a smooth projective surface. By a vertical curve we mean a reduced irreducible curve $C \subset Y$ that is contained in some scheme-theoretic fiber $Y_t = f^{-1}(t)$; if $Y_t$ is the (possibly singular, possibly non-reduced) surface containing $C$, the self-intersection $C^2$ is computed on the surface $Y_t$ (or, when $Y_t$ is singular, on a suitable component/desingularization carrying $C$, with the self-intersection number understood inside that fiber).

Fix an integer $g > 0$. Question: does there exist a constant $b(Y,g) \in \mathbb{R}$, depending only on $Y$ and $g$, such that
$$C^2 \geq -b(Y,g)$$
holds for every vertical curve $C \subset Y$ whose geometric genus equals $g$?
status_search_result: The bounded negativity conjecture and its weak/family versions remain active research topics. Work on a "Weak Bounded Negativity Conjecture" (e.g., Harbourne et al., 2017) addresses related statements for individual surfaces but does not establish the uniform bound in fibered threefolds asked here. No source found that resolves the family version for vertical curves of fixed geometric genus, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map from the complete linear system |D| to |D|_E|, must all base points in the image come from a fixed base curve of |D|, and, if |D| has no fixed component, must the restriction map have maximal rank?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the blow-up of the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $r$ points in general position, let $D$ be an effective divisor on $X$, and let $E \subset X$ be a $(-1)$-curve (a smooth rational curve with self-intersection $-1$). Consider the restriction map
$$\rho \colon |D| \longrightarrow |D|_E|$$
between complete linear systems, induced by restriction of sections to $E$. Prove or disprove the following two statements:

1. Every base point of the linear system $\rho(|D|) \subset |D|_E|$ (the image of $\rho$) arises as the intersection with $E$ of a fixed component of the linear system $|D|$ on $X$.

2. If $|D|$ has no fixed component on $X$, then the linear map $\rho$ has maximal rank, i.e., it is either injective or surjective.
category_tag: Linear systems on blow-ups of P^2
status_search_result: No source was found stating that this specific conjecture about restriction of linear systems to (-1)-curves on general blow-ups of P^2 has been resolved.   C · C ≥ − b_s(X, g)?

paper_title: Observational properties of diffuse radio sources in Galaxy Clusters: Current knowledge and open questions
original_question: Do galaxy clusters that host ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos, meaning radio halos with GHz-frequency synchrotron spectral index around α ∼ 2 under the convention S ∝ ν^-α, have basic differences from galaxy clusters that host “classical” radio halos with typical spectral-index values around 1.2–1.4?
self_contained_problem: Consider galaxy clusters that host diffuse, Mpc-scale, centrally located synchrotron radio emission known as radio halos, whose integrated flux density S at frequency ν is modeled as a power law S ∝ ν^{-α} with spectral index α measured at GHz frequencies. Call a radio halo "classical" if its spectral index lies in the range α ≈ 1.2–1.4, and "ultra-steep-spectrum" if α ≈ 2. Determine whether galaxy clusters that host ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos differ in their fundamental physical properties (such as merger dynamical state, total mass, thermal/X-ray characteristics, or intracluster turbulence/energetics) from galaxy clusters that host classical radio halos, and identify any observational signatures that distinguish these two host populations.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2021–2025) continues to investigate ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos as a distinct subclass, with the working hypothesis that they trace less energetic mergers in lower-mass clusters under turbulent (re)acceleration models. Mass-selected samples and deep low-frequency observations (LOFAR, uGMRT) are still characterizing the host-cluster differences, and no definitive consensus distinguishes USSRH hosts from classical-halo hosts beyond merger energetics trends; the question remains open.

paper_title: Observational properties of diffuse radio sources in Galaxy Clusters: Current knowledge and open questions
context_brief: Integrated spectra of halos and relics
original_question: For radio halos and relics in galaxy clusters, what are their well-defined integrated radio spectra from roughly hundred-MHz frequencies to GHz frequencies, and what do the spectral shapes and spectral-index values reveal about the underlying relativistic electron population and the re-acceleration processes that generate the diffuse emission?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the diffuse, extended synchrotron radio emission observed from the intracluster medium of galaxy clusters, classified into two morphological types: (i) radio halos, which are large (~Mpc-scale), centrally located, low-surface-brightness sources roughly coincident with the X-ray-emitting thermal gas, and (ii) radio relics, which are elongated, often peripheral sources frequently associated with merger shock fronts. Both types of source emit via synchrotron radiation from a population of relativistic electrons (Lorentz factor γ ≫ 1) gyrating in cluster-scale magnetic fields of order ~µG. The integrated radio spectrum of such a source is the function S(ν) giving total flux density as a function of frequency ν, conventionally fit (locally) by a power law S(ν) ∝ ν^{−α} with spectral index α, but possibly exhibiting curvature (a high-frequency steepening or a low-frequency flattening) that constrains the energy distribution N(E) ∝ E^{−δ} of the emitting electrons and any cooling, injection, or re-acceleration processes acting on them.

The problem is the following:

(a) For each known radio halo and radio relic, determine the integrated radio spectrum S(ν) over the frequency range from approximately 100 MHz to several GHz, with sufficient frequency coverage and accuracy to detect spectral curvature and to measure the spectral index α (and any spatial variations of α via spectral imaging).

(b) From the measured spectral shapes and spectral-index values, infer the energy distribution and maximum energy of the underlying relativistic electron population, and identify the physical re-acceleration mechanism (e.g., second-order Fermi turbulent re-acceleration in halos versus diffusive shock acceleration or shock re-acceleration in relics, as opposed to purely secondary models in which electrons arise from hadronic collisions of cosmic-ray protons with thermal nuclei) that is consistent with these spectra. In particular, characterize whether and at what frequency the integrated halo spectra exhibit a high-frequency cutoff/steepening predicted by stochastic re-acceleration models, and whether relic spectra are consistent with the spectral-index/Mach-number relation predicted by diffusive shock acceleration.
status_search_result: Subsequent observations with LOFAR, MWA, uGMRT, and JVLA have substantially increased the number of halos and relics with measured integrated spectra from ~100 MHz to GHz, confirming features such as high-frequency steepening in some halos (e.g., the Coma cluster, A521) consistent with turbulent re-acceleration, and power-law/curved relic spectra broadly consistent with shock (re-)acceleration scenarios. However, tensions remain (e.g., relic Mach numbers inferred from radio versus X-ray, and the origin of seed electrons), and well-sampled spectra still exist only for a modest subset of sources, so the question is partially addressed but not fully resolved.

paper_title: Observational properties of diffuse radio sources in Galaxy Clusters: Current knowledge and open questions
original_question: Which galaxy clusters contain both a firmly detected shock front and a radio relic with a clear spatial and physical connection, and does a larger sample of such systems support the view that relics are produced by merger-driven shocks with Mach numbers less than or approximately equal to 3?
self_contained_problem:
Galaxy clusters frequently host extended, diffuse, polarized synchrotron sources at their peripheries known as radio relics. It is widely believed that relics trace merger-driven shock waves propagating through the intracluster medium, which (re)accelerate relativistic electrons. A "shock front" in this context is an X-ray–detected discontinuity in temperature and density (e.g., as identified with high-resolution X-ray imaging spectroscopy), characterized by a sonic Mach number M = v_s / c_s, where v_s is the shock speed and c_s is the upstream sound speed.

Problem. Compile the set of galaxy clusters in which (i) a shock front has been firmly detected through X-ray observations and (ii) a radio relic has been observed whose location, morphology, and polarization properties show a clear spatial and physical association with that shock front. For each such system, determine the Mach number of the shock from X-ray (and, where possible, radio spectral) measurements. Then decide whether the resulting sample is consistent with the hypothesis that radio relics are produced by merger-driven shocks with Mach numbers M ≲ 3, or whether it requires revising this expected Mach-number range.
category_tag: Galaxy cluster radio relics and merger shocks
status_search_result: Since 2011 the sample of clusters with both an X-ray–detected shock front and an associated radio relic has grown (e.g., A520, A754, A2163, CIZA J2242.8+5301, A3667, the Bullet Cluster, El Gordo). Recent observations and large MHD simulations (e.g., TNG-Cluster, 2024) confirm that most relic-associated shocks are weak merger shocks with Mach numbers in the range ~2–4, broadly consistent with M ≲ 3 but with some relics requiring higher Mach numbers and challenging simple diffusive-shock-acceleration efficiency. Thus the underlying observational program is ongoing and the Mach-number picture is partially confirmed but still under active investigation.

paper_title: Observational properties of diffuse radio sources in Galaxy Clusters: Current knowledge and open questions
context_brief: Population status of ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos
original_question: Are ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos a genuine population of diffuse cluster radio sources rather than only two confirmed objects, and would finding more such halos provide observational support for the turbulent re-acceleration model of radio-halo formation?
self_contained_problem:
In the context of diffuse non-thermal radio emission from galaxy clusters, a giant radio halo is a Mpc-scale, low-surface-brightness, centrally located synchrotron source whose integrated radio spectrum follows a power law S_ν ∝ ν^α. A radio halo is called ultra-steep-spectrum (USSRH) if its spectral index satisfies α < −1.5 (equivalently, the spectrum is steeper than this value over the observed frequency range). Within the turbulent re-acceleration model, merger-driven magnetohydrodynamic turbulence in the intra-cluster medium re-accelerates relativistic electrons via stochastic (second-order Fermi) processes; the model generically predicts that a significant fraction of mergers (especially those involving lower-mass systems) should produce halos with α < −1.5, while flatter-spectrum halos are expected for the most energetic mergers.

Determine whether ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos constitute a genuine, statistically populated class of diffuse cluster radio sources (as opposed to a small number of isolated cases), and assess whether the observed abundance and statistical properties of such USSRHs—when compared to predictions of the turbulent re-acceleration model—provide quantitative observational support for that model of radio halo formation.
status_search_result: Subsequent low-frequency surveys with LOFAR, GMRT/uGMRT and MWA have substantially expanded the number of identified ultra-steep-spectrum radio halos. A 2024 LOFAR study reports that roughly 64% (7/11) of analyzed halos have α < −1.5, consistent with predictions of the turbulent re-acceleration model. This supports USSRHs as a real population and provides observational backing for turbulent re-acceleration, though precise statistics and full population-level confirmation across cluster mass and merger states are still being refined.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: Are the observed long-range-loss dependencies on opposing beam intensity and transverse emittance nearly universal for a well-tuned collider operating away from harmful resonances, and if so, do they also hold in the LHC, which has several long-range beam-beam interactions per turn?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a circular hadron collider in which two counter-rotating bunched beams interact at one or more interaction regions. Around each main interaction point the beams share a common beam pipe over a finite distance, so that in addition to the head-on beam-beam collision each test particle of one beam encounters the opposing bunch at several parasitic ("long-range") crossings per turn, where the two beams are transversely separated by a few r.m.s. beam sizes. Let N denote the bunch population (number of particles per bunch) of the opposing beam and ε its transverse normalized emittance. For a well-tuned machine whose betatron tunes are kept away from low-order resonances harmful to single-particle stability, empirical observations in existing colliders suggest that the rate of beam loss attributable to long-range beam-beam interactions depends on the opposing-beam parameters only through certain specific functional combinations of N and ε (a "long-range loss law").

(a) Determine whether these observed dependencies of the long-range loss rate on (N, ε) are nearly universal across well-tuned colliders operated away from harmful resonances, in the sense of being independent of the specific machine, optics, and number of long-range encounters per turn (up to an overall normalization).

(b) In particular, determine whether the same functional dependencies hold in a collider configuration with several long-range beam-beam encounters per interaction region per turn (such as a high-energy proton-proton collider with strong parasitic crossings), and identify the explicit scaling law L = f(N, ε) governing the long-range-induced loss rate in that regime.
status_search_result: Recent literature on long-range beam-beam effects in the LHC and HL-LHC continues to study scaling of losses and emittance growth with bunch intensity, emittance, and separation, and reports that observed scalings are consistent with simple assumptions but no universal closed-form law has been established. Mitigation via wire compensators is an active area, with first experimental evidence published in 2024. The question of universality of long-range loss laws across machines therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: Why did KEKB achieve a maximum vertical beam-beam parameter of only 0.09 in the higher-energy ring when beam-beam simulations predicted 0.15, and what mechanisms were limiting further luminosity increase under crab-cavity operation?
self_contained_problem: Consider the KEKB asymmetric electron–positron collider operating with crab cavities. In the strong–strong (and weak–strong) beam–beam simulation models for this machine, the maximum attainable vertical beam–beam parameter ξ_y in the higher‑energy ring is predicted to be approximately 0.15, whereas in actual operation only ξ_y ≈ 0.09 was achieved. Identify and quantitatively explain the physical mechanisms responsible for this discrepancy between the simulated and the measured maximum vertical beam–beam parameter, and determine what dynamical effects (e.g. synchro‑betatron resonances, chromatic coupling, machine errors, lattice nonlinearities, electron‑cloud effects, noise, or crab‑cavity imperfections) limit further increase of the luminosity under crab‑cavity collision. Provide a model that reproduces the observed saturation at ξ_y ≈ 0.09 and predicts the operational changes required to recover the simulated value of 0.15.
status_search_result: Subsequent reports on KEKB crab-cavity operation acknowledge that the achieved vertical beam-beam parameter (~0.09) remained well below the simulated value (~0.15), and that the cause was not fully identified. Contributing factors discussed include operation near a synchro-betatron resonance, chromatic coupling (partly mitigated by skew sextupoles), and contradictions between simulated and measured beam lifetime. No definitive resolution has been published; the question remained open at KEKB shutdown, with investigations continuing in the SuperKEKB context.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: What quantitative theoretical model can explain why, in SPS and similar hadron-collider observations, proton losses became more sensitive to high-order resonances when the opposing anti-proton bunch emittance was reduced to nearly match the proton emittance, even though the beam-beam parameter was about 40% lower?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a hadron collider in which a bunch of protons interacts head-on (and possibly through long-range encounters) with a bunch of anti-protons of equal energy. Each beam is characterized by a transverse rms emittance (ε_p for protons, ε_a for anti-protons) and the standard linear beam-beam tune-shift parameter ξ, which for round Gaussian beams is
  ξ = (N r_0) / (4 π ε_n),
where N is the opposing bunch population, r_0 is the classical proton radius, and ε_n is the normalized transverse emittance of the opposing beam. Single-particle proton motion in the presence of the nonlinear beam-beam kick from the anti-proton charge distribution is otherwise governed by the (weak-strong) Hamiltonian
  H(x,p_x,y,p_y;s) = H_lattice(x,p_x,y,p_y;s) + δ_p(s) U(x,y; σ_x(ε_a), σ_y(ε_a)),
where U is the Bassetti–Erskine potential of a Gaussian charge distribution with rms sizes σ_{x,y} determined by ε_a, and δ_p denotes periodic kicks at the interaction point(s).

Empirically, in regimes where the anti-proton emittance ε_a is large compared to the proton emittance ε_p, proton losses are dominated by relatively low-order betatron resonances n_x Q_x + n_y Q_y = p (with |n_x|+|n_y| small). When ε_a is reduced so that ε_a ≈ ε_p, observations show that proton losses become markedly more sensitive to high-order resonances (large |n_x|+|n_y|), even when this reduction in ε_a simultaneously decreases the beam-beam parameter ξ by roughly 40%.

Problem. Develop a quantitative theoretical model — in terms of the resonance driving terms generated by U at given ε_a/ε_p, the resulting nonlinear detuning, the dynamic-aperture or diffusion rate of proton trajectories under repeated kicks, and the proton phase-space density occupying these resonances — that predicts and explains why decreasing ε_a toward ε_p enhances the contribution of high-order resonances to proton losses despite the accompanying ~40% reduction in ξ. The model should yield a calculable loss rate (or diffusion coefficient) as a function of ε_a/ε_p and ξ that reproduces the observed crossover from low-order- to high-order-resonance-dominated loss as ε_a → ε_p.
status_search_result: The originating discussion explicitly notes that no quantitative theoretical model for this emittance-ratio-dependent enhancement of high-order resonance losses has yet been developed. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent published model that quantitatively explains the SPS proton-antiproton observations of increased sensitivity to high-order resonances when emittances become comparable despite a lower beam-beam parameter. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: Why did the RHIC pi coherent beam-beam mode appear without causing an instability even though it lies outside the incoherent spectrum and was theoretically expected to be undamped, and what damping mechanism, if any, would control this mode in the LHC?
self_contained_problem:
Consider two counter-rotating bunched hadron beams in a circular collider undergoing head-on beam-beam collisions. The transverse coherent dipole oscillation spectrum of the two-beam system contains two discrete modes: the σ-mode (0-mode), in which the two bunches oscillate in phase, and the π-mode, in which they oscillate out of phase. The σ-mode lies inside the incoherent betatron tune spread of single-particle frequencies and is therefore Landau-damped, whereas the π-mode is shifted outside the incoherent continuum (for nearly equal beams and beam-beam parameter ratios above roughly 0.6) and is, in classical rigid-bunch theory, undamped. An undamped coherent mode is generally expected to drive a transverse instability in the presence of machine impedance.

Experimentally, in the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) the π coherent beam-beam mode has been clearly observed lying outside the incoherent spectrum, yet no associated transverse instability developed.

Provide a quantitative explanation of the following two questions:

(a) Identify the physical damping or stabilizing mechanism(s) that prevent the experimentally observed RHIC π-mode from driving a coherent transverse instability, despite its position outside the incoherent betatron tune spread and the presence of machine impedance. Derive, under stated approximations, the corresponding damping rate or stability criterion as a function of the beam-beam parameter ξ, the synchrotron tune Q_s, the chromaticity, the bunch length, and the relevant impedance.

(b) Determine, under the parameters of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) (proton-proton head-on collisions at top energy, with its characteristic ξ, Q_s, bunch length, chromaticity, and transverse impedance budget), whether the same mechanism(s) suffice to damp the π-mode, and if not, specify what additional damping mechanism would be required and quantify its necessary strength.
status_search_result: Subsequent literature identifies synchro-betatron coupling, which produces incoherent synchrotron sidebands that overlap with the π-mode and provide Landau damping, as the leading candidate explanation for the absence of π-mode instability at RHIC. Studies of LHC coherent beam-beam modes (e.g., simulations and the 2014 analysis of the LHC π-mode) discuss the same mechanism and propose additional measures (e.g., transverse feedback, electron lenses for Landau damping). However, a definitive quantitative match between observations and theory and a fully validated LHC damping prescription remain partial; the issue is treated as understood in principle but not closed in detail.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: For possible future LHC crab-cavity operation, how sensitive are the beams to cavity phase noise and to synchro-betatron resonances driven by dispersion in the crab cavities, and are there additional beam-dynamics limitations that detailed studies should uncover before implementation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a high-energy hadron collider in which crab cavities are installed near an interaction point to rotate the bunches transversely so that head-on collisions occur despite a nonzero crossing angle. Model each beam as an ensemble of particles whose six-dimensional phase-space coordinates evolve under a one-turn symplectic map that includes (i) linear transverse and longitudinal optics with horizontal dispersion D(s) at the crab-cavity locations, (ii) a transverse RF kick of the form Δp_x = (eV/E) sin(ω_RF t + φ + ξ(n)) delivered by each crab cavity, where ξ(n) is a stochastic phase-noise process with power spectral density S_φ(ω), and (iii) the beam–beam kick at the interaction point produced by the opposing bunch.

Address the following:

1. Phase-noise sensitivity. Derive the rate of transverse emittance growth dε/dt of a Gaussian bunch as a functional of the crab-cavity phase-noise spectrum S_φ(ω), the cavity voltage V, frequency ω_RF, the beta function β* and dispersion D* at the cavity, and the synchrotron and betatron tunes. Determine the maximum tolerable integrated phase-noise level such that the emittance growth time exceeds a prescribed luminosity-lifetime threshold.

2. Synchro-betatron resonances from dispersion. For nonzero dispersion D ≠ 0 at a crab cavity, identify all resonance conditions of the form m Q_x + n Q_s = p (with integers m, n, p) that are excited by the combined dispersive–crab coupling, compute the leading-order resonance driving terms as functions of D, V, and the optical functions, and determine the resulting stable phase-space region (dynamic aperture) as a function of the distance to the nearest such resonance.

3. Additional limitations. Identify and quantitatively characterize any further single-beam or beam–beam dynamical limitations introduced by crab-cavity operation (e.g., coupling impedance, transverse wakefields, noise-induced diffusion enhanced by beam–beam, failure scenarios), giving thresholds beyond which stable collider operation is not possible.
status_search_result: Subsequent studies for the HL-LHC crab-cavity program have produced quantitative tolerances on cavity phase noise (emittance-growth formulas validated against experiment at SPS) and analyses of synchro-betatron resonances driven by dispersion, but not all dynamical limitations have been fully characterized; commissioning-era studies continue. The problem is therefore partially solved.

paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
original_question: Do longitudinally flat bunch profiles in large-Piwinski-angle luminosity schemes for the LHC genuinely produce lower transverse diffusion than Gaussian bunches when evaluated in more detailed beam-beam studies, and if they do, can such flat-profile schemes remain attractive even without very large Piwinski angles and very high bunch intensities?
self_contained_problem:
Consider two counter-rotating proton bunches in a high-energy storage ring (such as the Large Hadron Collider) that cross at an interaction point with a nonzero crossing angle. Let the Piwinski angle be defined by \Phi = \sigma_z \theta_c / (2 \sigma_x), where \sigma_z is the rms longitudinal bunch length, \sigma_x is the transverse rms beam size at the interaction point, and \theta_c is the full crossing angle. A luminosity scheme is said to operate in the large-Piwinski-angle regime when \Phi \gg 1, in which the geometric overlap of the colliding bunches is concentrated along the longitudinal direction.

Model each bunch as a charged-particle distribution with a fixed transverse Gaussian profile and a longitudinal density either (i) Gaussian \rho_G(s) \propto \exp(-s^2/(2\sigma_z^2)), or (ii) longitudinally flat: \rho_F(s) constant on an interval [-L/2, L/2] (suitably smoothed) and matched to give the same total bunch population and same rms length. Test particles in one bunch experience the nonlinear electromagnetic kick of the opposing bunch at the crossing, and over many turns develop a slow growth of transverse action characterized by a transverse diffusion coefficient D_\perp (computed from a long-term tracking simulation of the beam-beam interaction including all relevant nonlinear effects, lattice nonlinearities, and tune modulation).

(a) In a detailed beam-beam tracking study going beyond preliminary models, does the longitudinally flat profile (ii) yield a strictly smaller transverse diffusion coefficient D_\perp than the Gaussian profile (i) at matched total intensity, rms bunch length, and crossing angle, across the operationally relevant range of tunes and chromaticities?

(b) If (a) holds, does the advantage of profile (ii) over profile (i) persist in regimes of moderate Piwinski angle (\Phi of order unity) and moderate bunch intensity, rather than only in the large-\Phi, high-intensity limit, in the sense that D_\perp(flat) < D_\perp(Gaussian) and the resulting integrated luminosity per unit emittance growth is improved?
status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found. Subsequent studies of large-Piwinski-angle and flat-bunch luminosity schemes (notably for HL-LHC and crab-kissing/crab-waist proposals) have continued to investigate diffusion and dynamic aperture differences between flat and Gaussian longitudinal profiles, but the literature does not provide a clean, universally accepted confirmation that flat profiles produce lower transverse diffusion than Gaussian ones across all regimes, nor that the scheme is attractive at moderate Piwinski angles and intensities. The status is best characterized as unknown / unresolved in published comparative beam-beam studies.

paper_title: Bimagic Squares of Bimagic Squares and an Open Problem
context_brief: Bimagic-sum invariance in nested square constructions
original_question: For the three tabulated families of bimagic squares — order 256×256 with listed subgroups 64×64, 16×16, and 4×4; order 625×625 with listed subgroups 125×125, 25×25, and 5×5; and order 2401×2401 with listed subgroups 343×343, 49×49, and 7×7 — prove mathematically the observed property stated by the source: for k = 4, 5, and 7, in the first sub-group the bimagic sum S2 is the same, summarized by the pattern k^4 → k^3 → k^2 → k^1.
self_contained_problem:
A magic square of order n is an n×n array containing n² distinct numbers such that the sum of the entries in every row, every column, and both main diagonals equals the same constant S₁ (the magic sum). The square is called bimagic if, in addition, the sum of the squares of the entries in every row, every column, and both main diagonals equals a common constant S₂ (the bimagic sum).

Consider the following three constructions, each presenting a "bimagic square of bimagic squares":

(i) An order 256×256 bimagic square (so n = 256 = 4⁴) whose entries are 1, 2, …, 256², partitioned into a hierarchy of nested sub-blocks of orders 64×64 (= 4³), 16×16 (= 4²), and 4×4 (= 4¹), each itself being a bimagic square (with respect to suitably scaled or translated entry sets).

(ii) An order 625×625 bimagic square (n = 625 = 5⁴) on entries 1, 2, …, 625², with nested sub-blocks of orders 125×125, 25×25, and 5×5, each bimagic.

(iii) An order 2401×2401 bimagic square (n = 2401 = 7⁴) on entries 1, 2, …, 2401², with nested sub-blocks of orders 343×343, 49×49, and 7×7, each bimagic.

For each of these three families (k = 4, 5, 7), it is observed that in the "first sub-group" of the nested decomposition, the bimagic sum S₂ takes the same value across the chain of nested blocks of orders k⁴ → k³ → k² → k¹.

Prove this invariance: namely, give a mathematical proof that, in each of the three constructions above, the bimagic sum S₂ of the first sub-group is constant along the chain of nested blocks of orders k⁴, k³, k², and k¹, for k = 4, 5, and 7.
status_search_result: Web searches turn up the original construction and related work on block-wise bimagic squares of orders 25, 125, 625, etc., but no subsequent paper providing a general mathematical proof of the observed S₂-invariance pattern k⁴ → k³ → k² → k¹ for k = 4, 5, 7. No clear resolution was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.

original_question: What is the actual low-temperature magnetic-domain structure of pure LiHoF4, an insulating dipolar Ising ferromagnet whose Ho3+ moments order below about 1.53 K along the crystalline c axis, and can experiments verify the predicted rich structure in which the ground-state domains consist of parallel antiferromagnetically aligned sheets whose sizes and possible branching depend on demagnetization effects and sample geometry?
status_search_result: Direct imaging experiments on LiHoF4 (e.g., scanning Hall probe microscopy at ultra-low temperatures and the 2009 study by Biltmo–Henelius and collaborators) have observed regular domain patterns of cylinder/sheet-like domains a few micrometers wide whose size depends on sample geometry, broadly consistent with theoretical predictions for a dipolar Ising ferromagnet. However, full quantitative verification of the predicted antiferromagnetically aligned sheet ground state and of branching in thick samples remains incomplete, so the problem appears partially solved.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
context_brief: Hyperfine effects in the global phase diagram
original_question: What quantitatively accurate role do Ho hyperfine interactions play in the global concentration-temperature-transverse-field phase diagram of LiHoxY1−xF4, especially in regimes where the ferromagnetic or spin-glass critical temperature drops below roughly 0.5 K and the hyperfine interaction inhibits quantum fluctuations and strongly renormalizes the critical transverse field?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the diluted dipolar Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$, modeled as a system of Ho$^{3+}$ ions placed at random with concentration $x \in (0,1]$ on the Ho sublattice of the LiYF$_4$ crystal, with a non‑Kramers ground doublet (effective Ising spin $S^z = \pm 1$) split by crystal field excited states, coupled by long‑range magnetic dipole–dipole interactions, subject to a uniform transverse magnetic field $B_x$, at temperature $T$, and including the on‑site hyperfine coupling $A\, \mathbf{I}\cdot\mathbf{J}$ between the Ho electronic moment $\mathbf{J}$ and the $I = 7/2$ $^{165}$Ho nuclear spin (with all eight nuclear levels retained).

Within this microscopic model, carry out a quantitatively accurate determination (for example, by quantum Monte Carlo simulation that treats the hyperfine interaction non‑perturbatively rather than as a renormalization of the bare transverse field) of the global phase diagram in the three‑dimensional parameter space $(x, T, B_x)$, including
(a) the ferromagnetic phase boundary at large $x$,
(b) the spin‑glass phase boundary at small $x$,
(c) any intermediate or paramagnetic regions and their crossovers,
in particular in the regime where the ferromagnetic or spin‑glass critical temperature drops below approximately $0.5$ K, where the hyperfine interaction strongly inhibits quantum fluctuations and substantially renormalizes the critical transverse field $B_x^c(x,T)$.

Establish, with controlled numerical accuracy, the quantitative role of the hyperfine coupling on the location and shape of the boundaries of the ferromagnetic and spin‑glass phases throughout the $(x, T, B_x)$ diagram.
status_search_result: Subsequent work (e.g. quantum Monte Carlo studies treating the hyperfine coupling approximately via a renormalized transverse field, and studies of induced random fields and quantum annealing in the dipolar Ising magnet) has made progress on portions of the (x, T, B_x) phase diagram, but a quantitatively accurate determination of the full global phase diagram with hyperfine interactions treated non-perturbatively (especially below ~0.5 K where hyperfine effects dominate) does not appear to have been completed in the literature, leaving the problem effectively open.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Do transverse-field-induced random fields in diluted ferromagnetic LiHoxY1−xF4, for example at Ho concentration x = 0.44, produce Griffiths singularity effects in the paramagnetic regime just above the ferromagnetic transition temperature Tc, and what systematic experimental investigation is needed to test the claimed susceptibility-scaling behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the diluted dipolar-coupled Ising magnet LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4 in an applied transverse magnetic field, modeled as a random transverse-field Ising system with long-range dipolar interactions in which the transverse field, via the off-diagonal components of the dipolar coupling between non-Kramers Ho^{3+} ions, induces an effective random longitudinal (symmetry-breaking) field on each spin. For the diluted ferromagnetic regime (in particular at Ho concentration x = 0.44), let χ(T, H_t) denote the linear magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature T and transverse field H_t, and let T_c(H_t) denote the ferromagnetic ordering temperature.

Determine whether the transverse-field-induced random longitudinal fields produce Griffiths-singularity effects in the paramagnetic regime at temperatures just above T_c(H_t); that is, decide whether there exists a temperature window T_c(H_t) < T < T*(H_t) in which thermodynamic quantities (in particular χ(T, H_t)) exhibit Griffiths-type non-analytic behavior arising from rare large ferromagnetically ordered clusters in the presence of these induced random fields, and identify the scaling form of χ(T, H_t) consistent with such a Griffiths phase. Equivalently, devise and justify a systematic experimental and theoretical protocol able to confirm or rule out the proposed Griffiths-singularity interpretation of the observed transverse-field and temperature dependence of χ in the diluted ferromagnetic regime of this compound.

status_search_result: The question of whether transverse-field-induced random fields generate Griffiths singularities in the paramagnetic regime of diluted ferromagnetic LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4 (x ≈ 0.44) remains an actively discussed open problem. The status appears to be open / partially explored.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Why do technically demanding AC-susceptibility and specific-heat experiments on high-dilution LiHoxY1−xF4 disagree about whether the system shows conventional spin-glass freezing or unusual antiglass behavior, particularly between the earlier measurements of Reich, Ghosh, and collaborators and the later measurements of Quilliam and collaborators?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the dilute dipolar Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ in the high-dilution regime (Ho concentration $x \approx 4.5\%$), where Ho$^{3+}$ ions occupy a fraction $x$ of the Y sites and interact predominantly via long-range magnetic dipole-dipole couplings with strong uniaxial (Ising) anisotropy along the crystallographic $c$-axis. At millikelvin temperatures, two qualitatively different scenarios have been proposed for the low-temperature collective behavior of the diluted Ho$^{3+}$ moments:

(a) a conventional spin-glass freezing, in which the distribution of magnetic relaxation times broadens monotonically as the temperature is lowered, accompanied by a featureless specific heat without anomalies attributable to entangled clusters; and

(b) an "antiglass" state, in which the imaginary part of the AC susceptibility $\chi''(\omega,T)$ exhibits a frequency distribution that narrows (rather than broadens) on cooling, and the specific heat displays anomalous features interpreted as signatures of coherent, entangled magnetic clusters.

Two sets of technically demanding low-temperature experiments (AC susceptibility and specific heat) on nominally similar high-dilution samples have produced mutually inconsistent results, one set supporting scenario (b) and a later set supporting scenario (a).

Problem. Identify the physical or experimental origin of this disagreement and determine which of the two scenarios (conventional spin-glass freezing or antiglass behavior) correctly describes the equilibrium low-temperature state of LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ in the high-dilution limit $x \approx 4.5\%$. In particular, account for: (i) whether the frequency distribution of $\chi''(\omega,T)$ broadens or narrows as $T \to 0$; (ii) whether the low-temperature specific heat exhibits anomalies consistent with entangled-cluster (antiglass) physics; and (iii) the role, if any, of sample preparation, hyperfine couplings, off-diagonal dipolar terms, or out-of-equilibrium dynamics in producing the observed discrepancy.
category_tag: dilute dipolar Ising magnets / spin glasses
status_search_result: The discrepancy between the early AC-susceptibility/specific-heat measurements of Reich, Ghosh, and collaborators (supporting an "antiglass" state) and the later measurements of Quilliam et al. on highly dilute LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ remains unresolved. Subsequent work (e.g., μSR studies and re-examinations of nonlinear susceptibility by Jönsson et al. and Ancona-Torres et al.) has prolonged rather than settled the debate, and no consensus explanation for the disagreement has been published. The status is therefore open.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Do sample shape and demagnetization effects influence whether a spin-glass phase exists in highly diluted LiHoxY1−xF4, even though such effects are expected not to determine the existence of the spin-glass phase?
self_contained_problem: Consider the diluted dipolar Ising magnet LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4 in the highly diluted regime (small magnetic-ion concentration x, e.g. x ≲ 0.25), modeled as Ising moments placed on a fraction x of the rare-earth sites of the LiYF_4 lattice and interacting via the long-ranged magnetic dipole–dipole interaction (together with weak nearest-neighbour exchange and hyperfine couplings). For a finite single-crystal sample of given geometric shape, the long-range dipolar interaction produces shape-dependent demagnetization fields that modify the internal magnetic field experienced by the spins. The standard expectation is that, while these demagnetization corrections shift transition temperatures and rescale susceptibilities, they should not determine whether a thermodynamic spin-glass phase exists in the diluted system. Rigorously establish (or disprove) the following: do the macroscopic sample shape and the associated demagnetization effects influence whether a true spin-glass phase (a thermodynamic phase with broken replica symmetry or, equivalently, a divergent nonlinear susceptibility at a finite freezing temperature) exists in highly diluted LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4? Specifically, determine whether the existence of a spin-glass phase in this dilute dipolar Ising system is independent of sample shape and demagnetization, or whether there exist sample geometries for which the spin-glass phase is suppressed or qualitatively altered.
status_search_result: The question of whether a genuine spin-glass phase exists in highly diluted LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4 remains controversial, with conflicting experimental and theoretical reports of glassy dynamics, finite-T spin-glass transitions, and antiglass behavior. Sample-shape and demagnetization effects have not been systematically isolated as a determinant of the spin-glass phase, and recent work shows that thermal boundary conditions and macroscopic sample features do affect observed glassy behavior. The specific question therefore appears unresolved.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: For diluted dipolar Ising models intended to describe LiHoxY1−xF4, can larger classical Monte Carlo simulations bring finite-size corrections under control, reconcile the different spin-glass correlation-length crossings along the a and c axes, and thereby determine the finite-temperature spin-glass transition more reliably?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a site-diluted dipolar Ising model on the lattice of magnetic sites of LiHoF4 (a body-centered tetragonal lattice with the easy axis along the crystallographic c-direction). At each site i a classical Ising spin S_i = ±1 is placed with probability x and the site is left empty with probability 1−x; the occupied spins interact through the (truncated or Ewald-summed) dipole–dipole interaction
H = (1/2) Σ_{i≠j} ε_i ε_j D_{ij} S_i S_j ,
where ε_i ∈ {0,1} are the quenched occupation variables and D_{ij} is the standard Ising-projected dipolar coupling between sites i and j (taking into account the uniaxial anisotropy along the c-axis).

For a finite system of linear size L with periodic boundary conditions, define the spin-glass two-point correlation function in the usual way from two real replicas, and from it the second-moment spin-glass correlation lengths ξ_sg^{(a)}(T,L) and ξ_sg^{(c)}(T,L) measured along the a- and c-axes respectively. Standard finite-size scaling predicts that, at a continuous spin-glass transition of temperature T_c, the dimensionless ratios ξ_sg^{(a)}/L and ξ_sg^{(c)}/L curves for different L should cross at the same temperature T_c.

Question. For dilutions x relevant to LiHo_x Y_{1−x} F_4 (in particular in the strongly diluted regime), do classical Monte Carlo simulations on system sizes large enough to control the leading corrections to finite-size scaling produce ξ_sg^{(a)}/L and ξ_sg^{(c)}/L crossings that converge to a single common temperature T_c > 0, thereby reliably establishing a finite-temperature spin-glass transition and its critical temperature?
status_search_result: Subsequent large-scale Monte Carlo studies using improved cluster algorithms (Alonso–Fernández, and later work culminating in PRB 100, 064425 (2019)) provide evidence for a finite-temperature spin-glass transition in the diluted dipolar Ising model in three dimensions and report critical exponents ν≈1.27(8), η≈0.228(35). However, published reports still note that ξ_L/L crossings are strongly affected by corrections to scaling, and a fully controlled reconciliation of the a-axis and c-axis correlation-length crossings for the LiHo_xY_{1−x}F_4 microscopic model has not been definitively demonstrated. The existence question is largely settled in favor of T_c > 0, but the precise reliable determination of T_c via reconciled axis-resolved crossings is only partially resolved.

paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
original_question: Can comparative studies of other highly diluted Ising magnetic materials, including diluted spin-ice compounds (DyxY1−x)2Ti2O7 and (HoxY1−x)2Ti2O7 and proposed transverse-field Ising materials HoxY1−x(OH)3 and DyxY1−x(OH)3, clarify the physics responsible for the high-dilution behavior of LiHoxY1−xF4?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of strongly diluted, rare-earth Ising magnetic materials in which a magnetic ion is partially substituted by a non-magnetic one, producing a quenched dilution of dipolar-coupled effective Ising spins.

Concrete representatives include:
(i) LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4, a dipolar-coupled Ising magnet in which the Ho^{3+} ground-state doublet behaves as an effective Ising spin and the hyperfine coupling to the I=7/2 nuclear moment plus the application of a transverse magnetic field generate an effective transverse-field Ising model on the diluted lattice;
(ii) the diluted pyrochlore spin-ice compounds (Dy_x Y_{1-x})_2 Ti_2 O_7 and (Ho_x Y_{1-x})_2 Ti_2 O_7, in which Ising moments sit on a pyrochlore lattice with dominant nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic plus long-range dipolar interactions producing a "2-in / 2-out" ice-rule manifold;
(iii) the proposed transverse-field Ising materials Ho_x Y_{1-x}(OH)_3 and Dy_x Y_{1-x}(OH)_3, in which the rare-earth Ising moments form a stacked-triangular lattice with dipolar interactions and a single-ion crystal-field doublet susceptible to a transverse field.

In the strongly diluted regime (x small, well below any ferromagnetic or spin-ice ordering threshold), LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4 displays anomalous low-temperature behaviour whose nature (e.g., absence of a conventional spin-glass freezing, antiglass features, persistent dynamics, role of hyperfine and off-diagonal dipolar terms generating effective random transverse fields) is not understood from first principles.

Problem. Determine, by means of a comparative theoretical and/or experimental study of the highly diluted limit of these materials, the microscopic mechanism responsible for the anomalous low-temperature collective behaviour of LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4. Specifically:

(a) Identify which features of the low-temperature phase diagram of LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4 at small x are universal to dipolar-coupled diluted Ising systems and which are specific to the LiHoF_4 host (e.g., to the strong ^{165}Ho hyperfine coupling, to the off-diagonal terms of the dipolar tensor producing random effective transverse fields under an applied field, or to the Ising lattice geometry).

(b) Predict, for (Dy_x Y_{1-x})_2 Ti_2 O_7, (Ho_x Y_{1-x})_2 Ti_2 O_7, Ho_x Y_{1-x}(OH)_3, and Dy_x Y_{1-x}(OH)_3 at strong dilution, whether a conventional spin-glass transition, an "antiglass" regime, or a quantum-disordered phase is realized as a function of x, temperature, and (where applicable) transverse field, and compare with the corresponding regime of LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4.

(c) From this comparison, formulate the minimal effective Hamiltonian that captures the high-dilution physics of LiHo_x Y_{1-x} F_4.
status_search_result: The nature of the low-temperature phase of strongly diluted LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4 remains controversial, with conflicting experimental claims (spin-glass transition near 43 mK vs. absence of a conventional spin-glass transition) and ongoing theoretical work on the role of hyperfine coupling and random transverse fields. No comparative study definitively settling the high-dilution physics via the proposed pyrochlore and hydroxide analogues has been published; the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
original_question: Can a practical exchange-correlation kernel fxc for linear-response TDDFT be constructed that is nonlocal and frequency dependent, improves systematically on ALDA, and avoids the unphysical poles caused by the linearized Sham-Schlueter or Klein-functional route, where double inversion of the non-interacting Kohn-Sham response function chi0 turns zeros of chi0 into double poles in fxc? One proposed direction is to start from the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than the Klein functional, but it remains open whether that avoids the known pathology without creating new ones.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a many-electron system in linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT). Let χ₀(r,r';ω) denote the non-interacting Kohn–Sham density-density response function and χ(r,r';ω) the interacting density-density response function. They are related by the Dyson-like equation
   χ = χ₀ + χ₀ (v_C + f_xc) χ,
where v_C(r,r') = 1/|r−r'| is the bare Coulomb interaction and f_xc[n](r,r';ω) is the exchange–correlation kernel, defined formally as the second functional derivative of the exchange–correlation action with respect to the time-dependent density.

Pathology. Solving for f_xc from the above relation requires inverting χ₀ twice:
   f_xc = χ₀⁻¹ − χ⁻¹ − v_C.
Consequently, every frequency ω at which χ₀(ω) has a zero eigenvalue produces a double pole of f_xc(ω); when this f_xc is reinserted into the Dyson equation, the resulting interacting χ(ω) acquires unphysical poles in the upper half of the complex frequency plane (violating causality). This pathology is intrinsic to approximations derived via the linearized Sham–Schlüter equation or, equivalently, via variational schemes built from the Klein functional Φ_K[G].

Adiabatic local density approximation (ALDA). The ALDA kernel
   f_xc^ALDA(r,r';ω) = δ(r−r') · d²(n ε_xc^hom(n))/dn² |_{n=n(r)}
is local in space and frequency-independent; it lacks the structure needed to capture particle–hole interactions beyond the random phase approximation (RPA).

Problem. Construct a practical exchange–correlation kernel f_xc(r,r';ω) for linear-response TDDFT that simultaneously satisfies all of the following:
 (i) is spatially nonlocal and frequency-dependent;
 (ii) provides a systematically improvable hierarchy of approximations going beyond ALDA and RPA, capturing particle–hole interactions;
 (iii) is free of the double-pole pathology, i.e. zeros of χ₀(ω) do not generate spurious poles of f_xc(ω), and the resulting full response χ(ω) has no poles in the upper half complex frequency plane;
 (iv) does not introduce new analytic or causality-violating pathologies of its own.

Specifically, decide whether such a kernel can be obtained by deriving f_xc from a variational principle based on the Luttinger–Ward functional Φ_LW[G] (a closed, skeleton-diagrammatic functional of the dressed Green's function G whose functional derivative gives the self-energy Σ = δΦ_LW/δG), in place of the Klein functional. Either exhibit such a construction together with a proof that conditions (i)–(iv) are met, or prove that any kernel obtained from the Luttinger–Ward route necessarily violates at least one of (i)–(iv).
status_search_result: Searches show ongoing development of nonlocal, frequency-dependent exchange-correlation kernels (e.g. Bethe–Salpeter-derived, TDCDFT-based, nonadiabatic kernels for strongly correlated systems, and machine-learned functionals), but no construction is reported that derives f_xc from the Luttinger–Ward functional and rigorously establishes both systematic improvability beyond ALDA/RPA and absence of the double-pole / upper-half-plane pole pathology. The question therefore appears still open.

paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
original_question: What are the physical regimes and corrective principles for Kadanoff-Baym dynamics combined with many-body perturbation theory when conserving approximations still show fundamental failures, such as breakdown at strong interaction, artificial correlation-induced damping, questionable steady states in extended systems, and violations of positivity in two-particle correlation functions? The setting is the nonequilibrium Green's-function approach, where the Kadanoff-Baym equations use a self-energy from approximations such as second Born, GW, or T-matrix, which conserve macroscopic quantities but do not guarantee all physically required properties.
status_search_result: The question concerns long-standing open issues in NEGF/Kadanoff–Baym dynamics with conserving many-body approximations. Subsequent literature (Stefanucci–van Leeuwen and collaborators, work on the Generalized Kadanoff–Baym Ansatz, time-linear schemes, and positivity-preserving approximations) has clarified some aspects—e.g. artificial damping is now broadly attributed to self-consistency in Φ-derivable schemes, and partial fixes (HF-GKBA, T-matrix improvements) exist—but a complete principled resolution covering strong coupling, steady-state physicality, and positivity remains unresolved. Status is best described as open / partially understood.
