paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: When the threshold condition ensuring existence of an absolute constrained minimizer fails for the action functional on a star graph, does the action still possess a local constrained minimum that is strictly larger than its infimum? Likewise, when the analogous threshold fails for the energy constrained at fixed mass, does the constrained energy still have a local constrained minimum above its infimum?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a star graph consisting of $N\ge 3$ half-lines joined at a common vertex $v$. For $\Psi=(\psi_j)_{j=1}^N\in L^2(\mathcal{G})=\bigoplus_{j=1}^N L^2(\mathbb{R}^+)$, denote the mass by $M(\Psi)=\sum_j\int_0^\infty|\psi_j(x)|^2\,dx$. Fix a coupling constant $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and a focusing power $p>2$. Consider on $\mathcal{G}$ the nonlinear Schrödinger problem with an attractive $\delta$-interaction of strength $\alpha$ at $v$: functions are continuous at $v$, $\psi_1(0)=\cdots=\psi_N(0)$, and the Kirchhoff-type condition $\sum_j\psi_j'(0)=\alpha\psi_1(0)$ holds. Define the energy
$$E(\Psi)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^N\int_0^\infty|\psi_j'|^2\,dx+\frac{\alpha}{2}|\Psi(v)|^2-\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j=1}^N\int_0^\infty|\psi_j|^p\,dx,$$
on the form domain $H^1(\mathcal{G})$, and, for $\omega>0$, the action
$$S_\omega(\Psi)=E(\Psi)+\frac{\omega}{2}M(\Psi).$$
There is a known threshold $\alpha^\ast<0$ (depending on $N$ and $p$) such that:

(i) for every $\omega>0$ with $-N\sqrt{\omega}<\alpha<\alpha^\ast$, the action $S_\omega$ admits an absolute minimizer on the natural Nehari-type constraint;

(ii) for every $\alpha<0$, the energy $E$ admits an absolute minimizer at fixed mass $M(\Psi)=m$ for all $m$ below an explicit critical value $m^\ast(\alpha)$.

Prove or disprove the following:

(a) When the condition $-N\sqrt{\omega}<\alpha<\alpha^\ast$ in (i) fails, the action $S_\omega$ still possesses, on the constrained set, a local minimizer whose action value is strictly greater than the infimum.

(b) When the analogous mass condition $m<m^\ast(\alpha)$ in (ii) fails, the energy $E$ at fixed mass $m$ still possesses a local minimizer on $\{M(\Psi)=m\}$ whose energy value is strictly greater than the infimum.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on quantum graphs
status_search_result: The energy part (b) of the conjecture has been addressed by Adami, Cacciapuoti, Finco, and Noja in "Stable standing waves for a NLS on star graphs as local minimizers of the constrained energy" (arXiv:1509.01810, 2016), where they prove that on a star graph with attractive delta interaction the symmetric standing wave is a local minimizer of the constrained energy at fixed mass for all admissible masses, even when the absolute-minimum threshold fails, yielding orbital stability. The corresponding statement for the action functional (part (a)) does not appear to be explicitly resolved in the same generality, so the full conjecture is at least partially solved.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: For nonlinear Schrödinger equations on graphs whose linear part has eigenvalues, bifurcation theory can produce nonlinear standing-wave branches that emerge from linear bound states. How can one also obtain and analyze branches of nonlinear standing waves that have no linear counterpart, such as nonlinear excited or bound states that do not bifurcate from the zero solution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (a finite or infinite collection of edges, each identified with an interval, glued at vertices). Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,\partial_t \psi(t,x) = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi(t,x) + V(x)\,\psi(t,x) - |\psi(t,x)|^{p-1}\psi(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ equipped with self-adjoint (e.g. Kirchhoff) vertex conditions, $V:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a (possibly zero) external potential, and $p>1$. Standing waves are solutions of the form $\psi(t,x)=e^{-i\omega t}\varphi_\omega(x)$ with frequency $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$, where $\varphi_\omega$ solves the stationary equation
$$ -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \varphi_\omega + V\varphi_\omega - |\varphi_\omega|^{p-1}\varphi_\omega = \omega\,\varphi_\omega.$$

Assume the linear operator $H=-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}+V$ has discrete eigenvalues. Standard local bifurcation theory then produces, for every eigenvalue $\omega_0$ of $H$ with eigenfunction $\phi_0$, a smooth branch $\omega\mapsto\varphi_\omega$ of small nonlinear standing waves emanating from the trivial solution with $\varphi_{\omega_0}=0$ and tangent to $\phi_0$. Such branches are said to have a linear counterpart.

It is known, however, that on certain metric graphs (e.g. star graphs) there exist nonlinear bound and excited states $\varphi_\omega$ that do not belong to any branch bifurcating from the zero solution at a linear eigenvalue — i.e. nonlinear standing waves without linear counterpart.

Problem. Develop a general method to construct and analyze (existence, multiplicity, parameter dependence on $\omega$, qualitative shape, and orbital/spectral stability) branches of nonlinear standing waves $\varphi_\omega$ on a metric graph $\mathcal{G}$ that do not bifurcate from the zero solution at any eigenvalue of $H=-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}+V$. In particular, determine whether such "branches without linear counterpart" can always be obtained as bifurcations from (non-small) solitary waves of the potential-free problem when the external potential $V$ is switched on, and characterize the metric graphs and nonlinearity exponents $p$ for which such branches exist.
category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: existence and multiplicity results for non-bifurcating ("peaked") positive bound states on metric graphs have been obtained via Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction (e.g., solutions concentrating at vertices of odd degree ≥ 3 that are not minimizers). For specific graphs like the tadpole, families of continuous branches of solitons without linear analog have been constructed alongside bifurcating branches. However, a general theory covering arbitrary graphs, exponents, and the full conjecture that such branches arise as bifurcations from non-small solitary waves when an external potential is turned on does not appear to be established, so the problem as a whole is partially solved.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: Are standing waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs asymptotically stable? More precisely, if a solution starts close in the energy norm to a standing wave e^{iωt}Φ_ω, does the solution converge at large time to another nearby standing wave plus a dispersive linear term and a decaying remainder? In order to prove such a result, can one develop the necessary analysis of the Hamiltonian linearization JL on graphs, including spectral information and dispersive estimates for exp(tJL), and can this be done for important cases such as subcritical power nonlinearities, where the methods described in the paper presently fail?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph (for instance a star graph with a finite number of half-line edges joined at a single vertex), equipped with a self-adjoint realization $H$ of the Laplacian on $\mathcal{G}$ determined by suitable vertex coupling conditions. Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\partial_t u(t,x) = H u(t,x) - f(|u(t,x)|^2) u(t,x), \qquad x\in\mathcal{G},\ t\in\mathbb{R}, $$
where $f$ is a nonlinearity (for example a pure power $f(s)=s^{p/2}$ in the subcritical regime, or a nonlinearity concentrated at the vertex). For $\omega>0$ let $\Phi_\omega\in H^1(\mathcal{G})$ be a bound state, i.e.\ a real-valued solution of
$$ H\Phi_\omega - f(\Phi_\omega^2)\Phi_\omega = -\omega \Phi_\omega, $$
generating the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega(x)$. Linearizing the equation around such a standing wave yields a Hamiltonian operator $JL$ acting on $\mathbb{C}$-valued functions on $\mathcal{G}$ that is neither self-adjoint nor skew-adjoint.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic stability statement: there exist $\delta>0$, a phase $\omega_\infty$ near $\omega$, an asymptotic profile $\Phi_{\omega_\infty}$, an asymptotic state $\Psi_\infty$, and a remainder $R_\infty$ with $\|R_\infty(t)\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})}	o 0$ as $t	o\infty$, such that whenever the initial datum $u(0)$ satisfies $\inf_{	heta\in\mathbb{R}}\|u(0)-e^{i	heta}\Phi_\omega\|_{H^1(\mathcal{G})}<\delta$, the corresponding global solution decomposes as
$$ u(t) = e^{i\omega_\infty t}\Phi_{\omega_\infty} + U_t^\ast \Psi_\infty + R_\infty(t), $$
where $U_t = e^{-itH}$ is the free Schrödinger evolution on $\mathcal{G}$.

As steps toward this result, develop the spectral theory of the Hamiltonian linearization $JL$ on $\mathcal{G}$ (location of the spectrum, generalized kernel, embedded eigenvalues, resonances), and establish dispersive and Strichartz estimates for $e^{tJL}$ on $\mathcal{G}$ sufficient to control the nonlinear remainder. In particular, address the case of subcritical power nonlinearities, where standard methods based on weighted dispersive estimates do not apply.
status_search_result: Asymptotic stability of standing waves has been established in restricted settings on metric graphs, notably for the NLS on a star graph with a delta-type concentrated nonlinearity at the vertex (Adami–Noja–Sacchetti and subsequent works), where dispersive estimates are available in weighted spaces. For subcritical power nonlinearities on graphs, however, the spectral analysis of the Hamiltonian linearization $JL$ and the corresponding dispersive/Strichartz estimates needed to close the asymptotic stability argument have not been fully developed, and the general question remains open.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: How do solitons scatter on graphs with nontrivial topology beyond the simple star-graph setting? In particular, for graphs such as trees or other networks with internal structure, can one rigorously describe propagation and scattering of solitons and determine how the topology and available dispersive estimates affect the dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a connected metric graph with nontrivial topology beyond a star graph — for instance, a finite or infinite tree with bounded vertex degrees, or a network containing internal edges and/or loops. Each edge e of G is identified with an interval (of finite or infinite length), and a function u on G is a collection {u_e}_{e∈E(G)} of functions on the edges. On each edge consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
   i ∂_t u_e = −∂_{xx} u_e − |u_e|^2 u_e,
coupled at every vertex v by Kirchhoff (free) boundary conditions: continuity of u across v, and vanishing of the signed sum of outgoing derivatives ∑_{e∋v} ∂_x u_e(v) = 0. Let H = −Δ_G denote the corresponding self-adjoint Kirchhoff Laplacian on L^2(G).

A soliton on a single edge (viewed as a line) is the standard NLS profile φ_{c,v}(x,t) = √(2c) sech(√c (x−vt)) e^{i(vx/2 − (v^2/4 − c)t)} with speed v ∈ ℝ and amplitude parameter c > 0.

(a) Establish dispersive and Strichartz-type estimates for the linear propagator e^{−itH} on G that are sufficient to develop a local and global well-posedness theory for the cubic NLS on G in an appropriate energy space.

(b) Using such estimates, prove a rigorous scattering theorem for incoming solitons: given a high-velocity soliton ψ_0 ≈ φ_{c,v}(·,0) initially supported far from the vertex set on a chosen incoming edge, describe the asymptotic behavior of the solution u(t) as t → +∞, in particular decompose u(t) along each outgoing edge into a sum of transmitted/reflected soliton-like profiles plus a dispersive remainder, and compute the corresponding transmission and reflection coefficients in terms of the topology (vertex degrees, edge lengths, internal cycles) of G.

(c) Determine how the topology of G — e.g. branching of trees, presence of bounded internal edges, or loops — quantitatively affects the dispersive decay rates, the validity of Strichartz inequalities, and the resulting soliton dynamics.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that while dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger propagator have been established on star graphs and have been extended in some works to certain tree, loop, and combined graphs, a rigorous theory of soliton scattering on metric graphs of nontrivial topology (transmission/reflection laws, asymptotic completeness with soliton resolution) remains an active and apparently open research problem; no source was found that resolves it in full generality.

paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
original_question: For nonlinear Schrödinger equations on graphs with nonlinearities that are close to, but not exactly, the integrable cubic case, do outgoing waves produced by a fast soliton-vertex interaction remain close to solitons on timescales comparable to those proved for cubic NLS? In other words, how stable is the fast-soliton scattering picture under non-integrable perturbations of the cubic nonlinearity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation posed on a metric graph $\mathcal{G}$ (a connected graph whose edges are identified with intervals of $\mathbb{R}$, joined at vertices on which Kirchhoff or other self-adjoint coupling conditions are imposed):
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\Delta_{\mathcal{G}} \psi + f(|\psi|^2)\psi, \qquad \psi(t,\cdot)\in L^2(\mathcal{G}), $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the Laplacian determined by the vertex conditions. For the cubic case $f(s)=-s$ on the line, the equation is integrable, and on graphs it is known that an incoming soliton of speed $v$ approaching a vertex produces, on each outgoing edge, a wave that is close in $H^1$ to a (rescaled) soliton on a time-scale of order $\log v / v$ as $v\to\infty$ (with explicit error bounds depending on $v$).

Let $f$ be a smooth, real-valued nonlinearity that is a small perturbation of the cubic case in a suitable norm (e.g. $f(s) = -s + \varepsilon g(s)$ with $g$ smooth, $\varepsilon$ small, and appropriate decay/growth conditions ensuring local well-posedness of the equation in $H^1(\mathcal{G})$ and existence of ground-state solitons close to the cubic ones). 

Question: For an incoming high-speed solitary wave (a solitary wave of the perturbed NLS with speed $v$ large) interacting with a vertex of $\mathcal{G}$, do the outgoing waves on each edge remain $H^1$-close to (rescaled) solitary waves of the perturbed equation, with closeness valid on a time-scale comparable to the cubic case (in particular, of order $\log v / v$ as $v \to \infty$, uniformly for $\varepsilon$ small enough)? Equivalently, prove or disprove the stability of the fast-soliton scattering picture at vertices under non-integrable perturbations of the cubic nonlinearity.
category_tag: nonlinear Schrödinger equation on metric graphs
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any work that establishes (or refutes) fast-soliton scattering at graph vertices for non-integrable perturbations of the cubic NLS on metric graphs on a time-scale comparable to that obtained via integrability in the pure cubic case. The available literature on NLS on graphs and on soliton perturbation theory does not appear to contain a definitive resolution, so the status is taken as unknown / likely open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Consider the single-input time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic smooth pair of vector fields. Must every time-optimal trajectory for this generic 3-dimensional problem be piecewise smooth, meaning that the trajectory has only finitely many switching points and is smooth between them?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth $3$-dimensional manifold and consider the single-input control-affine system
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $(f,g)$ is a generic pair of smooth vector fields on $M$ (genericity in the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology on the space of pairs of smooth vector fields). A measurable control $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$ together with the corresponding absolutely continuous trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ is called time-optimal if no other admissible control steers $q(0)$ to $q(T)$ in time strictly less than $T$.

Question: Is it true that, for a generic pair $(f,g)$, every time-optimal trajectory of the system is piecewise smooth, meaning that it has only finitely many switching times and is smooth on each interval between consecutive switching times?
status_search_result: The question of piecewise smoothness (finiteness of switchings) for time-optimal trajectories of a generic single-input control-affine system on a 3-manifold is explicitly stated as open. Related work by Agrachev–Sigalotti and Agrachev–Biolo establishes regularity results under additional genericity conditions and treats 2D-control variants in dimension 3, but no general resolution of the n=3 single-input generic case has been located in the search results.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a generic smooth pair of vector fields f and g in the single-input time-optimal system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1, on a 3-dimensional manifold, must each individual time-optimal trajectory have only finitely many switching points, even if no uniform bound over nearby trajectories is assumed?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth control-affine single-input time-optimal control system on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ of the form
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
where $f, g$ are smooth vector fields on $M$ and admissible controls are measurable functions $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. A trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ corresponding to such a control is called time-optimal if it minimizes the transfer time $T$ between its endpoints among all admissible trajectories.

A switching point of a trajectory associated to a control $u$ is a time $t\in(0,T)$ such that $u$ is not constant on any neighborhood of $t$.

Endow the space of pairs $(f,g)$ of smooth vector fields on $M$ with the Whitney $C^\infty$ topology. Prove or disprove: there exists a residual (generic) subset of pairs $(f,g)$ such that for every pair in this subset, every individual time-optimal trajectory of the corresponding system has only finitely many switching points (no uniform bound over nearby trajectories is required).
status_search_result: Recent work on switching structure for generic single-input time-optimal systems in dimension 3 (notably results showing local bounds on the number of switchings near generic points, and results showing that optimal controls are smooth outside a countable set whose accumulation structure is bounded by iterated Fuller-type singularities) does not establish the finiteness of switchings along an individual time-optimal trajectory; infinitely many (Fuller-like) switchings remain compatible with the known generic regularity. No source located that resolves the question for individual trajectories, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: In the same real analytic time-optimal control setting, can one always avoid time-optimal trajectories whose switching points occupy a set of positive measure? Equivalently, whenever two points can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory, must there exist such a trajectory whose switching set has measure zero?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a real analytic time-optimal control problem of the form
  ẋ(t) = f(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ M,  u(t) ∈ U,
where M is a real analytic manifold, U ⊂ ℝ^m is a control set (e.g. a compact polytope), and f is real analytic in x and (in standard formulations) affine in u. A time-optimal trajectory is an absolutely continuous curve x(·) : [0, T] → M, generated by a measurable control u(·) : [0, T] → U, that joins two given points x(0) = p and x(T) = q in minimum time among all admissible trajectories.

For an admissible control u(·), define its switching set to be the set of times t ∈ [0, T] at which u is not locally constant (equivalently, every neighborhood of t contains points where u takes at least two distinct values). Call this the switching set of the corresponding trajectory.

Question: Is it true that whenever two points p, q ∈ M can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory, there exists a time-optimal trajectory from p to q whose switching set has Lebesgue measure zero? Equivalently, can time-optimal trajectories whose switching sets have positive Lebesgue measure always be avoided?

Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M and a fixed starting point q0, consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H1 admissible paths starting at q0 to M, sending each path γ to γ(1). Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or can the singular curves issuing from q0 fill the entire manifold M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold equipped with a sub-Riemannian structure, that is, a smooth subbundle $\Delta \subset TM$ together with a smooth fibrewise inner product on $\Delta$. Fix a base point $q_0 \in M$. Let $\Omega_{q_0}$ denote the Hilbert manifold of admissible (horizontal) paths $\gamma:[0,1] \to M$ of Sobolev class $H^1$ that start at $q_0$, i.e. absolutely continuous curves with $\dot\gamma(t) \in \Delta_{\gamma(t)}$ a.e. and $\int_0^1 \langle \dot\gamma(t),\dot\gamma(t)\rangle\, dt < \infty$. Define the endpoint map
$$E_{q_0}: \Omega_{q_0} \longrightarrow M, \qquad E_{q_0}(\gamma) = \gamma(1).$$
A point $q \in M$ is called a regular value of $E_{q_0}$ if every $\gamma \in E_{q_0}^{-1}(q)$ is a regular point of $E_{q_0}$ (i.e. the differential $dE_{q_0}(\gamma)$ is surjective); equivalently, $q$ is not the endpoint of any singular (abnormal) horizontal curve issuing from $q_0$.

Question: Must the endpoint map $E_{q_0}$ always possess at least one regular value in $M$? Equivalently, is it possible that the set of endpoints of singular horizontal curves starting at $q_0$ covers the entire manifold $M$?
status_search_result: Recent literature on the structure of the endpoint map near singular curves and on sub-Riemannian Jacobi/exponential maps (e.g. work on normal forms near "nice" singular curves and the survey literature on singular curves) discusses partial structural results but does not establish existence of regular values of the endpoint map in general. No source found resolves whether singular curves from a fixed point can fill the whole manifold; the question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a rank-2 Martinet distribution in ℝ3, where points of the Martinet surface lie on optimal singular curves, what is the C1 classification of the germs of small sub-Riemannian spheres at points where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve? In other words, how do these sphere singularities look up to local C1 diffeomorphism in the generic Martinet case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider ℝ³ with coordinates (x, y, z) equipped with a rank-2 distribution Δ ⊂ TℝR³, that is, a smooth field of 2-planes. Such a distribution is called a Martinet distribution if Δ is bracket-generating and the Martinet surface

  Σ = { p ∈ ℝ³ : Δ(p) + [Δ, Δ](p) ≠ T_p ℝ³ }

is a smooth 2-dimensional submanifold (the locus where the Lie bracket of sections of Δ fails to span the tangent space). Endow Δ with a smooth sub-Riemannian metric g (a smoothly varying inner product on the 2-plane field), and consider the associated sub-Riemannian distance d: a horizontal curve is an absolutely continuous curve tangent a.e. to Δ, its length is computed via g, and d(p, q) is the infimum of lengths of horizontal curves joining p to q. The sub-Riemannian sphere of radius r centered at p₀ is

  S(p₀, r) = { q ∈ ℝ³ : d(p₀, q) = r }.

A horizontal curve γ is called a singular (abnormal) curve of Δ if it is a critical point of the endpoint map restricted to horizontal curves with fixed initial point; in the Martinet case, the singular curves are precisely the integral curves of the line field Δ ∩ TΣ on the Martinet surface, and for generic metrics these singular curves are locally length-minimizing.

Assume (Δ, g) is generic among Martinet sub-Riemannian structures on ℝ³, and let p₀ ∈ Σ. For sufficiently small r > 0, the sphere S(p₀, r) intersects an optimal singular curve issuing from p₀; let q be such an intersection point.

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to germs of local C¹ diffeomorphisms of ℝ³ at q, of the possible germs of S(p₀, r) at q.
status_search_result: The C¹ classification of germs of small sub-Riemannian spheres at points of optimal singular curves in the generic Martinet case is described as an open question. Subsequent literature (e.g., the survey on singular curves in sub-Riemannian geometry, results on non-subanalyticity of Martinet spheres, and the 2022 work establishing the strong Sard conjecture and C¹ regularity of singular minimizers in analytic 3D sub-Riemannian structures) has advanced understanding of the singular minimizers and the (non-)regularity of Martinet spheres but does not appear to provide a complete C¹ classification of the relevant sphere germs.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Let q0 ∈ ℝ2 and let f0, f1 be smooth vector fields defined near q0 such that f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2. For the almost-Riemannian control system qdot = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with unit-speed constraint, what is the C1 classification of the germs of the distance function Sq0 for generic pairs (f0, f1) satisfying these conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a pair of smooth vector fields $f_0, f_1$ defined in a neighborhood of a point $q_0 \in \mathbb{R}^2$. Associated with this pair is the almost-Riemannian control system
$$\dot q = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q), \qquad u_0^2 + u_1^2 = 1,$$
with the unit-speed constraint. The almost-Riemannian distance $S_{q_0}(q)$ from $q_0$ is the infimum of times $T \ge 0$ such that there exists a measurable control $(u_0, u_1)$ with $u_0^2 + u_1^2 = 1$ steering $q_0$ to $q$ in time $T$.

Let $\Delta(q) = \det(f_0(q), f_1(q))$ and define the singular set $\mathcal{Z} = \{q : \Delta(q) = 0\}$. For $q$ in the singular set, write $n_2(q)$ for the order of vanishing of $\Delta$ at $q$ along $\mathcal{Z}$, and $n_3(q)$ for an associated higher-order invariant (the number of additional brackets needed beyond second order to span the tangent space at $q$), defined so that $(n_2, n_3) = (0,0)$ at Riemannian points, $(1,0)$ at generic singular points, etc.

Assume $f_0(q_0) \wedge f_1(q_0) = 0$, $n_2(q_0) = 1$, and $n_3(q_0) = 2$.

Determine the $C^1$-classification of the germs at $q_0$ of the distance function $S_{q_0}$ for generic pairs $(f_0, f_1)$ subject to the conditions above.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a publication providing a $C^1$-classification of the distance-function germs in this specific almost-Riemannian regime ($n_2=1$, $n_3=2$). Related works on almost-Riemannian and sub-Riemannian distance singularities exist, but none found directly resolves this classification question, so the status is unclear.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: For rank-2 distributions that are not singular transitive, is the symmetry group always infinite-dimensional? The question asks whether the finite-dimensionality phenomenon might fail completely outside the singular-transitive case for rank-2 distributions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth connected manifold and let $D \subset TM$ be a rank-2 distribution on $M$ (a smooth subbundle of the tangent bundle of fiber rank 2). The symmetry algebra of $D$ is the Lie algebra $\mathrm{sym}(D)$ of vector fields $X$ on $M$ whose local flow preserves $D$, i.e. $[X, \Gamma(D)] \subset \Gamma(D)$.

Iteratively define the weak derived flag of $D$ by $D^{(0)} = D$ and $D^{(i+1)} = D^{(i)} + [D, D^{(i)}]$ (as sheaves of vector fields). The distribution $D$ is called singular transitive if, on a dense open subset of $M$, the weak derived flag stabilizes at a proper subbundle $D^{(\infty)} \subsetneq TM$ of constant rank, so that the leaves of $D^{(\infty)}$ provide a non-trivial foliation to which $D$ is tangent.

Question: Is it true that for every rank-2 distribution $D$ on a manifold $M$ (of dimension $\geq 4$) that is not singular transitive, the symmetry algebra $\mathrm{sym}(D)$ is infinite-dimensional?
status_search_result: A targeted web search for the symmetry dimension of non-singular-transitive rank-2 distributions did not return direct evidence of a resolution. The question is phrased as an expectation rather than a theorem, and no follow-up paper establishing or refuting the infinite-dimensionality claim in full generality was located.

paper_title: Some open problems
original_question: Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equation on the torus with forcing restricted to a control space E. If D is an open subset of the torus, does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace E of the closure of {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D} that is independent of the viscosity ν and still makes the system approximately controllable, or controllable in finite-dimensional projections, by localized degenerate forcing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d/2\pi\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) be the torus, and let $V$ denote the space of divergence-free, mean-zero smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{T}^d$. For $\nu>0$, consider the controlled incompressible Navier–Stokes system
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = \eta(t,x), \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
on $\mathbb{T}^d$, where the forcing $\eta(t,\cdot)$ takes values in a prescribed finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset V$ (the control space) and is otherwise arbitrary.

Let $D\subset \mathbb{T}^d$ be a fixed nonempty open set, and let $\overline{\{u\in V : \mathrm{supp}\,u\subset D\}}$ denote the closure (in a suitable Sobolev topology on $V$) of divergence-free vector fields supported in $D$.

Question: Does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace 
$$E \subset \overline{\{u\in V : \mathrm{supp}\,u\subset D\}},$$
chosen independently of the viscosity $\nu>0$, such that the controlled system above is
(a) approximately controllable in $V$, and/or
(b) controllable in projection onto every finite-dimensional subspace of $V$,
by forcings $\eta$ valued in $E$? Provide an effective construction of such a space $E$.
status_search_result: Controllability of 2D Navier–Stokes and Euler equations by degenerate (low-mode) forcing has been established by Agrachev–Sarychev and extended by others, including approximate controllability and controllability in finite-dimensional projections, with criteria valid uniformly in viscosity (including ν=0). However, those results use forcings supported on a finite set of Fourier modes, which are not localized in space. The localized version — where the control space E lies in the closure of vector fields supported in a prescribed open set D, is finite-dimensional, and independent of ν — does not appear to have been resolved in the literature reviewed; recent works (e.g., Nersesyan and collaborators) continue to address related localized controllability questions but do not explicitly settle this. Status appears open.

paper_title: On some open questions in bilinear quantum control
context_brief: Positive minimal time in infinite-dimensional approximate control
original_question: Let (A,B) satisfy Assumption 1 for the bilinear quantum system dψ/dt = (A + u(t)B)ψ, and suppose (A,B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, so the reachable set from φ_1 is dense in H. Define ρ to be the infimum of all T ≥ 0 such that the union of states reachable from φ_1 by piecewise-constant controls over times 0 ≤ t ≤ T is dense in H. Does there exist a system (A,B) that is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0, whose drift operator A is unbounded, whose control operator B has no eigenvector, and for which the minimal approximate-controllability time satisfies ρ > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a separable complex Hilbert space H with Hermitian inner product, and a bilinear control system of the form

  dψ/dt = (A + u(t) B) ψ,   ψ(0) = φ_1,

where:

• A is a (possibly unbounded) skew-adjoint operator on H with purely discrete spectrum, having an orthonormal basis (φ_k)_{k≥1} of eigenvectors with A φ_k = i λ_k φ_k, λ_k ∈ ℝ;
• B is a skew-symmetric operator on H such that A + uB generates a unitary propagator Υ^u_{t,0} on H for every piecewise-constant control u : [0,∞) → ℝ (denote by PC the set of such controls);
• (A,B) is assumed to admit a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, i.e. there is a graph on the indices {1,2,…} whose edges are the pairs (j,k) with ⟨φ_j, B φ_k⟩ ≠ 0 such that the graph is connected, and along every cycle of edges the spectral gaps |λ_j − λ_k| are non-resonant in the standard sense used to guarantee approximate controllability.

For a real number k > 0, the system (A,B) is called k-weakly-coupled if |A|^{k/2} is well-defined via functional calculus, B maps the domain D(|A|^{k/2}) into itself, and there exists a constant C_k such that

  |Re ⟨ |A|^k ψ , B ψ ⟩ | ≤ C_k ⟨ |A|^k ψ , ψ ⟩   for all ψ ∈ D(|A|^k).

Under these assumptions, the reachable set ⋃_{t ≥ 0} { Υ^u_{t,0} φ_1 : u ∈ PC } is dense in the unit sphere of H. Define

  ρ(A,B) = inf { T ≥ 0 : ⋃_{0 ≤ t ≤ T} { Υ^u_{t,0} φ_1 : u ∈ PC } is dense in the unit sphere of H }.

Question: Does there exist a pair (A,B) satisfying all the hypotheses above such that

  (i) (A,B) is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0,
  (ii) A is unbounded,
  (iii) B has no eigenvector in H, and
  (iv) ρ(A,B) > 0 ?
status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing the minimal time for approximate bilinear controllability of Schrödinger-type systems is widely acknowledged as an open problem. Subsequent works (e.g., Beauchard–Coron–Marbach on minimal time for approximate bilinear control, and Boscain–Caponigro–Chambrion–Sigalotti and Duca–Nersesyan on small-time controllability examples) have produced both examples of positive minimal time and examples of small-time approximate controllability, but no source found explicitly resolves the specific question of producing such an example simultaneously k-weakly-coupled for all k>0, with A unbounded and B having no eigenvector. Status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

paper_title: On some open questions in bilinear quantum control
context_brief: Reducing the switch complexity of approximate steering controls
original_question: Let (A,B) satisfy Assumption 1 and admit a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. Then for every target state ψ_b on the unit sphere of H and every ε > 0, one can find a piecewise-constant control u_ε : [0,T_ε] → {0,1} such that the propagated first eigenstate Υ^{u_ε}_{T_ε,0} φ_1 is within ε of ψ_b. Existing constructions can produce such controls with a number of discontinuities of order 1/ε. Is it possible instead to construct controls u_ε whose number of discontinuities is little-o of 1/ε as ε → 0?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm ∥·∥. Consider a bilinear control system on H of the form

  i d/dt ψ(t) = (A + u(t) B) ψ(t),

where:
- A is a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator on H with domain D(A), having purely discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal basis (φ_k)_{k≥1} of eigenvectors, with A φ_k = λ_k φ_k and simple eigenvalues λ_1 < λ_2 < ….
- B is a symmetric operator on H such that A + uB is essentially self-adjoint on D(A) for every u in some interval containing {0,1}, and such that the well-posedness assumption (henceforth "Assumption 1") holds: for every piecewise-constant u : [0,T] → {0,1} the Schrödinger equation above generates a unitary propagator Υ^u_{t,s} on H with Υ^u_{T,0} φ_1 ∈ H of unit norm.
- (A,B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, meaning there exists a permutation σ of ℕ* such that for every k ≥ 1 one has ⟨B φ_{σ(k)}, φ_{σ(k+1)}⟩ ≠ 0, the differences λ_{σ(k+1)} − λ_{σ(k)} are all distinct, and these gaps are non-resonant in the standard sense used for approximate controllability via adiabatic/Lie–Galerkin techniques.

Known fact. Under these hypotheses, for every target state ψ_b on the unit sphere of H and every ε > 0 there exist T_ε > 0 and a piecewise-constant control u_ε : [0,T_ε] → {0,1} such that

  ∥ Υ^{u_ε}_{T_ε,0} φ_1 − ψ_b ∥ < ε.

Moreover, classical constructions yield such u_ε with N(ε) discontinuities, where N(ε) = O(1/ε) as ε → 0+.

Question. Does there exist, under the same hypotheses, a family of piecewise-constant controls (u_ε)_{ε>0} : [0,T_ε] → {0,1} satisfying the approximate steering bound ∥Υ^{u_ε}_{T_ε,0} φ_1 − ψ_b∥ < ε whose number of discontinuities N(ε) satisfies

  N(ε) = o(1/ε)  as  ε → 0+ ?

That is, can the switch-complexity of approximate steering from the ground state φ_1 to an arbitrary unit target be made asymptotically smaller than 1/ε?
status_search_result: A web search returned related work on controllability of bilinear quantum systems and explicit-time/explicit-field constructions (e.g., Duca's 2017 work on explicit control fields), but no source directly establishing or refuting an o(1/ε) bound on the number of discontinuities for piecewise-constant {0,1}-valued approximate steering controls under a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. The status of this specific switch-complexity improvement could not be verified from available search results.

paper_title: Some remarks concerning the Grothendieck Period Conjecture
original_question: Let Qbar be the algebraic closure of Q in C. Let X be a smooth projective variety over Qbar, and let X_C^an be the compact complex analytic manifold associated to X after base change to C. For an integer k, set H_Gr^{2k}(X,Q(k)) = H_dR^{2k}(X/Qbar) intersect H^{2k}(X_C^an,Q(k)) inside H^{2k}(X_C^an,C), where Q(k) = (2*pi*i)^k Q. Let cl_Gr^X: Z^k(X)_Q -> H_Gr^{2k}(X,Q(k)) be the Q-linear cycle-class map from codimension-k algebraic cycles with rational coefficients. Is cl_Gr^X surjective; equivalently, is every cohomology class that is both algebraic-de-Rham rational and Betti-rational with Tate twist Q(k) the class of a codimension-k algebraic cycle with rational coefficients?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ denote the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$ inside $\mathbb{C}$. Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, and let $X_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{an}}$ denote the compact complex analytic manifold associated to the base change $X \times_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} \mathbb{C}$. For an integer $k \ge 0$, the algebraic de Rham cohomology $H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ embeds (after extending scalars to $\mathbb{C}$ and using the period comparison isomorphism) into the Betti cohomology $H^{2k}(X_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbb{C})$. Define the Grothendieck (de Rham–Betti) cohomology with Tate twist by
$$H^{2k}_{\mathrm{Gr}}(X, \mathbb{Q}(k)) \;:=\; H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \;\cap\; H^{2k}(X_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbb{Q}(k)) \;\subset\; H^{2k}(X_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{an}}, \mathbb{C}),$$
where $\mathbb{Q}(k) = (2\pi i)^k \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{C}$. Let
$$\mathrm{cl}^X_{\mathrm{Gr}} : Z^k(X)_{\mathbb{Q}} \longrightarrow H^{2k}_{\mathrm{Gr}}(X, \mathbb{Q}(k))$$
be the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear cycle class map sending a codimension-$k$ algebraic cycle on $X$ (with rational coefficients) to its de Rham–Betti class. Is $\mathrm{cl}^X_{\mathrm{Gr}}$ surjective? Equivalently: must every cohomology class on $X_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{an}}$ that is simultaneously rational over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ in algebraic de Rham cohomology and rational (with twist $\mathbb{Q}(k)$) in Betti cohomology be the class of a codimension-$k$ algebraic cycle with rational coefficients?
category_tag: Grothendieck period conjecture / de Rham–Betti cycle classes
status_search_result: The surjectivity of the de Rham–Betti cycle class map (the strong form of the Grothendieck Period Conjecture for smooth projective varieties over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$) is widely regarded as open. Only partial results are known, e.g. de Rham–Betti classes on products/powers of elliptic curves (with CM cases going back to Chudnovsky) are known to be algebraic. The general conjecture remains unresolved.

paper_title: Some remarks concerning the Grothendieck Period Conjecture
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety over Qbar. For all nonnegative self-products X^n and all integers j and k, must the Grothendieck cohomology group H_Gr^j(X^n,Q(k)) vanish unless j = 2k? Equivalently, outside the degree equal to twice the Tate twist, are there no de Rham-Betti classes on self-products that are simultaneously rational in the algebraic de Rham and Betti realizations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. For each integer $n\geq 0$, equip the self-product $X^n$ with its algebraic de Rham cohomology $H^j_{\mathrm{dR}}(X^n/\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ and its Betti cohomology $H^j_B(X^n(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Q})$, related by the period comparison isomorphism
$$\alpha:H^j_{\mathrm{dR}}(X^n/\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\otimes_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\mathbb{C}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^j_B(X^n(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Q})\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb{C}.$$
For an integer $k$, define the de Rham–Betti cohomology group with Tate twist $k$ by
$$H^j_{\mathrm{Gr}}(X^n,\mathbb{Q}(k))=\{c\in (2\pi i)^k\,H^j_B(X^n(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Q})\;\mid\;\alpha^{-1}(c\otimes 1)\in H^j_{\mathrm{dR}}(X^n/\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\}.$$
Question: Is it true that for every smooth projective variety $X$ over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, every integer $n\geq 0$, and all integers $j,k$, one has $H^j_{\mathrm{Gr}}(X^n,\mathbb{Q}(k))=0$ whenever $j\neq 2k$? Equivalently, do nonzero de Rham–Betti classes on self-products $X^n$ exist only in degree $j=2k$?
category_tag: Grothendieck period conjecture / de Rham-Betti classes
status_search_result: The conjectural vanishing of $H^j_{\mathrm{Gr}}(X^n,\mathbb{Q}(k))$ for $j\neq 2k$ is a form of the Grothendieck period conjecture reflecting absence of weights for the de Rham–Betti realization. It remains open in general, but has been verified in special cases: degree 1 for products of curves, abelian varieties, and K3 surfaces, and degree 2 for smooth cubic fourfolds. Subsequent work (e.g. on de Rham–Betti classes with coefficients) extends but does not resolve the general statement.

paper_title: Some remarks concerning the Grothendieck Period Conjecture
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety over Qbar, let k be a nonnegative integer, and let K be an algebraically closed field of finite transcendence degree over Q containing Qbar. For a class alpha in H_dR^{2k}(X_K/K), say alpha is absolute rational if it is rational relative to every embedding K -> C, and say alpha is absolute Hodge if it is absolute rational and belongs to the k-th Hodge filtration piece F^k H_dR^{2k}(X_K/K). Does every absolute rational class alpha necessarily have to be an absolute Hodge class?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of finite transcendence degree over $\mathbb{Q}$ containing $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, and write $X_K = X \times_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} K$. Consider the algebraic de Rham cohomology $H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_K/K)$, equipped with its Hodge filtration $F^\bullet$.

For each embedding $\sigma\colon K \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$, base change yields a comparison isomorphism
$$H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_K/K) \otimes_{K,\sigma} \mathbb{C} \;\cong\; H^{2k}_{\mathrm{B}}(X_\sigma(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Q}) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathbb{C}.$$

A class $\alpha \in H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_K/K)$ is called:
- *absolute rational* if, for every embedding $\sigma\colon K \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$, the image of $\alpha$ under the above comparison lies in $(2\pi i)^k \cdot H^{2k}_{\mathrm{B}}(X_\sigma(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Q})$;
- *absolute Hodge* if it is absolute rational and additionally satisfies $\alpha \in F^k H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_K/K)$.

Question: Must every absolute rational class $\alpha \in H^{2k}_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_K/K)$ automatically be absolute Hodge? Equivalently, does absolute rationality force $\alpha$ to lie in the $k$-th piece $F^k$ of the Hodge filtration?

status_search_result: The implication "absolute rational ⇒ absolute Hodge" is a refinement related to the Grothendieck period conjecture and the theory of absolute Hodge classes. Web search did not surface any published proof or disproof of this specific implication; partial results on the Grothendieck period conjecture exist (e.g., in degree 1 for products of curves, abelian varieties, K3 surfaces, and in degree 2 for cubic fourfolds), but the general question of whether absolute rationality forces a class to lie in $F^k$ appears not to have a known resolution.

\begin{enumerate}
\item the minimal surfaces of $S^3$,
\item the standard (totally umbilical) $2$-spheres in $S^3$, and

original_question: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{E}^m$ denote Euclidean $m$-space, and let $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a connected (semi-)Riemannian manifold $M$ with Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ (acting componentwise on $\mathbb{E}^m$-valued functions). The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if the position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$ x = c + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k, $$
where $c \in \mathbb{E}^m$ is a constant vector and the nonconstant maps $x_i : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ satisfy $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for real numbers $\lambda_i$. If the $\lambda_i$ are mutually distinct, $x$ is called of $k$-type; if one of the $\lambda_i$ equals $0$, $x$ is called of null $k$-type.

A hypersurface $M^{n}$ in a sphere $S^{n+1} \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ is called a Dupin hypersurface if along each curvature line of every principal curvature, that principal curvature is constant; it is called proper Dupin if, additionally, the number of distinct principal curvatures is constant on $M$. A hypersurface in $S^{n+1}$ is called isoparametric if all its principal curvatures are constant.

Problem.
(a) Characterize all Dupin hypersurfaces $M \subset S^{n+1} \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ that are of finite type with respect to the inclusion $M \hookrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$.
(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere $S^{n+1}$ is isoparametric.
status_search_result: The question is a long-standing open problem in submanifold theory. While compact proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres are fully classified for $g=1,2,3$ principal curvatures, the cases $g=4,6$ remain unclassified, and the original Cecil–Ryan Lie-equivalence conjecture was disproved by Pinkall–Thorbergsson and Miyaoka–Ozawa. Recent partial results (e.g., closed proper Dupin hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature plus extra constancy hypotheses being isoparametric) provide partial progress, but a full characterization of finite-type Dupin hypersurfaces of a sphere and of when such hypersurfaces are isoparametric is not available.

original_question: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. Are all biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces minimal, equivalently are there any nonminimal biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a (smooth, connected) Riemannian manifold $M$ into Euclidean $m$-space, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric on $M$, acting componentwise on $\mathbb{E}^m$-valued functions. The mean curvature vector field $H$ of the immersion satisfies the Beltrami formula $\Delta x = -nH$, where $n = \dim M$. The immersion (or the submanifold $M$) is called biharmonic if $\Delta^2 x = 0$, equivalently $\Delta H = 0$. The immersion is minimal if $H \equiv 0$, and every minimal immersion is automatically biharmonic.

Prove or disprove: every biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space is minimal. Equivalently, does there exist an isometric immersion $x: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ with $\Delta H = 0$ but $H \not\equiv 0$?
status_search_result: Chen's biharmonic conjecture (1991) remains open in general. The general case (arbitrary submanifolds, and hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ for $n \geq 5$) is widely cited as still open in surveys through 2025.

original_question: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. For hypersurfaces of Euclidean spaces, is every biharmonic hypersurface minimal?

Let $x: M^n \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ be an isometric immersion of an $n$-dimensional connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean $(n+1)$-space, and let $H$ denote the mean curvature vector of the immersion. Let $\Delta$ be the (negative semi-definite, in the analyst's sign convention used here so that $\Delta x = -nH$ where appropriate; equivalently, the rough Laplacian acting componentwise) Laplace operator of the induced metric on $M$. The immersion is called biharmonic if $\Delta^2 x = 0$, which is equivalent to $\Delta H = 0$. Every minimal immersion (i.e., $H \equiv 0$) is biharmonic.

Prove or disprove: every biharmonic hypersurface of a Euclidean space is minimal. That is, if $x: M^n \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is an isometric immersion with $\Delta H = 0$, must $H \equiv 0$?

self_contained_problem:

paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Revisited
context_brief: Finite type under first standard immersions
original_question: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a compact homogeneous manifold N with irreducible isotropy action, the i-th standard immersion is built from an orthonormal basis of the eigenspace for the i-th positive Laplacian eigenvalue; the first standard immersion uses the first positive eigenvalue. Let N be an irreducible compact homogeneous manifold immersed in a Euclidean space E^N by its first standard immersion phi, and let M be a submanifold of N. Characterize when M is finite type in E^N via phi; in particular, characterize when M is 1-type or 2-type in E^N via phi.
self_contained_problem:
Let E^m denote m-dimensional Euclidean space. An isometric immersion x: M → E^m of a Riemannian manifold M is said to be of finite type if its position vector admits a decomposition
   x = c + x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_k,
where c ∈ E^m is a constant vector and each x_i: M → E^m is a non-constant smooth map satisfying Δ x_i = λ_i x_i for some real number λ_i, with Δ the Laplace–Beltrami operator of M acting componentwise. If the λ_i are mutually distinct, x is called k-type; if additionally one of the λ_i equals zero, x is called null k-type.

Let N be an irreducible compact homogeneous Riemannian manifold (i.e., a compact homogeneous Riemannian manifold whose isotropy representation is irreducible). Let 0 < μ_1 < μ_2 < ... be the positive eigenvalues of the Laplacian on N, and for each i let {f^i_1, ..., f^i_{m_i}} be an L^2-orthonormal basis of the eigenspace E_{μ_i}. The i-th standard immersion of N is the map N → E^{m_i} given (up to homothety) by p ↦ (f^i_1(p), ..., f^i_{m_i}(p)); for i = 1 this is the first standard immersion, denoted φ: N → E^{N}.

Now let M be a (connected) submanifold of N, and consider M as a submanifold of E^{N} via φ ∘ ι, where ι: M ↪ N is the inclusion. 

Problem: Give a characterization of those submanifolds M ⊂ N for which M is of finite type in E^{N} via φ. In particular, characterize the submanifolds M ⊂ N which are of 1-type, and those which are of 2-type, in E^{N} via φ.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not return any work providing a general characterization of submanifolds M of an irreducible compact homogeneous manifold N (immersed by its first standard immersion) that are of finite, 1-, or 2-type in the ambient Euclidean space. The problem appears in standard surveys on finite-type submanifolds as an open problem, and only partial results in special cases (e.g., spheres, projective spaces) are known. No definitive resolution was located.

original_question: In active galactic nuclei, accretion of gas onto a super-massive black hole is thought to power a relativistic jet that is roughly perpendicular to the accretion disk. What is the nature of the coupling between the accretion disk and the relativistic jet that allows some active galactic nuclei to launch these highly collimated, high-energy outflows?
status_search_result: The mechanism coupling accretion disks to relativistic jets in AGN remains an outstanding open problem in high-energy astrophysics. paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
context_brief: comparison with blazars and radio galaxies
original_question: Gamma-ray-emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets, but the previously established gamma-ray jet populations were blazars and radio galaxies. What are the differences between gamma-ray-emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies and blazars or radio galaxies in their physical properties, jet behavior, or evolutionary status?
self_contained_problem:
Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are luminous central regions of galaxies powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole. Some AGN launch collimated, relativistic jets of plasma; among the historically established gamma-ray–detected jetted AGN populations are blazars (jetted AGN whose jet is closely aligned with the line of sight, subdivided into BL Lac objects and flat-spectrum radio quasars) and radio galaxies (jetted AGN viewed at larger angles). A narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxy is a Seyfert 1 type AGN characterized by (i) full width at half maximum of the broad Hβ emission line less than 2000 km/s, (ii) a flux ratio [O III]λ5007/Hβ < 3, and (iii) often strong Fe II multiplet emission; NLS1s are typically associated with relatively low-mass supermassive black holes (∼10^6–10^8 M_⊙) accreting at high Eddington ratios. A subclass of NLS1s has been detected in gamma rays (E ≳ 100 MeV), implying that they too host relativistic jets.

Problem. Identify and characterize the systematic differences between the population of gamma-ray–emitting NLS1 galaxies and the populations of blazars and radio galaxies, in the following respects:

1. Physical properties of the central engine and host: distributions of black hole mass, Eddington ratio, accretion mode, host galaxy morphology (spiral vs. elliptical), and large-scale environment.

2. Jet properties: jet power, bulk Lorentz factor, viewing angle distribution, radio morphology and extent (compact vs. extended kpc-scale structure), broadband spectral energy distribution (peak frequencies of the synchrotron and inverse-Compton humps, Compton dominance), and high-energy variability.

3. Evolutionary status: whether gamma-ray NLS1s represent an early (young) phase of jetted AGN evolution that may evolve into blazars/radio galaxies, a parallel low-mass branch of the jetted AGN population, or a distinct phenomenon, and what observational diagnostics (e.g. extended radio emission, black hole mass growth time scales, host morphology) discriminate between these scenarios.

Provide a complete comparative description supported by quantitative population statistics.
status_search_result: This is an astrophysics research question rather than a closed mathematical problem. Studies since 2013 (e.g., Foschini et al., Berton et al., Paliya et al., D'Ammando reviews through 2024) have made substantial progress characterizing gamma-ray NLS1s — establishing they tend to host lower-mass, higher-Eddington black holes than blazars, often reside in spiral hosts, and may represent a young or rejuvenated phase of jetted AGN — but a complete, settled comparative picture (especially regarding host morphology statistics and evolutionary connection to blazars/radio galaxies) remains an active and unresolved research topic.

original_question: Only a small fraction of narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are radio-loud, and radio-loudness in this context is discussed in terms of the ratio of rest-frame 1.4 GHz to 4400 Å flux density. What is the origin of radio-loudness in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, especially in the gamma-ray-emitting subset?

Consider active galactic nuclei classified as narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies. Define a source to be radio-loud if the ratio R = F(1.4 GHz) / F(4400 Å) of rest-frame radio (1.4 GHz) to optical B-band (4400 Å) flux densities exceeds the conventional threshold (R > 10), and radio-quiet otherwise. Empirically, only a small fraction (of order a few percent) of NLS1 galaxies are radio-loud, and within this radio-loud subset a further subset is detected as gamma-ray emitters, indicating the presence of relativistic jets closely aligned with the line of sight. NLS1 galaxies are typically hosted in late-type (spiral) galaxies and powered by black holes with relatively low masses (≈ 10^6–10^8 M_sun) accreting at high Eddington ratios.

Identify and characterize the physical mechanism(s) responsible for the radio-loudness of NLS1 galaxies, with particular attention to the gamma-ray-emitting subset. In particular, determine which intrinsic parameters of the central engine and host (black hole mass and spin, accretion rate, jet launching mechanism, host morphology, environment) control whether an NLS1 develops a powerful relativistic jet, and explain why such jets occur in only a small fraction of the NLS1 population.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., reviews and studies from 2018–2019 on relativistic jets in gamma-ray-emitting NLS1 galaxies) continues to treat the origin of radio-loudness in NLS1s — and especially the conditions that allow a small fraction of them to launch powerful relativistic jets despite their low black-hole masses and spiral hosts — as an open question. paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
original_question: Is there a limiting black-hole mass above which active galactic nuclei are preferentially radio-loud, and if so how does that threshold apply to narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies whose commonly quoted black-hole masses are lower than those of typical radio-loud quasars?
self_contained_problem:
An active galactic nucleus (AGN) is the luminous central region of a galaxy powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole of mass $M_{\rm BH}$. An AGN is called radio-loud if the ratio $R = F_{5\,\mathrm{GHz}}/F_{B}$ of its rest-frame 5 GHz radio flux density to optical $B$-band flux density satisfies $R > 10$, and radio-quiet otherwise. Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies are a class of AGN distinguished by (i) full width at half maximum of the broad H$\beta$ emission line below $2000\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, (ii) a flux ratio $[\mathrm{O\,III}]\lambda 5007/\mathrm{H}\beta < 3$, and (iii) the presence of strong optical Fe II multiplets; their inferred black-hole masses, typically derived from single-epoch virial estimators using broad-line widths and continuum luminosities, are commonly reported in the range $10^{6}$–$10^{8}\,M_\odot$, lower than the masses $\gtrsim 10^{8}$–$10^{9}\,M_\odot$ usually inferred for radio-loud quasars.

Determine whether there exists a threshold mass $M^{*}$ such that AGN with $M_{\rm BH} > M^{*}$ are preferentially radio-loud (in the sense above) while AGN with $M_{\rm BH} < M^{*}$ are preferentially radio-quiet. If such a threshold $M^{*}$ exists, describe how the observed population of radio-loud NLS1 galaxies, whose virial black-hole mass estimates lie below $M^{*}$, can be reconciled with this threshold — for example, by systematic underestimation of $M_{\rm BH}$ in NLS1s due to disc-like broad-line region geometry and orientation effects, by relativistic beaming of jet emission inflating $R$, or by genuine violation of the threshold criterion.
status_search_result: The question of whether a black-hole mass threshold separates radio-loud from radio-quiet AGN has been debated for decades, with claims of a threshold near $\sim 10^{8}\,M_\odot$ challenged by the discovery of radio-loud and even jetted NLS1 galaxies with virial black-hole masses well below that value. Subsequent work has argued either that NLS1 black-hole masses are systematically underestimated (orientation/disc-BLR effects) or that radio loudness depends primarily on accretion rate and spin rather than mass alone. No consensus threshold has been established, so the problem remains open.

context_brief: large black holes in spiral-hosted NLSy1s
original_question: Some black-hole-mass estimates for gamma-ray-emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are corrected upward by accounting for radiation pressure, possible disk-like broad-line-region geometry, or optical/ultraviolet accretion-disk modeling, yielding masses of about 10^8 to 10^9 solar masses. If those larger mass estimates are correct, how can such large black holes exist in a class of active galactic nuclei that is usually hosted in spiral galaxies?
self_contained_problem:
Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies form a class of active galactic nuclei (AGN) characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical broad emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II emission, and weak [O III] emission. They are typically hosted in spiral galaxies and have traditionally been associated with relatively low-mass central black holes (M_BH ∼ 10^6–10^8 M_⊙) accreting near the Eddington limit. Standard single-epoch virial black hole mass estimators use the broad-line-region (BLR) radius–luminosity relation together with an isotropic-velocity geometric factor f.

For the subset of NLSy1 galaxies detected in γ-rays (which host relativistic jets), several alternative mass-estimation methods — namely (i) corrections to the virial estimate that account for radiation pressure on the BLR clouds, (ii) adoption of a flattened, disk-like BLR geometry with an inclination-dependent geometric factor f, and (iii) modeling of the optical/ultraviolet continuum as thermal emission from a standard accretion disk — give black hole masses in the range M_BH ∼ 10^8–10^9 M_⊙, an order of magnitude or more above conventional virial estimates.

Problem: Assuming these higher mass estimates (M_BH ∼ 10^8–10^9 M_⊙) are correct for γ-ray-emitting NLSy1s, provide a physically and observationally consistent explanation for how black holes of such large mass can reside in AGN hosted by spiral galaxies, given that galaxies hosting black holes in this mass range are normally massive ellipticals or galaxies with classical bulges obeying the M_BH–σ and M_BH–M_bulge scaling relations. In particular, identify the host-galaxy structural properties (e.g., classical bulge vs. pseudobulge, disk vs. merger remnant), the BH–host coevolution scenario, and/or revisions of scaling relations that would allow such systems to exist, and reconcile this with the observed prevalence of spiral morphologies among NLSy1 hosts.
status_search_result: The question of whether γ-ray NLSy1s truly harbor 10^8–10^9 M_⊙ black holes, and how such masses can be reconciled with spiral host morphologies, remains actively debated. Subsequent works either revise the masses downward via disk-like BLR geometric factors (e.g., Decarli et al., Liu et al. 2017 on 1H 0323+342) or argue the hosts contain classical bulges/merger features rather than pure disks (e.g., studies of PKS 2004-447 and 1H 0323+342). No consensus resolution has been reached.

paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
original_question: Radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies appear to have central-engine properties that differ from those of quasars and are reflected in their unusual optical characteristics. How do the properties of the central engine in radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies affect the mechanisms that produce gamma-ray emission?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 (RL-NLS1) galaxies, a subclass of active galactic nuclei (AGN) characterized by: (i) optical spectra with relatively narrow permitted Balmer emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) < 2000 km/s), strong Fe II multiplets, and weak [O III] emission; (ii) high radio-loudness parameter R = f(5 GHz)/f(B-band) > 10; and (iii) inferred supermassive black hole masses in the range ~10^6–10^8 solar masses, with high accretion rates near the Eddington limit. A subset of RL-NLS1s have been detected as sources of high-energy (>100 MeV) gamma-ray emission, indicating the presence of relativistic jets closely aligned to the line of sight, analogous to blazars but launched by central engines whose physical parameters (notably lower black hole mass, higher Eddington-normalized accretion rate, and distinct broad-line region structure) differ from those of flat-spectrum radio quasars.

Determine, quantitatively and from first principles, how the distinctive central-engine properties of RL-NLS1s — in particular the black hole mass, accretion rate, accretion disc structure, broad-line region geometry, and seed photon environment — control the gamma-ray production mechanisms in their relativistic jets. Specifically:

(a) Identify the dominant high-energy radiation process (synchrotron self-Compton vs. external Compton scattering of disc, broad-line region, or dusty torus photons) as a function of the central-engine parameters, and predict the location along the jet at which the bulk of the gamma-ray luminosity is produced.

(b) Derive the resulting spectral energy distribution and its expected variability timescales, and explain how these depend on the black hole mass and Eddington ratio characteristic of RL-NLS1s.

(c) Determine whether the central-engine differences relative to flat-spectrum radio quasars give rise to systematic differences in jet power, gamma-ray duty cycle, and maximum attainable photon energies, and characterize these differences.

status_search_result: The connection between central-engine properties of radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies and their gamma-ray production mechanisms remains an active topic of debate. context_brief: nature of G2/DSO near the Galactic Center
original_question: What is the physical nature of the G2/DSO source that was approaching the Galactic Center in 2013–2014: is it primarily a gas-and-dust cloud, a dust-enshrouded star, or something else, and how can near-infrared integral-field observations discriminate among the proposed scenarios?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the compact infrared source known as G2/DSO observed on a highly eccentric orbit approaching the supermassive black hole Sgr A* at the center of the Milky Way, with pericenter passage in 2013–2014. Two principal scenarios have been proposed for its physical nature: (i) a pure gas-and-dust cloud with no central stellar object, which on a close passage would be tidally disrupted and dispersed; and (ii) a dust-enshrouded star whose extended envelope produces the observed infrared excess and Brγ emission while the stellar core keeps the source compact through pericenter.

(a) Determine the physical nature of G2/DSO: is it primarily a coreless gas-and-dust cloud, a dust-enshrouded star, or some other configuration?

(b) Identify observational diagnostics, accessible through near-infrared integral-field-unit (IFU) spectroscopy (e.g. compactness vs. tidal stretching of the Brγ line emission before and after pericenter, K-band continuum identification, line-of-sight velocity evolution, polarization signature), that discriminate between these scenarios, and state quantitatively how the predicted signatures differ in each scenario.
status_search_result: Observations during and after the 2014 pericenter passage indicate G2/DSO remained spatially compact in Brγ emission, contradicting the pure coreless-cloud scenario and favoring a dust-enshrouded (likely young) star in an accretion phase. Near-infrared IFU observations, K-band identifications, and polarimetry have been the key discriminants. The dust-enshrouded star interpretation is now widely supported, though details (stellar type, accretion state, role of the dusty envelope) remain under study, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully closed.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
context_brief: nuclear star clusters and massive black holes
original_question: Do very massive black holes inhibit the formation of nuclear star clusters, or are nuclear star clusters instead disrupted during the growth of the central black hole?
self_contained_problem: Galactic nuclei are observed to host nuclear star clusters (NSCs), central massive black holes (MBHs), or both. Empirically, NSCs are prevalent in galaxies with stellar masses below roughly 10^10 solar masses, MBHs dominate in galaxies above roughly 10^12 solar masses, and intermediate-mass galaxies frequently host both. Determine which of the following two scenarios accounts for the absence of nuclear star clusters in the most massive galaxies hosting very massive central black holes: (i) the presence of a sufficiently massive central black hole inhibits the formation of a nuclear star cluster in the first place; or (ii) a nuclear star cluster does form but is subsequently disrupted (for example by tidal stresses, dynamical heating, or other interactions) during the growth of the central black hole. Provide a physical mechanism, supported by dynamical and/or formation arguments, that distinguishes between these two scenarios as a function of the host-galaxy and black-hole mass.
status_search_result: Subsequent work indicates both mechanisms are at play: dynamical studies show that a sufficiently massive central black hole can suppress core collapse and tidally expand/disrupt a pre-existing NSC, while observational scaling relations and simulations suggest NSC growth is also quenched in the most massive galaxies. The relative importance of inhibition versus disruption as a function of galaxy/BH mass remains under active investigation, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully settled.

paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
context_brief: jet drivers in Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 galaxies
original_question: In radio-loud Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 galaxies, which have relatively low black-hole masses yet can host powerful relativistic jets, what physical drivers launch the jets, and is jet launching controlled by the spin of the compact object or by other parameters?
self_contained_problem:
Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies are a class of active galactic nuclei characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (FWHM(Hβ) ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II emission, and inferred central black-hole masses in the range M_BH ∼ 10^6 – 10^8 M_⊙, typically accreting close to the Eddington limit. A subset of NLS1s is radio-loud and has been observed to host relativistic, sometimes γ-ray emitting, jets — a phenomenon traditionally associated with much more massive black holes in radio galaxies and blazars. Because their black-hole masses bridge the stellar-mass and supermassive regimes, these radio-loud NLS1s are often viewed as a missing link in the unification of relativistic jets across all mass scales.

Identify and characterize the physical mechanisms responsible for launching relativistic jets in radio-loud NLS1 galaxies. In particular, determine whether the jet-launching process is primarily controlled by the spin of the central compact object (e.g., via a Blandford–Znajek-type mechanism), or whether other parameters — such as accretion rate, magnetic flux threading the black hole and inner disk, host-galaxy or environmental properties, black-hole mass, or disk-wind/Blandford–Payne processes — provide the dominant control. Provide observational and/or theoretical criteria that discriminate among these possibilities.
category_tag: Relativistic jets in active galactic nuclei
status_search_result: Recent literature (post-2017 reviews and individual source studies of radio-loud NLS1s such as 1H 0323+342, PKS 0558-504, and RX J2314.9+2243) continues to debate the jet-launching mechanism. Some studies infer high black-hole spin from disk modeling, while others argue spin alone is insufficient and emphasize magnetic flux, accretion rate, or host-galaxy properties. No consensus has emerged, and reviews still describe the physical drivers and the role of spin as open questions.

original_question: What physical mechanisms launch highly ionized gas close to active galactic nuclei, and how are those ionized outflows connected to other feedback mechanisms such as jets or larger-scale outflows?
self_contained_problem: In the context of active galactic nuclei (AGN), the central regions of accreting supermassive black holes are observed to drive significant amounts of highly ionized gas outward at high velocities, in addition to producing relativistic jets and large-scale (kpc-scale) outflows of cooler/molecular and warm ionized gas. Identify and characterize the physical launching mechanisms — such as radiation pressure on lines and dust, magnetohydrodynamic acceleration from the accretion disk, thermal driving from a hot corona, or magnetocentrifugal winds — that produce the highly ionized gas observed close to the central engine of AGN. Furthermore, determine how these nuclear ionized outflows are physically and causally connected to other AGN feedback channels, including relativistic jets and larger-scale (galaxy-wide) outflows: specifically, establish whether the nuclear ionized winds drive, are driven by, or coexist independently with these other feedback components, and quantify the energy, momentum, and mass-loading relationships between them.
status_search_result: The launching mechanisms of nuclear highly ionized AGN outflows (e.g., ultra-fast outflows and warm absorbers) and their coupling to jets and galaxy-scale outflows remain an active and debated research area. Recent observational and theoretical studies (e.g., XRISM results, multi-phase outflow surveys) continue to investigate radiation-driven vs. magnetically-driven scenarios and the jet/wind connection, with no consensus model.

status_search_result: The structure of the broad-line region and its connection to a clumpy/molecular torus remains an active area of research in AGN astrophysics. paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
original_question: Do active galactic nuclei that genuinely lack a broad-line region exist, or are observed cases without broad emission lines mainly caused by observational biases such as spatial resolution and sensitivity, by obscuration and orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration?
self_contained_problem:
In the standard unified model of active galactic nuclei (AGN), every AGN possesses a broad-line region (BLR): a population of dense gas clouds, located close to the central supermassive black hole, that produces broad permitted emission lines (with full-widths of order 10^3–10^4 km/s) in the rest-frame optical/UV spectrum. Within this model, AGN that do not display broad emission lines (so-called type 2 AGN) are interpreted as objects in which the BLR is hidden from the observer's line of sight by an obscuring dusty torus, by orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration; alternatively, broad lines may be missed because of insufficient spatial resolution or sensitivity, or because they are diluted by host-galaxy starlight.

An alternative hypothesis posits that there exist genuine "non-hidden BLR" AGN (sometimes called "true type 2" AGN) in which the BLR is physically absent, for instance because at sufficiently low Eddington-scaled accretion rates the accretion flow transitions to a radiatively inefficient mode that cannot sustain the BLR clouds.

Question: Do AGN that intrinsically lack a broad-line region truly exist as a physical class, or can every observed AGN without detected broad emission lines be accounted for by observational biases (spatial resolution, sensitivity, host-galaxy dilution), by obscuration and orientation effects, or by transient partial obscuration?
status_search_result: Multiple observational studies since the late 2000s have identified candidate "true type 2" Seyfert galaxies (e.g., NGC 3147, NGC 3660, Q2131-427) which display narrow emission lines without evidence of X-ray absorption and without polarized broad lines, supporting the existence of AGN intrinsically lacking a BLR, typically at low Eddington ratios. However, the size and purity of this class remain debated, with ongoing work refining samples and ruling out obscuration/dilution alternatives, so the question is partially resolved rather than fully settled.
