paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
context_brief: Adiabaticity and coherence limits of the Unified Model
original_question: How can the validity limits of the Unified Model for collective quadrupole motion in finite nuclei be quantified, specifically the breakdown of adiabatic separation when collective and quasiparticle time scales become comparable and the loss of coherence caused by the small number of correlated nucleons?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Unified Model of collective quadrupole motion in a finite nucleus, in which a small number A of nucleons is described by a Hamiltonian that couples intrinsic quasiparticle degrees of freedom to collective quadrupole shape variables (β, γ) and their conjugate momenta. The model rests on two implicit assumptions: (i) adiabatic separation of scales, requiring that the characteristic collective time T_coll be much larger than the characteristic quasiparticle time T_qp; and (ii) coherence of the collective mode, requiring that a sufficiently large number of nucleons participate coherently in each collective quantum so that the mode behaves as a well-defined bosonic excitation.

Provide a quantitative, non-perturbative formulation that determines the validity limits of this model. Specifically:

1. Derive a precise criterion, expressed in terms of T_coll/T_qp (or equivalently the ratio of collective excitation energy to the two-quasiparticle gap), at which the adiabatic separation breaks down. In particular, characterize the regime T_coll/T_qp ≲ 3 in which adiabaticity fails, and describe how the coupling between quasiparticle and collective degrees of freedom should be treated non-perturbatively in this regime.

2. Define a coherence length (or coherence number) N_coh for the collective quadrupole mode in terms of the underlying nucleonic correlations, and quantify how the granular structure of the collective degrees of freedom—arising from the finite number of correlated nucleons—produces progressive decoherence of the collective modes as the number of excitation quanta n increases. Determine the maximal n for which the collective description remains meaningful as a function of A and N_coh.

3. Combine (1) and (2) into a unified domain-of-validity diagram for the Unified Model, identifying which observables (energies, B(E2) values, branching ratios) remain reliable and which require corrections beyond the adiabatic, coherent approximation.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual/quantitative problem about the validity limits of the Unified Model of nuclear collective motion. No definitive, generally accepted quantitative criterion for the breakdown of adiabaticity (T_coll/T_qp threshold) or for the coherence length in terms of the number of correlated nucleons is established in the literature; partial progress exists via microscopic approaches (QRPA, IBM mappings, generator coordinate method, symmetry-adapted no-core shell model), but a unified quantitative answer remains an active research topic.

paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
context_brief: Finite boson-number cutoff in the Interacting Boson Model
original_question: Does the Interacting Boson Model assumption that the number of collective s and d bosons is finite and equal to half the number of valence nucleons or holes systematically fail for high-spin yrast collectivity, and can this be tested across nuclei by comparing predicted and measured B(E2) transition strengths beyond the spin range allowed by the boson-number cutoff?
self_contained_problem:
In the Interacting Boson Model (IBM) of nuclear collective motion, low-lying collective excitations of an even-even nucleus are described in terms of a finite system of bosons of two kinds: monopole bosons s (angular momentum 0) and quadrupole bosons d (angular momentum 2). A central postulate of the IBM is that the total boson number N is fixed and equal to half the number of valence nucleons (or valence holes) outside the nearest doubly-magic core. Because each d boson carries angular momentum 2, the maximal yrast spin that can be built from N_d ≤ N quadrupole bosons is I_max = 2N, and the electric-quadrupole transition strengths B(E2; I → I−2) within the ground-state band are predicted to decrease as I approaches this cutoff and to vanish at I = 2N.

Formulate and resolve the following question rigorously:

(a) Does the finite boson-number assumption of the IBM (N = (number of valence nucleons or holes)/2) systematically fail to describe high-spin yrast collectivity in deformed even-even nuclei, in the sense that observed B(E2; I → I−2) values along the ground-state band remain large (and in particular nonzero) for spins I exceeding the IBM cutoff 2N?

(b) Devise a systematic, model-independent experimental test across a representative set of nuclei that compares IBM-predicted B(E2; I → I−2) strengths within the ground-state band against measured values for spins approaching and exceeding the boson-number limit, and determine whether the discrepancy is generic rather than confined to isolated cases.

Provide either a proof that the finite boson-number cutoff is consistent with high-spin yrast B(E2) data (with quantified deviations within experimental uncertainty), or evidence that the cutoff is systematically violated, identifying the class of nuclei in which the failure occurs.
category_tag: Interacting Boson Model / nuclear collective motion
status_search_result: The question concerns a long-standing conceptual issue regarding the finite boson-number cutoff in the IBM. Available literature continues to debate the validity of the IBM at high spin, with isolated case studies (e.g., in rare-earth deformed nuclei) showing tension with measured B(E2) values beyond the cutoff, but no comprehensive systematic test has been established that resolves the question. The status is best described as open.

paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
context_brief: Appearance and disappearance of rotational modes
original_question: Under what microscopic conditions do rotational collective modes appear as nuclei move away from closed shells, and under what conditions do those rotational modes disappear with excitation energy above the yrast line, when collective rotation and single-particle motion are strongly coupled on comparable time scales?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite system of A interacting nucleons (protons and neutrons) governed by a realistic two-body (and possibly three-body) nuclear Hamiltonian. Treat the system within a self-consistent mean-field framework in which the nucleons move in an average potential generated by themselves, and consider the cranked (rotating) mean-field approximation: minimize the expectation value of H − ωJ_x in a Slater determinant (or HFB quasiparticle vacuum), where J_x is the angular-momentum projection along a body-fixed axis and ω is a Lagrange multiplier (cranking frequency). Assume that the time scales of collective rotational motion and of single-particle motion are comparable, so that the two are strongly coupled.

In this framework, characterize, in terms of the underlying single-particle structure (shell filling, deformation of the self-consistent mean field, pairing correlations, level density near the Fermi surface, and quasiparticle alignments), the following:

(a) Necessary and sufficient microscopic conditions on a nucleus with given proton and neutron numbers (Z, N) for rotational collective modes — i.e. regular rotational bands of states whose energies depend on angular momentum I approximately as E(I) ≈ I(I+1)/(2𝓘) with a well-defined moment of inertia 𝓘 — to emerge as one moves away from closed-shell (magic) nucleon numbers.

(b) Necessary and sufficient microscopic conditions under which these rotational modes cease to exist (band termination / damping of rotational correlations) as the excitation energy E* increases above the yrast line (the locus of lowest-energy states for each angular momentum I).

Provide a precise criterion, expressible through properties of the self-consistent rotating mean-field solution and its quasiparticle spectrum, that distinguishes the regimes of existence and non-existence of rotational collective motion in both situations (a) and (b).
status_search_result: The microscopic conditions for the onset and damping of nuclear rotational bands remain an active research area. Studies based on cranked mean-field, tilted-axis cranking, and shell-model approaches have given partial answers (e.g., onset of deformation away from magic numbers, rotational damping above the yrast line at E* of a few MeV studied by Døssing, Matsuo, Bracco and others), but no complete microscopic criterion exists. The question is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
context_brief: Non-perturbative collective-quasiparticle coupling beyond the adiabatic region
original_question: How can the strong coupling between collective quadrupole degrees of freedom and quasiparticle degrees of freedom be treated non-perturbatively for higher excited states and odd-A nuclei outside the low-density adiabatic region?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a nuclear many-body system whose low-energy dynamics is described by two interacting sectors of degrees of freedom: (i) collective quadrupole degrees of freedom, encoded by the five real shape variables associated with the quadrupole tensor (parameterised, e.g., by the Bohr variables (β, γ) together with three Euler angles), and (ii) quasiparticle degrees of freedom, obtained from a Bogoliubov transformation of single-nucleon creation/annihilation operators acting on a paired Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov vacuum. Let H = H_coll + H_qp + H_coup denote a Hamiltonian on the tensor-product Hilbert space of these two sectors, where H_coup represents a particle–vibration (quadrupole–quasiparticle) coupling.

In the low-level-density adiabatic regime the coupling H_coup can be treated perturbatively (e.g., by quasiparticle–phonon expansions or generator-coordinate-method approximations). Outside this regime — for higher excited states, where level density is large and adiabaticity fails, and for odd-mass (odd-A) nuclei, where a blocked quasiparticle is always present — the coupling becomes strong and perturbation theory diverges; both non-adiabaticity (failure of the Born–Oppenheimer separation between collective and intrinsic motion) and decoherence (loss of phase coherence between collective wave packets due to coupling to the dense quasiparticle background) must be incorporated.

Problem. Devise a mathematically controlled, non-perturbative scheme for diagonalising (or otherwise computing the spectrum and transition matrix elements of) such a coupled collective–quasiparticle Hamiltonian H in the strong-coupling regime applicable to higher-lying excited states and to odd-A nuclei, in a way that simultaneously accommodates non-adiabatic effects and decoherence between the collective and quasiparticle sectors.
status_search_result: The question concerns a long-standing methodological challenge in nuclear structure theory: a fully non-perturbative treatment of strong collective–quasiparticle coupling beyond adiabatic, low-energy regimes. Recent literature on quasiparticle–phonon coupling, particle–vibration coupling (PVC), and generator-coordinate/symmetry-projected methods (e.g., works by Litvinova, Tselyaev, and collaborators, and ongoing development of multi-reference EDF methods) indicates partial progress for specific observables but no general accepted non-perturbative framework for higher states and odd-A nuclei. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Transpose Schur inclusions for elementary and complete seeds
original_question: When (m,n) = (ad,bd) with d = gcd(m,n), write e_{m,n}(x;q,t) := e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) and h_{m,n}(x;q,t) := h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t). Let α′ = α′(m,n) be the number of integer points between the (m,n-1)-staircase path and the minimal (m,n)-staircase, and let β′ be the analogous exponent appearing in the transpose version of the complete-homogeneous inequality. For every pair m,n ≥ 1, can one prove the Schur-positivity inequalities q^{α′} e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) ⪯_s e_{m,n}(x;q,t) and q^{β′} e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) ⪯_s (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}(x;q,t), preferably by explaining them as inclusions of bigraded representations?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Work in the algebra of symmetric functions in variables x = (x_1,x_2,...) over the field Q(q,t). For coprime positive integers a,b let e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) and h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) denote the rectangular (q,t)-elementary and (q,t)-complete symmetric functions associated with the (ad,bd)-rectangle, defined as the images, under the operators of the elliptic Hall algebra acting on symmetric functions, of e_d and h_d via the natural slope-(b/a) action (so that for d=1 these reduce to the (a,b)-elementary and complete symmetric functions of rectangular Catalan combinatorics, and for (a,b) = (1,1) they specialize to the standard nabla-deformed e_d and h_d).

For arbitrary positive integers m,n with d = gcd(m,n) and m = ad, n = bd, set
   e_{m,n}(x;q,t) := e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t),    h_{m,n}(x;q,t) := h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t).

Schur order. For two symmetric functions F,G ∈ Λ ⊗ Q(q,t) write F ⪯_s G iff G − F expands in the Schur basis with coefficients that are polynomials in q,t with nonnegative integer coefficients.

Staircase exponents. For positive integers m,n let the (m,n)-staircase be the lattice path from (0,n) to (m,0) lying just below the diagonal joining these two points; let α'(m,n) denote the number of integer points strictly between the (m,n−1)-staircase and the minimal (m,n)-staircase, and let β'(m,n) be the analogous count obtained by exchanging the roles of e and h (the count appropriate to the transpose/complete-homogeneous version below).

Problem. Prove that for every pair of integers m,n ≥ 1 the following Schur-positivity inequalities hold:
   (i)  q^{α'(m,n)} · e_{m,n−1}(x;q,t)  ⪯_s  e_{m,n}(x;q,t),
   (ii) q^{β'(m,n)} · e_{m,n−1}(x;q,t)  ⪯_s  (−qt)^{1−d} · h_{m,n}(x;q,t).

It is desired, moreover, to realize each inequality as the bigraded character identity coming from an explicit inclusion of bigraded S_N-modules (where N is the appropriate degree), so that the difference of the two sides is the bigraded Frobenius characteristic of an S_N-module quotient.

paper_title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS
context_brief: Multiplicativity of specialized operators at t = 1
original_question: For any seed f_d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let Θ_{a,b}(f_d) be the corresponding operator and let f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1) denote its value on 1 after specializing t = 1. Does the specialized operator Θ_{a,b}(f_d)|_{t=1} act on every symmetric function g(x) simply as multiplication by f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1)? Equivalently, can one prove the multiplicativity relation (f_d g_k)^{(a,b)}(x;q,1) = f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1) g^{(a,b)}_k(x;q,1) for all seeds and all coprime a,b ≥ 1?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. Assume one has, for each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$, a family of linear operators
$$\Theta_{a,b}(f_d):\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)}\longrightarrow \Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q,t)},$$
indexed by "seed" symmetric functions $f_d$ of degree $d$ (the operators arise from the elliptic Hall algebra / rectangular Catalan combinatorics framework, generalizing the nabla operator). For a seed $f_d$ and coprime $a,b\ge 1$, define the symmetric function
$$f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) := \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(1).$$

Question. Prove or disprove: for every seed $f_d$ and every pair of coprime integers $a,b\ge 1$, the specialization at $t=1$ of the operator $\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)$ acts on $\Lambda_{\mathbb{Q}(q)}$ as multiplication by the symmetric function $f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)$; that is,
$$\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(g(x))\big|_{t=1} \;=\; f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)\cdot g(x)$$
for every symmetric function $g(x)$.

Equivalently, establish the multiplicativity identity
$$(f_d\, g_k)^{(a,b)}(x;q,1) \;=\; f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)\, g_k^{(a,b)}(x;q,1)$$
for all seeds $f_d, g_k$ and all coprime $a,b\ge 1$.
status_search_result: A web search surfaced the original problem list and later expository works by Bergeron (2021–2022 notes on Macdonald polynomials, operators, and rectangular Catalan combinatorics), which continue to discuss the t=1 specialization where nabla-type operators become multiplicative, but no source consulted explicitly announces a proof of the multiplicativity statement for all seeds and all coprime (a,b). Status could not be definitively verified from the available evidence.

paper_title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS
context_brief: e-positivity of monomial-seed operators at t = 1 + r
original_question: For a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,1+r) := Θ_{a,b}(m_μ)(1) specialized at t = 1 + r. Is the renormalized symmetric function (-1)^(d-ℓ(μ)) m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,1+r) always e-positive, meaning that its expansion in the elementary symmetric basis has coefficients in N[q,r]? If it is, can this e-positivity be explained by a direct combinatorial enumeration analogous to the Dyck-path formula discussed earlier in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda$ denote the ring of symmetric functions in infinitely many variables $x = (x_1, x_2, \ldots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. For a partition $\mu = (\mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots)$, let $m_\mu(x)$ denote the monomial symmetric function and $\ell(\mu)$ the number of (nonzero) parts of $\mu$, with $|\mu| = d$. For coprime integers $a, b \geq 1$, let $\Theta_{a,b}$ be the rectangular-Catalan symmetric-function operator on $\Lambda$ associated with the slope $b/a$ (the operator built from the modified Macdonald and nabla-type operators that conjecturally produces the rectangular $(a,b)$-Catalan symmetric function when applied to $1$). For a partition $\mu$ of $d$, define
$$m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, t) \;:=\; \Theta_{a,b}(m_\mu)\big|_{1},$$
that is, the symmetric function in $\Lambda$ obtained by applying $\Theta_{a,b}(m_\mu)$ to the constant $1$. Substitute $t = 1 + r$ to obtain $m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, 1+r) \in \Lambda \otimes \mathbb{Q}(q,r)$.

(i) Prove or disprove: for every partition $\mu \vdash d$ and every pair of coprime integers $a, b \geq 1$, the renormalized symmetric function
$$(-1)^{d - \ell(\mu)}\, m^{(a,b)}_\mu(x; q, 1+r)$$
is $e$-positive, meaning that when expanded in the basis $\{e_\lambda(x)\}_{\lambda \vdash d}$ of elementary symmetric functions, all coefficients lie in $\mathbb{N}[q, r]$.

(ii) If $e$-positivity holds, exhibit an explicit combinatorial interpretation of these coefficients as a weighted enumeration of lattice paths (in the style of a $q,t$-statistic on Dyck paths in the $a \times b$ rectangle) that explains the positivity.
category_tag: symmetric functions and rectangular Catalan combinatorics
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published proof or refutation of this specific $e$-positivity conjecture for the renormalized monomial-seed rectangular Catalan symmetric functions specialized at $t = 1+r$. Related rectangular shuffle/Catalan conjectures (e.g., the rational shuffle theorem) have been resolved, but the precise statement here, including the combinatorial-enumeration refinement, does not appear to be settled in available sources.

paper_title: Pulsar Electrodynamics: an unsolved problem
original_question: How can one construct a consistent global model of pulsar electrodynamics for an obliquely rotating neutron star—that is, a self-consistent description of the plasma together with the electromagnetic field across the pulsar magnetosphere and wind—that explains the role of the inductive electric field and displacement current, allows for regions with nonzero parallel electric field (E_parallel ≠ 0), and remains valid despite the lack of corotation and other limitations identified in existing models?
status_search_result: The construction of a fully self-consistent global model for the electrodynamics of an obliquely rotating pulsar magnetosphere and wind remains an open problem. Force-free, MHD, and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of oblique rotators (e.g., Philippov–Spitkovsky and successors, and radiative MHD treatments through 2022–2024) have made substantial progress in modeling global field structure and spin-down, but they rely on idealizations (force-free closure, prescribed pair injection, limited resolution of gaps) and have not produced a complete consistent description that simultaneously resolves the inductive field, displacement current, E_∥ ≠ 0 acceleration regions, and the global circuit without corotation assumptions. No widely accepted pulsar emission mechanism has been established.

paper_title: Syzygies of projective varieties of large degree: recent progress and open problems.
context_brief: sharp vanishing range for Veronese syzygies
original_question: For projective space P^n, integers b and d, and the Veronese syzygy groups K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)), is the non-vanishing range proved in Theorem 2.1 exact? Equivalently, do all groups K_{p,q}(n,b;d) vanish whenever p lies outside the range predicted by that theorem?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n,b,d$ be integers with $n\ge 1$, $b\ge 1$, and $d\ge b+1$. Consider the projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and the line bundles $B=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(b)$ and $L=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(d)$. Let $S=\mathrm{Sym}^\bullet H^0(\mathbb{P}^n,L)$ be the homogeneous coordinate ring of the $d$-uple Veronese embedding, and consider the graded $S$-module
$$M(B;L)=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb{Z}} H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, B\otimes L^{\otimes m}).$$
For integers $p\ge 0$ and $q\ge 0$, let
$$K_{p,q}(n,b;d):=K_{p,q}(\mathbb{P}^n,B;L)$$
denote the Koszul cohomology group computed as the degree-$(p+q)$ component of $\mathrm{Tor}^S_p(M(B;L),\mathbb{C})$ — equivalently, the $(p,q)$-th graded Betti number of the minimal free resolution of $M(B;L)$ over $S$.

For each $1\le q\le n$, define the predicted non-vanishing range $(\ast)_q$ for $p$ to be
$$\binom{d+q}{q}-\binom{d-b-1+q}{q}-q \;\le\; p \;\le\; \binom{d+n}{n}-\binom{d+n-q}{n}\binom{b+q-1}{q-1}-q,$$
and for $q=0$ the range $0\le p\le b$, and for $q=n+1$ a single value (the Castelnuovo–Mumford end), with $K_{p,q}=0$ for $q\ge n+2$ or $q\le -1$.

Question: Is the predicted non-vanishing range exact? That is, prove or disprove: for all $n\ge 1$, all $b\ge 1$, all sufficiently large $d$, and all $0\le q\le n+1$,
$$K_{p,q}(n,b;d)=0 \quad \text{whenever } p \text{ lies outside the range } (\ast)_q.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture that the Ein–Lazarsfeld non-vanishing range for Veronese syzygies $K_{p,q}(n,b;d)$ is sharp (i.e. these groups vanish outside that range) appears to remain open in general. While the asymptotic vanishing conjecture of Ein–Lazarsfeld has been confirmed (asymptotic sharpness), the precise/exact non-vanishing range conjecture is still being investigated through computational evidence and partial results.

original_question: In the asymptotic Boij-Soderberg decomposition for the syzygies under discussion, especially for the coefficients x_i(P^2,B;L_d), can one normalize both the coefficients and the relevant indices i so that, as d tends to infinity, they are sampled values of a smooth function on a dense subset of its domain? The same source notes that one would also like an analogous formulation in dimensions n >= 3, although the appropriate Boij-Soderberg data are then less canonical.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $B$ be a coherent sheaf on $\mathbb{P}^2$ (for instance $B=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}$), and let $L_d = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(d)$. For each sufficiently large $d$, consider the minimal graded free resolution of the section module $\bigoplus_m H^0(\mathbb{P}^2, B \otimes L_d^{\otimes m})$ over the homogeneous coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^2$ embedded by $|L_d|$, and let $\beta_{i,j}(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d)$ denote its graded Betti numbers. The Boij–Söderberg decomposition expresses the Betti table $\beta(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d)$ uniquely as a positive rational combination
$$\beta(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d) \;=\; \sum_{\pi} x_\pi(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d)\,\pi$$
of pure diagrams $\pi$ corresponding to strictly increasing degree sequences. Indexing the relevant pure diagrams by an integer $i$ (running over the homological positions where syzygies occur), let $x_i(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d)$ denote the corresponding Boij–Söderberg coefficients.

Question. Do there exist normalizations
$$\tilde{x}_i(d) \;=\; \alpha(d)\, x_i(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d), \qquad t_i(d) \;=\; \varphi_d(i),$$
of the coefficients and of the indexing variable $i$, with $\varphi_d$ mapping the relevant range of $i$ into a fixed interval $I \subset \mathbb{R}$, such that as $d \to \infty$ the points
$$\bigl\{\bigl(t_i(d),\,\tilde{x}_i(d)\bigr) : i \text{ in the relevant range}\bigr\}$$
form a dense subset of the graph of a smooth function $f \colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ on $I$ (i.e., the discrete data $\tilde{x}_i(d)$ arise as samples $f(t_i(d))$ of a smooth limiting profile)?

Furthermore, formulate and answer the analogous question for $\mathbb{P}^n$ with $n \geq 3$, where one must first specify a canonical choice of Boij–Söderberg data to which the normalization is to be applied.
status_search_result: A web search returns work on asymptotic syzygies (e.g. nonvanishing results, Boij–Söderberg theory for Grassmannians, computational studies of Betti tables on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$) but no source establishing or refuting the existence of a smooth limiting profile for the normalized Boij–Söderberg coefficients $x_i(\mathbb{P}^2,B;L_d)$ as $d\to\infty$. The status appears to remain unresolved in the literature reachable through search.

paper_title: Syzygies of projective varieties of large degree: recent progress and open problems.
original_question: For a smooth projective curve C with gonality gon(C), and for a sufficiently positive line bundle L_d on C, is the Koszul cohomology group K_{p,1}(C,K_C;L_d) nonzero exactly for those p with gon(C) <= p + 1? The source explicitly states this gonality conjecture and then states that it follows from Theorem 4.3, so within this source artifact it is presented as resolved.
self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth complex projective curve of genus $g$, and let $\mathrm{gon}(C)$ denote its gonality, i.e., the minimal degree of a non-constant morphism from $C$ to $\mathbb{P}^1$. Let $K_C$ be the canonical line bundle of $C$, and for $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $L_d$ be a line bundle on $C$ of degree $d$.

For a line bundle $L$ on $C$ and an auxiliary line bundle $B$, the Koszul cohomology group $K_{p,q}(C, B; L)$ is defined as the cohomology in the middle of the complex
$$\wedge^{p+1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + (q-1)L) \to \wedge^p H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + qL) \to \wedge^{p-1} H^0(C,L) \otimes H^0(C, B + (q+1)L).$$

Prove or disprove: there exists an integer $d_0$ (depending on $C$) such that for every line bundle $L_d$ on $C$ with $d \geq d_0$, and for every integer $p \geq 0$,
$$K_{p,1}(C, K_C; L_d) \neq 0 \iff \mathrm{gon}(C) \leq p+1.$$

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories that satisfy the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal, and Moore-Seiberg, or at least prove that such rational conformal field theories exist. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and the minimal models, or prove their existence as rational conformal field theories satisfying those axioms.
self_contained_problem:
Construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories satisfying the geometric/categorical axioms of Kontsevich–Segal and the Moore–Seiberg axioms, or at least prove that such rational conformal field theories exist.

In more detail: a Segal-type two-dimensional conformal field theory is a symmetric monoidal projective functor from the category whose objects are disjoint unions of unit circles and whose morphisms are conformal equivalence classes of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary (composed by sewing) to the category of locally convex topological vector spaces, together with the additional analytic and modular data (modular functor, factorization on sewing of surfaces of all genera, modular invariance of partition and correlation functions, duality and crossing relations) singled out by Moore and Seiberg. A conformal field theory is called rational if the associated space of states decomposes as a finite direct sum of irreducible representations of a pair of commuting chiral algebras and the corresponding modular functor takes values in finite-dimensional vector spaces.

(a) Produce a mathematical construction of a class of such rational conformal field theories satisfying all of these axioms (genus-zero, genus-one, and higher-genus sewing, modular invariance, and the Moore–Seiberg consistency relations), or alternatively give a proof that such theories exist.

(b) In particular, carry this out for the Wess–Zumino–Witten models associated to a simple, simply connected compact Lie group G at every positive integer level k, and for the Virasoro minimal models with central charge c = 1 − 6(p−q)^2/(pq) for coprime integers p, q ≥ 2: construct them, or prove their existence, as rational conformal field theories satisfying the Kontsevich–Segal and Moore–Seiberg axioms.
status_search_result: A long-running program of Y.-Z. Huang has constructed rational closed conformal field theories from representations of vertex operator algebras, including the Wess–Zumino–Novikov–Witten models and the Virasoro minimal models, and has established as theorems many of the key required structures (operator product expansion, modular invariance, Verlinde formula, modular tensor category structure, full rational CFT). However, a higher-genus convergence problem remains, so the full Kontsevich–Segal axiomatization in all genera is not yet completely verified. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Suppose the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has an inner product that is invariant under the conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators. Is the locally convex topological completion obtained by adjoining elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces isomorphic, as a locally convex topological vector space with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form, to the Hilbert-space completion of that graded state space?

Let V be the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory in the sense of two-dimensional conformal field theory, so that V = ⨁_{n} V_{(n)} is a graded vector space equipped with intertwining operators producing the conformal-field correlation maps for genus-zero Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries. Suppose V carries an inner product (a nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form) that is compatible with — i.e. invariant under — the conformal fields constructed from these intertwining operators.

(a) The locally convex topological completion V^{LC} obtained from V by adjoining elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces (i.e. the completion arising from the Kontsevich–Segal-type sewing of higher-genus surfaces, viewed as a locally convex topological vector space with the induced grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form).

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
context_brief: Moduli space of conformal field theories
original_question: Study the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories by giving it topological and geometric structures, and prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in that moduli space.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the collection $\mathcal{M}$ of all (isomorphism classes of) two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs), where a two-dimensional CFT is understood in the standard mathematical sense (e.g., as a unitary full CFT consisting of a pair of vertex operator algebras for the chiral and anti-chiral sectors, together with a modular-invariant torus partition function and a consistent collection of correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus, or equivalently as a Segal-type functor from a category of Riemann surfaces with conformal structure to a category of Hilbert spaces). A CFT is called rational if its chiral algebra is a rational vertex operator algebra, i.e., it has finitely many irreducible modules and its category of modules is a modular tensor category.

(a) Endow $\mathcal{M}$ with a natural topology and a geometric structure (for instance, that of a (possibly infinite-dimensional, stratified) manifold or analytic space) such that continuous deformations of CFTs—e.g., exactly marginal deformations driven by exactly marginal operators—correspond to continuous paths, and such that the central charge and other natural invariants vary continuously.

(b) With respect to such a topology and geometric structure on $\mathcal{M}$, prove that every rational conformal field theory is an isolated point of $\mathcal{M}$, i.e., that no rational CFT admits a nontrivial continuous family of CFT deformations.
status_search_result: The problem of equipping the moduli space of 2D CFTs with topological/geometric structure and proving rational CFTs are isolated points remains open as a general mathematical statement. Partial results and supporting evidence exist: in physics literature it is widely believed that RCFTs are typically isolated (e.g., not dense in CFT moduli spaces of Calabi–Yau sigma models for n>2), and rational points have been studied in specific c=1, c=3/2 examples and via complex-multiplication criteria, but a general topological/geometric framework on the full moduli space and a proof of isolatedness in that setting has not been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra such that V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, and V is C2-cofinite. Is the braided tensor category constructed in the cited work [H8] from [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] rigid?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}V_{(n)}$ be a simple vertex operator algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying:
(1) $V_{(0)}=\mathbb{C}\mathbf{1}$ and $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n<0$, and the contragredient module $V'$ is isomorphic to $V$ as a $V$-module;
(2) $V$ is $C_2$-cofinite, i.e. $\dim V/C_2(V)<\infty$, where $C_2(V)$ is the subspace of $V$ spanned by elements of the form $\operatorname{Res}_x x^{-2}Y(u,x)v$ for $u,v\in V$, with $Y:V\otimes V\to V[[x,x^{-1}]]$ the vertex operator map.

Under these hypotheses, the category of grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules carries a natural braided tensor category structure (the logarithmic vertex tensor category structure of Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang).

Prove or disprove: this braided tensor category is rigid, i.e., every object admits a left and a right dual in the tensor-categorical sense.
category_tag: Vertex operator algebras and tensor categories
status_search_result: The conjecture is established in important special cases but remains open in full generality. Huang proved rigidity (and modularity) when $V$ is additionally rational. McRae has shown rigidity under the additional assumption that the modular $S$-transformation of the character of $V$ is a linear combination of characters of $V$-modules. Recent work (e.g., on $N=1$ super-Virasoro and Virasoro logarithmic minimal models) verifies rigidity in further specific $C_2$-cofinite (non-rational) examples, but no general proof for all simple, self-contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite VOAs is known.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
original_question: If one can construct N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds, then study their representation theory and use it to construct the corresponding N = 2 superconformal field theories, including proofs of the operator product expansion of intertwining operators and of modular invariance, together with the construction of modular tensor categories in a suitable sense and of full N = 2 superconformal field theories.
self_contained_problem:
Assume that for every Calabi–Yau manifold $X$ (a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing first Chern class) one can construct an associated $N=2$ vertex operator superalgebra $V_X$, that is, a $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded vertex operator superalgebra carrying an action of the $N=2$ superconformal algebra of central charge $c = 3\dim_{\mathbb C} X$, whose chiral data encode the geometry of $X$ (for instance via a sigma-model or chiral de Rham–type construction). Carry out the following program for such $V_X$:

1. Develop the representation theory of $V_X$: classify a suitable category of (admissible, grading-restricted, generalized) modules over $V_X$ and describe their fusion rules.

2. For triples of modules, construct the spaces of intertwining operators and prove the convergence and associativity of products of intertwining operators (i.e., the operator product expansion for intertwining operators among $V_X$-modules).

3. Prove modular invariance of the graded characters and, more generally, of the genus-one (pseudo-)trace functions associated to $V_X$-modules, including the action of $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ on the space of conformal blocks on the torus.

4. Using (1)–(3), endow the module category of $V_X$ with the structure of a modular tensor category in an appropriately formulated sense (allowing for the supersymmetric and possibly non-rational, non-finite features inherent in Calabi–Yau models).

5. From this modular tensor category, construct a full $N=2$ superconformal field theory associated to $X$: a consistent assignment of correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of all genera, with a modular-invariant torus partition function and crossing-symmetric sphere correlators, realizing the chiral algebra $V_X$.

Provide the constructions and proofs above, or determine the obstructions that prevent such a program from being carried out for general Calabi–Yau $X$.

Partial progress exists in special cases (e.g., chiral de Rham complex, Gepner/minimal-model constructions, work of Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang on tensor categories for VOAs), but the full problem for general Calabi–Yau targets remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
context_brief: Vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
original_question: Find a direct connection between the representation-theoretic approach via vertex operator algebras and the approach via conformal nets, and prove that at least for rational conformal field theories these two approaches are equivalent.
self_contained_problem:
Two mathematically rigorous frameworks for chiral two-dimensional conformal field theory are:

(1) Vertex operator algebras (VOAs): a vector space V with a vacuum 1, a conformal vector ω, and a state–field correspondence Y(·, z) : V → End(V)[[z, z^{-1}]] satisfying the Jacobi identity and Virasoro relations; together with a category Rep(V) of admissible V-modules, which for a rational (regular) VOA carries the structure of a modular tensor category (Huang's theorem).

(2) Conformal nets: an assignment I ↦ A(I) of von Neumann algebras to proper open intervals I of the unit circle S^1, satisfying isotony, locality, Möbius (or diffeomorphism) covariance, positivity of energy, existence of a vacuum, and the split property; for a completely rational conformal net A, the category Rep(A) of Doplicher–Haag–Roberts representations is a modular tensor category (Kawahigashi–Longo–Müger).

Problem. Construct a direct, canonical correspondence between these two approaches. Concretely: 

(a) Define a natural procedure that to a suitable unitary VOA V associates a conformal net A_V on the Hilbert space completion of V, and conversely a procedure that recovers a VOA from a conformal net satisfying appropriate smoothness conditions, in such a way that the two procedures are mutually inverse on a large class of models.

(b) Show that, when V is a rational (unitary) vertex operator algebra and A_V is the associated conformal net, the modular tensor categories Rep(V) and Rep(A_V) are equivalent as (unitary) modular tensor categories.

Prove that, at least for rational conformal field theories, the VOA-based and conformal-net-based formulations are equivalent in this sense.
category_tag: Vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
status_search_result: Carpi–Kawahigashi–Longo–Weiner (Mem. AMS 254, 2018; arXiv:1503.01260) gave a general procedure assigning a conformal net A_V to every strongly local unitary VOA V, providing a direct connection between the two frameworks. original_question: Let n > 2, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^{n+1}) solve the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, where J_u = ∂u/∂x_1 × ... × ∂u/∂x_n is the vector of n x n minors of Du. Must every such weak solution be continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n>2$ and let $B^n\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Let $H:\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a bounded Lipschitz function. For a map $u=(u^1,\dots,u^{n+1})\in W^{1,n}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$, define the vector of $n\times n$ minors of the differential $Du$ by
$$J_u \;=\; \frac{\partial u}{\partial x_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_n}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{n+1},$$
i.e. the $i$-th component of $J_u$ is $(-1)^{i-1}\det\bigl(\partial_{x_1}\widehat{u^i},\dots,\partial_{x_n}\widehat{u^i}\bigr)$, where $\widehat{u^i}$ denotes the $n$-tuple of components of $u$ with the $i$-th component omitted. Consider weak solutions $u\in W^{1,n}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ of the $n$-dimensional $H$-system
$$-\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u\bigr) \;=\; H(u)\,J_u\qquad\text{in } B^n,$$
in the sense that
$$\int_{B^n}|\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u:\nabla\varphi\,dx \;=\; \int_{B^n} H(u)\,J_u\cdot\varphi\,dx\qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B^n,\mathbb{R}^{n+1}).$$
Question: Must every such weak solution $u$ be continuous on $B^n$?
status_search_result: The continuity of arbitrary weak $W^{1,n}$ solutions of the $n$-dimensional $H$-system with bounded Lipschitz $H$ in dimension $n>2$ is regarded as an open regularity problem. Continuity (and Hölder regularity) is known under additional hypotheses, e.g. when the gradient lies in the Lorentz space $L^{n,2}$ or when $|\nabla u|^{n/2}$ is square integrable, but no proof is available for general $W^{1,n}$ weak solutions. The $n=2$ case (classical $H$-surface equation) is by contrast known to give continuous solutions.

context_brief: Endpoint Lorentz estimate for Riesz transforms
original_question: Let R = (R_1, ..., R_n) be the vectorial Riesz transform. Is the endpoint Lorentz-space estimate ||f||_{L^{(p,∞)}}^{p-1} <= C ||Σ_{α=1}^n R_α(|Rf|^{p-2} R_α f)||_{L^{(p',∞)}} valid?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $R=(R_1,\dots,R_n)$ denote the vector-valued Riesz transform on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where each component is the Calderón–Zygmund operator
\[
R_\alpha f(x) = c_n \,\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{x_\alpha-y_\alpha}{|x-y|^{n+1}}\,f(y)\,dy,\qquad \alpha=1,\dots,n,
\]
with the standard normalizing constant $c_n$. For a measurable function $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $1\le q<\infty$, let $\|g\|_{L^{(q,\infty)}}$ denote the weak-$L^q$ (Lorentz) quasinorm
\[
\|g\|_{L^{(q,\infty)}} = \sup_{\lambda>0} \lambda \,\bigl|\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:|g(x)|>\lambda\}\bigr|^{1/q}.
\]
Fix $1<p<\infty$ and let $p'=p/(p-1)$. Set $|Rf|=\bigl(\sum_{\alpha=1}^n |R_\alpha f|^2\bigr)^{1/2}$.

Question: Does there exist a constant $C=C(n,p)>0$ such that, for every Schwartz function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
\[
\|f\|_{L^{(p,\infty)}}^{\,p-1} \;\le\; C\,\Bigl\|\sum_{\alpha=1}^n R_\alpha\!\bigl(|Rf|^{p-2}\,R_\alpha f\bigr)\Bigr\|_{L^{(p',\infty)}} ?
\]
Determine whether this endpoint Lorentz-space inequality holds or fails.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution (positive or negative) of this specific weak-type Lorentz endpoint inequality involving the nonlinear expression $\sum_\alpha R_\alpha(|Rf|^{p-2} R_\alpha f)$. Related work treats endpoint and weak-type bounds for Riesz transforms in various settings, but none directly addresses this formulation, so the status appears to be unknown based on available evidence.

original_question: Let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B, R^m) solve -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u, where Ω takes values in so(m) ⊗ R^n and belongs to the Lorentz space L^{(n,p)}. For which p in [1, n] does this guarantee that u is continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, $m \geq 1$, and let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the open unit ball. Consider a map $u \in W^{1,n}(B,\mathbb{R}^m)$ that is a weak solution of the critical $n$-Laplace system
$$-\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u\bigr) \;=\; \Omega \cdot |\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u \qquad \text{in } B,$$
where the potential $\Omega = (\Omega^i_j)_{i,j=1}^m$ takes values in $\mathfrak{so}(m) \otimes \mathbb{R}^n$ (so $\Omega^i_j = -\Omega^j_i$ are $\mathbb{R}^n$-valued $1$-forms), and the right-hand side is interpreted componentwise as $\sum_{j=1}^m \Omega^i_j \cdot |\nabla u|^{n-2}\nabla u^j$. Assume in addition that each component $\Omega^i_j$ belongs to the Lorentz space $L^{(n,p)}(B,\mathbb{R}^n)$ for some $p \in [1,n]$, where $L^{(n,p)}$ denotes the Lorentz space of pairs $(n,p)$ with the standard quasinorm
$$\|f\|_{L^{(n,p)}} = \left(\int_0^\infty \bigl(t^{1/n} f^*(t)\bigr)^p \frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/p}, \quad 1 \leq p < \infty,$$
and $L^{(n,\infty)}$ defined as weak-$L^n$ (with $L^{(n,n)} = L^n$).

Determine the set of values $p \in [1,n]$ for which the above assumption $\Omega \in L^{(n,p)}$ guarantees that every such weak solution $u$ is continuous in $B$.
status_search_result: Martino and Schikorra (Math. Ann. 2024, arXiv:2305.05961) established continuity of solutions to n-Laplace systems with antisymmetric potential under a Lorentz-space assumption on Ω, and as a corollary obtained continuity of critical n-harmonic maps into manifolds under the assumption ∇u ∈ L^(n,2) — described as the weakest assumption to date. This represents a substantial advance, but a complete characterization of all p ∈ [1,n] for which L^(n,p)-integrability of Ω forces continuity does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature.

paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
original_question: For the quartic polynomial x^2(x-y)(x-z) + y^2(y-x)(y-z) + z^2(z-x)(z-y), which is nonnegative for all real x, y, z and falls into Hilbert's exceptional three-variable degree-four sum-of-squares case, find an explicit representation of this polynomial as a sum of squares of real polynomials.
self_contained_problem:
Hilbert proved that every nonnegative homogeneous polynomial in three variables of degree four with real coefficients can be written as a sum of squares of real polynomials. Consider the ternary quartic
\[
P(x,y,z) \;=\; x^{2}(x-y)(x-z) + y^{2}(y-x)(y-z) + z^{2}(z-x)(z-y),
\]
which is nonnegative for all real $x,y,z$ (this is Schur's inequality with exponent $2$). Find an explicit representation of $P(x,y,z)$ as a sum of squares of real polynomials in $x,y,z$.
status_search_result: An explicit sum-of-squares representation of the Schur quartic is known and elementary; the problem of producing such a representation has been resolved. Standard derivations rearrange the symmetric expression into a manifest sum of squares of polynomials, consistent with Hilbert's theorem on ternary quartics.

paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
original_question: Within the same one-quarter-class setting for orthogonal polynomial sequences, are there examples other than the Meixner polynomials of the second kind (the Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials) whose orthogonality measure has spectrum extending over the entire real line, corresponding to the case σ = -∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{P_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a monic orthogonal polynomial sequence on the real line, defined by the three-term recurrence
$$P_{n+1}(x) = (x-\beta_n)P_n(x) - \gamma_n P_{n-1}(x), \qquad n\ge 0,$$
with $P_{-1}(x)=0$, $P_0(x)=1$, real $\beta_n$, and $\gamma_n>0$ for all $n\ge 1$. Assume the sequence belongs to the so-called one-quarter class in the sense of Chihara, namely
$$\beta_n \to \infty, \qquad \gamma_n \to \infty, \qquad \frac{\gamma_n}{\beta_{n-1}\beta_n} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{4} \qquad (n\to\infty).$$
For such a sequence, define
$$\sigma \;=\; \liminf_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\beta_n - 2\sqrt{\gamma_n}\bigr) \;\in\;[-\infty,\infty),$$
which controls the spectrum of the (unique, when the moment problem is determinate) orthogonality measure $\mu$: the true interval of orthogonality is contained in $[\sigma,\infty)$, and the case $\sigma=-\infty$ corresponds to $\mu$ having spectrum extending over the entire real line.

A known instance with $\sigma=-\infty$ is provided by the Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials (the Meixner polynomials of the second kind), whose orthogonality measure is supported on all of $\mathbb{R}$.

Problem. Exhibit (or prove the non-existence of) a monic orthogonal polynomial sequence in the one-quarter class above, other than the Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials, for which $\sigma=-\infty$, i.e., whose orthogonality measure has spectrum equal to the whole real line.
status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem at the OPSFA13 open problems session (2015) and recorded in the corresponding 2016 SIGMA report. No subsequent literature found in the search identifies additional examples of one-quarter-class orthogonal polynomial sequences with full-real-line spectrum beyond the Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials, nor a proof of non-existence. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
original_question: Develop a systematic method for simplifying multiple hypergeometric summations and iterated-integral-derived sums to lower-order sums, ideally to single-sum or other recognizably closed forms when such reductions exist, using a combination of algorithmic tools such as holonomic-systems or difference-field methods together with whatever structural insight is needed to identify the correct reduced form.
self_contained_problem:
A multiple hypergeometric sum is a finite or infinite sum of the form
\[ S(n) \;=\; \sum_{k_1,\,k_2,\,\dots,\,k_r} F(n,k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r), \]
where the summand $F$ is a proper hypergeometric term, meaning that the ratios $F(\dots,k_i+1,\dots)/F(\dots,k_i,\dots)$ and $F(n+1,\dots)/F(n,\dots)$ are rational functions of all variables, and where the summand may also involve products and quotients of Pochhammer symbols, factorials, and binomial coefficients, including those that arise naturally from iterated integral representations such as connection-coefficient computations between families of orthogonal polynomials.

Develop a systematic algorithmic procedure that takes as input such a multi-index hypergeometric sum $S(n)$ and produces, when one exists, an equivalent expression of strictly lower nesting depth: ideally a single sum, or, when possible, a closed form expressible in terms of standard hypergeometric functions ${}_pF_q$, gamma functions, or similar recognized special functions. The procedure should:

(i) decide, in a constructive sense, whether such a reduction to lower-order summation exists;
(ii) when reduction exists, output an explicit lower-order representation;
(iii) combine algorithmic tools available for this setting, including holonomic-systems methods (creative telescoping, $\partial$-finite closure properties, Zeilberger-type algorithms in several variables) and difference-field methods (Karr's algorithm and its $\Pi\Sigma^*$-extensions), with whatever additional structural input (such as integral representations, contiguous relations, or symmetry of the summand) is required to identify the correct reduced form.

In particular, characterize a class of multiple hypergeometric sums for which a reduction to a single sum is guaranteed to be effectively computable, and provide an algorithm whose output on this class is a single-sum or closed-form representation of $S(n)$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open problem area rather than a specific conjecture. While substantial algorithmic progress exists (Wilf–Zeilberger theory, Chyzak's holonomic-systems package, Schneider's Sigma package implementing difference-field methods, Koutschan's HolonomicFunctions), no fully systematic, complete procedure for reducing arbitrary multiple hypergeometric summations to lower-order or closed forms is known. Recent surveys and software developments continue to extend, but not close, this problem area.

paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
original_question: Does there exist, for general invariant random-matrix ensembles, a corresponding Wigner-like family having the same limiting spectral density, analogous to the way Wigner ensembles correspond to Gaussian Unitary Ensembles and Wishart ensembles correspond to Laguerre Unitary Ensembles?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. For a continuous "potential" function V: ℝ → ℝ growing sufficiently fast at infinity, the associated unitary invariant random matrix ensemble of size N consists of N×N Hermitian matrices M endowed with the probability density

  P_V(M) dM = (1/Z_N) exp(-N tr V(M)) dM,

where dM is Lebesgue measure on Hermitian matrices and Z_N is a normalizing constant. Under standard hypotheses, the empirical spectral distribution (1/N) Σ_{i=1}^N δ_{λ_i(M)} converges weakly almost surely as N → ∞ to a deterministic compactly supported probability measure μ_V on ℝ, called the limiting spectral density of the ensemble.

Two classical situations are well understood:

(a) When V(x) = x²/2 (the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble, GUE), μ_V is the Wigner semicircle law. The corresponding "Wigner family" consists of N×N Hermitian random matrices W_N = (W_{ij}) with independent entries (modulo the Hermitian constraint) having mean 0 and variance 1/N (with appropriate moment conditions); the empirical spectral distribution of any such Wigner matrix converges to the same semicircle law as the GUE.

(b) When V is the Laguerre potential (the Laguerre Unitary Ensemble, LUE), μ_V is the Marchenko–Pastur law. The corresponding "Wishart family" consists of sample covariance matrices X_N X_N^* / N where X_N has independent entries with prescribed mean and variance; their empirical spectral distributions converge to the same Marchenko–Pastur law.

In each of these examples, an "invariant" ensemble (defined by a density invariant under unitary conjugation) is matched by a "Wigner-like" family (defined by independence of entries, without requiring unitary invariance) producing the same limiting spectral density.

Question. Does this correspondence extend to general unitary invariant ensembles? Precisely: for every sufficiently regular potential V, does there exist a family of N×N Hermitian random matrices, defined by independence (or suitable weak dependence) of their entries together with explicit moment/distributional conditions, whose empirical spectral distribution converges almost surely as N → ∞ to the same limiting measure μ_V as the invariant ensemble with density proportional to exp(-N tr V(M))? If so, describe such a "Wigner-like" construction; if not, characterize the obstruction.
status_search_result: Web searches indicate that Wigner-type constructions matching invariant ensembles are known only for special potentials (quadratic→semicircle/GUE, Laguerre→Marchenko-Pastur/LUE, and a few related cases), and that families of independent-entry matrices with variance profiles or correlated entries can produce broad classes of limiting laws. However, no source was found establishing or refuting a general correspondence between arbitrary invariant ensembles and Wigner-like (independent-entry) families with the same limiting spectral density. The status appears unresolved in full generality.

paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
original_question: Define polynomials Ã_n(t) by the recurrence (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)Ã_{n-1}(t) + (2n+1)nÃ_n(t) - (n+1)^2 nÃ_{n+1}(t) = 0 and suppose they are the partial sums Ã_n(t) = Σ_{k=0}^n A_k(t) arising from the related recurrence for A_n(t). Can one deduce directly from this recurrence that lim_{n→∞} Ã_n(t) = ∏_{j=1}^∞ (1 + t^3/(8j^3))?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{A_n(t)\}_{n\geq 0}$ be a sequence of polynomials, and define the partial sums
$$\tilde A_n(t) = \sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t).$$
Suppose that the polynomials $\tilde A_n(t)$ satisfy the three-term recurrence
$$\bigl(n^3 - (-1)^n t^3\bigr)\,\tilde A_{n-1}(t) + (2n+1)\,n\,\tilde A_n(t) - (n+1)^2\,n\,\tilde A_{n+1}(t) = 0, \qquad n \geq 1,$$
together with initial conditions ensuring $\tilde A_0(t) = 1$ and $\tilde A_1(t) = 1 + t^3/8$. It is known that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \tilde A_n(t) = \prod_{j=1}^{\infty}\left(1 + \frac{t^3}{8 j^3}\right).$$
Provide a direct proof of this limit identity that uses only the recurrence relation above (and the initial data) for the polynomials $\tilde A_n(t)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the OPSFA13 open-problems collection (SIGMA 12 (2016), 071). A targeted web search did not surface a follow-up paper providing a recurrence-based proof of the stated limit, so the current status could not be verified.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For tree-level string cosmologies containing Ramond-Ramond fields, what are the asymptotic properties of the resulting universes, are the known solutions stable and unique, and do there exist solutions that appear only subdominantly in the asymptotic regime in a way that constrains the allowed singular asymptotic states?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the tree-level low-energy effective action of a closed string theory in (d+1)-dimensional spacetime, containing the spacetime metric g_{μν}, the dilaton φ, and a Ramond–Ramond p-form gauge potential A_p with field strength F_{p+1} = dA_p, with action (in the string frame)

  S = ∫ d^{d+1}x √(−g) [ e^{−2φ}(R + 4(∂φ)^2) − (1/2·(p+1)!) F_{p+1}^2 ].

Restrict to spatially homogeneous, anisotropic Bianchi-type cosmological ansätze of the form
  ds^2 = −dt^2 + Σ_{i=1}^{d} a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2,  φ = φ(t),
with a compatible homogeneous Ramond–Ramond field-strength configuration, and study the resulting autonomous system of ordinary differential equations for the logarithmic scale factors β_i = ln a_i, the dilaton φ, and the RR field-strength components.

(a) Determine the complete set of asymptotic regimes (as t approaches the cosmological singularity and as t → ∞) for the trajectories of this dynamical system. In particular, classify all asymptotic states and the corresponding Kasner-like exponents (p_1, …, p_d) that can be approached.

(b) For each known exact cosmological solution of the above system with non-trivial RR flux, determine whether the solution is asymptotically stable (i.e. an attractor on an open set of initial data) and whether it is asymptotically unique within its class.

(c) Identify and classify all asymptotic solutions that are subdominant — solutions that exist as exact trajectories of the system but whose contributions are exponentially or polynomially suppressed relative to the dominant asymptotic state — and determine the constraints these subdominant solutions impose on the spectrum of admissible singular asymptotic states.
status_search_result: Recent work on asymptotic scalar field cosmology in string theory (e.g., Rudelius 2022) addresses asymptotic late-time behavior of string-derived cosmologies with exponential potentials, but a complete classification of asymptotic regimes, stability, uniqueness, and subdominant solutions for tree-level cosmologies including Ramond–Ramond fields does not appear to have been fully established. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory and Horava-Witten cosmology with nontrivial Ramond fields, what is their full asymptotic significance, and what is the dimension of the asymptotic attractor formed by these solutions under perturbation of the basic regimes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the cosmological dynamical systems arising from heterotic M-theory and from Hořava–Witten theory compactified on an interval, in the presence of nontrivial Ramond (form) field strengths. After dimensional reduction to a homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type or spatially flat FRW) cosmological ansatz with metric moduli (scale factors of the external space, the Calabi–Yau volume modulus, and the orbifold-interval modulus) coupled to dilaton/axion fields and to the Ramond form-field fluxes, one obtains an autonomous system of ordinary differential equations governing the time evolution of these moduli. Within this system there exist explicit exact cosmological solutions (the "basic regimes") parametrized by the flux data.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
context_brief: Genericity in string and M-theory cosmology
original_question: For the stable solutions obtained in the preceding string and M-theory asymptotic problems, what do full inhomogeneous generic perturbations look like, and what features must a generic analytic cosmological solution share with those stable solutions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the low-energy effective field equations of string and M-theory compactified to four spacetime dimensions, with bosonic content consisting of the spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, the dilaton $\phi$, and form-field strengths (e.g. an axion or NS–NS three-form $H$). Within this setting, suppose one has identified a class of spatially homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type) cosmological solutions that are asymptotically stable, in the sense that small homogeneous perturbations of initial data on a Cauchy surface decay (or remain bounded) toward the cosmological singularity or toward future infinity.

Address the following:

1. Extend the stability analysis of these homogeneous solutions to fully inhomogeneous perturbations of the metric, dilaton, and form fields. Determine the asymptotic form of a generic inhomogeneous perturbation, including its dependence on spatial coordinates, in the chosen asymptotic regime (singularity or infinity).

2. Characterize, for the real-analytic category, the universal features that any generic analytic cosmological solution to the same field equations must share with these stable homogeneous solutions. Concretely, identify the leading asymptotic behaviour (e.g. Kasner-like exponents, scaling of the dilaton, decay or growth of form fields), the number of free functions of the spatial coordinates parametrizing the generic solution, and any constraints these free functions must satisfy.

3. Determine whether the generic analytic solution is BKL-like (governed pointwise by a homogeneous model) or, on the contrary, exhibits genuinely inhomogeneous asymptotic structure not captured by any homogeneous truncation.
status_search_result: A targeted search returns related work on inhomogeneous string cosmologies, BKL-type analyses, and stability of homogeneous string/M-theory backgrounds, but no result establishing the generic inhomogeneous asymptotic profile of perturbations around the relevant stable homogeneous string/M-theory solutions, nor a complete characterization of the features shared by a generic analytic cosmological solution. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: In the basic string effective theory with quantum corrections, which asymptotic solutions remain stable when a general fluid with equation of state parameter left arbitrary is coupled to the dilaton, despite the strong nonlinearities of the field equations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the tree-level string effective action in $D=4$ spacetime dimensions, written in the string frame as
$$S = -\tfrac{1}{2\lambda_s^{D-2}}\int d^D x\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\bigl(R + (\nabla\phi)^2 + V(\phi)\bigr) + S_{\text{matter}},$$
where $\phi$ is the dilaton, $V(\phi)$ is a (possibly vanishing) dilaton potential, and $S_{\text{matter}}$ describes a perfect fluid coupled to the dilaton with energy density $\rho$, pressure $p=\gamma\rho$, and equation-of-state parameter $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ left arbitrary. Allow generic higher-curvature/$\alpha'$ quantum corrections of the form
$$\Delta S = \tfrac{1}{2\lambda_s^{D-2}}\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\bigl[\alpha'\,c_1 R_{GB}^2 + \alpha'\,c_2(\nabla\phi)^4 + \cdots\bigr],$$
involving the Gauss–Bonnet term and dilaton kinetic corrections, with coefficients $c_i$ allowed in the standard string-theoretic range.

Restrict to spatially flat, homogeneous, isotropic cosmologies with metric $ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2\,d\mathbf{x}^2$, dilaton $\phi=\phi(t)$, and fluid variables depending only on $t$, satisfying the resulting nonlinear field equations together with the fluid conservation law $\dot\rho + DH(1+\gamma)\rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\dot\phi(1-D\gamma)\rho = 0$ (or the analogous covariant equation when the dilaton couples to matter).

Determine, as a function of the fluid parameter $\gamma$, all asymptotic solutions $(a(t),\phi(t),\rho(t))$ as $t\to\pm\infty$ that are stable (in the sense of late- or early-time attractors of the dynamical system obtained from the equations of motion). Equivalently, classify the stable fixed points and asymptotic regimes of the corresponding cosmological dynamical system over the full range of $\gamma$, in the presence of the quantum/$\alpha'$ corrections.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a complete classification of stable asymptotic solutions of the quantum-corrected string cosmology with a general fluid parameter coupled to the dilaton. Partial results exist for special values of $\gamma$ (radiation, dust, stiff matter) and for specific correction schemes, but the full classification across arbitrary $\gamma$ with general higher-curvature corrections appears to remain open due to the nonlinearity of the field equations.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: In curved string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections and interacting fluids, what asymptotic behavior is produced by dominant versus subdominant curvature contributions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially curved Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) cosmology with metric

  ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 [ dr^2/(1 - k r^2) + r^2 (dθ^2 + sin^2θ dφ^2) ],   k ∈ {-1, 0, +1},

coupled to a dilaton field φ(t) and to a system of N interacting perfect fluids with energy densities ρ_i(t) and pressures p_i(t) = (γ_i - 1) ρ_i(t), i = 1, …, N, satisfying coupled conservation laws

  ρ̇_i + 3 H γ_i ρ_i = Q_i(ρ_1, …, ρ_N),     ∑_{i=1}^N Q_i = 0,

where H = ȧ/a is the Hubble rate and the interaction terms Q_i are smooth functions of the densities.

Take the low-energy effective string-frame action with leading α'-correction,

  S = ∫ d^4x √(-g) e^{-φ} [ R + (∇φ)^2 - V(φ) - α' c_1 R_GB^2 + … ] + S_matter,

where R_GB^2 = R^2 - 4 R_{μν} R^{μν} + R_{μνρσ} R^{μνρσ} is the Gauss–Bonnet term, c_1 is a constant, and α' > 0 is the string tension parameter. The resulting field equations form an autonomous dynamical system in the variables (H, φ̇, ρ_1, …, ρ_N) on which the spatial curvature term k/a^2 and the α'-correction enter as additional contributions.

Problem. Classify the asymptotic behavior, as t → +∞ and as t approaches any finite-time singularity, of all solutions of this system in terms of which contribution among
 (a) the spatial curvature term k/a^2,
 (b) the leading α' (Gauss–Bonnet) curvature correction, and
 (c) the interacting-fluid sector
is dominant and which is subdominant. In particular, determine, for every choice of k ∈ {-1, 0, +1}, of the barotropic indices γ_i, and of the interaction structure {Q_i}, the possible scaling exponents and stability properties of the asymptotic regimes that arise when the dominant contribution is the curvature term, the α'-correction, or the fluid sector, and identify the corrections induced by the subdominant terms.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this classification problem for curved interacting string cosmologies with higher-order curvature corrections was located. The problem is posed as an open research direction and no comprehensive answer appears in the literature.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: Are the deformed power-law cosmological solutions of M-theory asymptotically stable, and does that stability support the naturalness of inflation in M-theory cosmology?
self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory) with bosonic field content consisting of a Lorentzian metric g on an 11-manifold and a 3-form gauge potential A with 4-form field strength F = dA, governed by the action

  S = (1/2κ²) ∫ d¹¹x √(−g) [ R − (1/2)|F|² ] − (1/12κ²) ∫ A ∧ F ∧ F,

augmented by the leading higher-curvature/quantum correction terms (schematically, an R⁴-type eight-derivative contribution together with its supersymmetric completion). On a spatially homogeneous Bianchi-type or product-of-flat-factors ansatz, the uncorrected theory admits "power-law" cosmological solutions in which each spatial scale factor evolves as a power of cosmic time t, supported by a suitable flux configuration; turning on the higher-derivative corrections produces a one-parameter family of "deformed power-law" cosmological solutions of the corrected equations of motion.

Question: Are these deformed power-law cosmological solutions of corrected eleven-dimensional supergravity asymptotically stable as t → ∞ under small homogeneous (and, more generally, inhomogeneous) perturbations of the metric and 4-form flux? In particular, does the basin of attraction include an open neighborhood of generic initial data, so that a phase of accelerated expansion (inflation) arising from such a solution is dynamically natural in M-theory cosmology?
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a definitive proof or disproof of asymptotic stability for the deformed power-law cosmological solutions of higher-derivative-corrected eleven-dimensional supergravity. Partial stability analyses of related M-theory cosmological backgrounds exist, but no comprehensive resolution of the naturalness-of-inflation question in this setting was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For Robertson-Walker branes with a perfect fluid in the bulk or brane description, can one find a regular bulk solution that both localizes gravity on the brane and satisfies the null energy condition in the bulk, despite the obstruction already known for single-fluid models?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a five-dimensional bulk spacetime containing a codimension-one Robertson–Walker brane, with a perfect fluid energy–momentum tensor specified either in the bulk or induced on the brane. The bulk metric is taken to be regular (no curvature singularities or pathologies in the bulk geometry, away from the brane), and the induced geometry on the brane is a spatially homogeneous and isotropic Robertson–Walker spacetime. Two further requirements are imposed:

(i) Localization of gravity on the brane, i.e., the existence of a normalizable zero-mode of the linearized graviton fluctuations bound to the brane, reproducing four-dimensional Newtonian gravity at large distances on the brane.

(ii) The null energy condition in the bulk: T_{AB} k^A k^B \ge 0 for every null vector k^A, where T_{AB} is the bulk stress–energy tensor.

It is known that for a single perfect fluid in the bulk these three demands (regular bulk, gravity localization, and bulk null energy condition) cannot be simultaneously satisfied. The question is: does there exist a Robertson–Walker brane configuration sourced by a perfect fluid (in the bulk or on the brane) that admits a regular bulk solution while simultaneously localizing gravity on the brane and satisfying the null energy condition throughout the bulk?
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published resolution of this question for Robertson–Walker branes with perfect-fluid sources beyond the known no-go for single fluids; the problem appears to remain open in the braneworld-cosmology literature.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: Are the asymptotic brane solutions obtained in the Robertson-Walker braneworld problems stable under general inhomogeneous perturbations, and what does function counting imply about the degree of generality of the regular and singular asymptotic behaviors that are found?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a five-dimensional braneworld model in which the bulk spacetime contains a four-dimensional brane whose induced geometry is of Robertson–Walker (spatially homogeneous and isotropic) type. Suppose that, near a distinguished value of the extra-dimensional coordinate (taken either at a finite location or asymptotically far from the brane), one has classified the leading-order asymptotic forms of the metric and matter fields that solve the coupled bulk–brane Einstein equations under the homogeneity and isotropy assumption, obtaining a finite collection of formal asymptotic families (some regular, some singular).

(a) Carry out a linear perturbation analysis around each such asymptotic family in which the perturbations are allowed to depend on all five spacetime coordinates (i.e., general inhomogeneous and anisotropic perturbations, not restricted to preserve the Robertson–Walker symmetry). Determine, for each family, whether the perturbation modes remain bounded (in a suitable norm) as one approaches the distinguished coordinate value, and hence decide which asymptotic families are stable and which are unstable under such generic perturbations.

(b) For each asymptotic family, perform a function-counting argument: count the number of independent arbitrary functions of the appropriate number of variables that parametrize the general solution of the linearized system whose leading behavior matches that family, and compare with the maximum number of arbitrary functions allowed by the full nonlinear system (after gauge fixing). Conclude from this counting which of the asymptotic families are general (depending on the maximal number of free functions and thus representing the generic behavior) and which are non-generic (of measure zero in the space of solutions).
status_search_result: No specific publication establishing a complete genericity and stability classification of Robertson–Walker braneworld asymptotic solutions under general inhomogeneous perturbations via function counting was located. The problem appears to remain a research direction in string cosmology rather than a settled result.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: In the Ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios in M-theory, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable when the higher-order terms enter the evolution dominantly rather than subdominantly, and what does that reveal about ekpyrosis and the broader structure of M-theory cosmology?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the heterotic M-theory effective description of the Ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios, modeled by two boundary three-branes separated by an interval in an eleven-dimensional bulk. Working in the moduli-space approximation, the low-energy dynamics is governed by a four-dimensional effective action for the scale factor a(t) of the spatial sections together with the radion (inter-brane separation) modulus φ(t) and the Calabi–Yau volume modulus, supplemented by curvature corrections that arise as higher-order (in α' and in derivatives) terms beyond the leading two-derivative Einstein–scalar truncation.

A distinguished homogeneous, spatially flat solution of the leading-order equations is the Milne state: the brane configuration corresponding to a vanishing inter-brane velocity at past infinity with the four-dimensional metric tending to the flat Milne form ds² = −dt² + t² dx² as t → −∞ (equivalently, the empty Minkowski wedge realized as the past attractor of the moduli-space dynamics).

Now suppose that, in the regime of interest, the higher-order curvature/derivative corrections are not subdominant perturbations of the leading dynamics but instead enter the evolution equations dominantly, so that they govern the leading asymptotic behavior of the moduli (a, φ, …) as t → −∞.

Question. In this regime where the higher-order terms are asymptotically dominant, is the Milne state a globally asymptotically stable past attractor of the resulting moduli-space dynamical system? That is, do all initial data in an open neighborhood — and ideally in the full physically admissible phase space — of the Milne state evolve so that (a, φ, …) converge to the Milne configuration as t → −∞, with no other attracting solutions or runaway trajectories arising from the dominant higher-order corrections?
status_search_result: Web searches do not turn up a rigorous proof or disproof of global asymptotic stability of the Milne state in the regime where higher-order curvature/derivative corrections dominate the evolution in heterotic M-theory ekpyrotic/cyclic models. Existing dynamical-systems analyses of ekpyrotic scenarios discuss stability of various critical points and the role of higher-derivative stabilizing terms, but no source establishes the global asymptotic stability question with dominant higher-order terms. The problem appears to remain open.
