paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: What precise relation, if any, does the ambient cosmological construction have to twistor theory, especially to the null projective twistor 5-space PN and related H-space constructions, and how should one understand the validity of the asymptotic condition and the meaning of non-locality in the ambient 5-space?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the ambient cosmological construction in which a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M^4,g)$ is embedded as a hypersurface in a five-dimensional ambient space $(\widetilde{M}^5,\widetilde{g})$ carrying a perfect-fluid stress-energy content (rather than a pure cosmological constant $\Lambda$), with the embedding compatible with the conformal structure of $M^4$ at conformal infinity. On the twistor side, let $\mathbb{T}\cong\mathbb{C}^4$ denote twistor space equipped with the Hermitian form $\Sigma$ of signature $(2,2)$, and let $PN\subset P\mathbb{T}$ denote the null projective twistor 5-space, i.e., the real five-dimensional hypersurface of projective twistors $[Z]$ with $\Sigma(Z,Z)=0$, which is the space of null geodesics of conformally compactified Minkowski space. Recall further the nonlinear graviton / $\mathcal H$-space construction associating to suitable asymptotically flat (or self-dual) data a complex four-manifold of $\alpha$-planes.

(a) Determine whether there exists a canonical correspondence between the ambient 5-space $\widetilde{M}^5$ and $PN$ (or an appropriate deformation/$\mathcal H$-space generalization thereof) that intertwines the ambient fluid data with twistorial data, and if so describe this correspondence explicitly.

(b) Formulate and prove a precise asymptotic condition on $\widetilde{M}^5$ — replacing the cosmological-constant asymptotic conditions used in the $\Lambda$-case — under which the perfect-fluid ambient construction is well-posed and compatible with the proposed twistor correspondence.

(c) Give a precise mathematical meaning to "non-locality" of fields and observables on the ambient 5-space $\widetilde{M}^5$, and characterize how this non-locality is encoded on the twistor side (for example, via cohomological or contour-integral representations on $PN$ or its $\mathcal H$-space analogue).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a review of open problems in string cosmology, with the relation between the ambient 5-space construction with a perfect fluid and twistor theory (in particular $PN$ and $\mathcal H$-space) explicitly noted as unclear. No subsequent work establishing such a correspondence or formulating the asymptotic condition and non-locality in this setting has been located.

paper_title: Multi-D magnetohydrodynamic modelling of pulsar wind nebulae: recent progress and open questions
original_question: For young energetic pulsars whose magnetospheres create electron-positron pairs in cascades, what is the actual pair multiplicity κ, how does it depend on pulsar parameters, and can modeling of pulsar wind nebulae constrain κ tightly enough to determine whether any ion component of the wind can be energetically important?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a young, energetic rotation-powered pulsar whose magnetosphere accelerates primary electrons that initiate electromagnetic cascades, producing electron–positron pairs. Define the pair multiplicity κ to be the average number of pairs produced per primary electron extracted from the stellar surface, so that the relativistic magnetized wind launched by the pulsar is composed mostly of pairs together with a possible ionic component (with ion-to-electron mass ratio m_i/m_e ≈ 1836). Theoretical cascade models suggest 10^3 ≲ κ ≲ 10^7 for young energetic pulsars.

(a) Determine κ as a function of fundamental pulsar parameters (e.g. spin period P, period derivative Ṗ, surface magnetic field B, magnetic inclination angle, and curvature radius of magnetic field lines), based on a self-consistent model of polar-cap pair cascades.

(b) Using multi-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic modelling of the resulting pulsar wind nebula (the synchrotron-emitting bubble inflated by the pulsar wind into the surrounding medium) compared with multi-wavelength observations, derive constraints on κ that are tight enough to decide whether the inequality κ < m_i/m_e ≈ 10^3–10^4 can hold, in which case an ionic component, although numerically negligible, would carry an energetically dominant fraction of the wind power.
category_tag: pulsar wind nebulae and pair cascades
status_search_result: Pair multiplicity in young pulsar magnetospheres remains an active area of investigation. Theoretical cascade work (Timokhin & Harding 2015, 2019) bounds the maximum multiplicity at a few × 10^5 with weak dependence on B and curvature radius, while a 2025 A&A study used H.E.S.S. and LHAASO PWN observations to derive lower limits on κ for several young pulsars. No tight, generally accepted determination of κ has been established, and the question of whether an ion component can be energetically dominant remains unresolved.

paper_title: Multi-D magnetohydrodynamic modelling of pulsar wind nebulae: recent progress and open questions
context_brief: particle acceleration mechanisms at the termination shock
original_question: In the Crab Nebula, which acceleration mechanism or combination of mechanisms, and which locations along the wind termination shock, produce the observed broken particle spectrum, with low-energy radio-emitting particles having a flat injected slope and higher-energy particles having a steeper slope, given that driven magnetic reconnection, diffusive shock acceleration, and resonant ion-cyclotron absorption require different magnetization, striped-wind geometry, pair multiplicity, and ion-energy conditions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic, magnetized pulsar wind terminating in a standing shock (the termination shock, TS) embedded in a pulsar wind nebula. Downstream of the TS, ultra-relativistic electrons and positrons radiate synchrotron emission whose observed spectrum (as in the Crab Nebula) is well fit by an injected isotropic energy distribution of broken power-law form

   N(E) ∝ E^{-p₁}  for E ≲ E_b,
   N(E) ∝ E^{-p₂}  for E ≳ E_b,

with p₁ ≈ 1.5 (radio-emitting low-energy particles), p₂ ≈ 2.2 (optical/X-ray/γ-ray emitting high-energy particles up to a few TeV), and a break around E_b ∼ 100 GeV.

Three candidate acceleration mechanisms operate at or near the TS, each requiring distinct upstream conditions:

(i) Driven magnetic reconnection of the alternating-polarity "striped" component of the wind, requiring a sufficiently large magnetization σ, a striped-wind geometry within a latitude band around the magnetic equator, and high pair multiplicity κ;

(ii) Diffusive shock acceleration (DSA), requiring locally weak magnetization (σ ≪ 1) so that the relativistic shock is quasi-parallel/weakly magnetized, achievable only in sectors where upstream magnetic dissipation is strong;

(iii) Resonant ion-cyclotron absorption, requiring the presence of a relativistic ion component carrying a substantial fraction of the wind's energy at sufficiently high Lorentz factor, whose cyclotron waves downstream resonantly accelerate the pair plasma.

Problem. Determine, within a self-consistent multi-dimensional relativistic MHD model of the pulsar wind and its termination shock, the combination of these mechanisms and the corresponding spatial sectors of the TS (e.g., equatorial striped zone, mid-latitude oblique sectors, polar regions) that simultaneously reproduce:

(a) the flat low-energy slope p₁ ≈ 1.5 of the radio-emitting population,
(b) the steeper high-energy slope p₂ ≈ 2.2 up to multi-TeV energies,
(c) the location of the spectral break E_b,
(d) the inferred total particle injection rate and pair multiplicity, and
(e) consistency with the wind magnetization profile σ(θ) and striped-wind latitude extent inferred from global MHD modelling of the nebular morphology.

Specify which sectors of the TS contribute each spectral component, the required σ(θ), pair multiplicity κ, and ion energy fraction, and whether a single mechanism in different sectors, or a genuine combination of mechanisms, is necessary.
category_tag: relativistic MHD and particle acceleration in pulsar wind nebulae
status_search_result: The mechanism producing the broken injection spectrum at the Crab termination shock remains an open problem. Recent (2024) JWST observations of small-scale torus features provided the first direct observational evidence linking the spectral curvature to acceleration physics at the TS, and phenomenological models (e.g., Fraschetti & Pohl 2017) reproduce the broadband spectrum, but no consensus mechanism (reconnection vs. DSA vs. ion-cyclotron resonance) and no unique sector assignment along the TS has been established within self-consistent multi-D MHD models.

paper_title: Multi-D magnetohydrodynamic modelling of pulsar wind nebulae: recent progress and open questions
original_question: Can long-term three-dimensional relativistic MHD simulations of the Crab Nebula, including kink-driven magnetic-field evolution and realistic emission diagnostics, simultaneously reproduce the observed large-scale magnetic-field strength, torus and jet surface brightness, integrated synchrotron and inverse-Compton spectrum, and particle content after the nebula reaches self-similar expansion?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a pulsar wind nebula modeled as a relativistic, ideal magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) flow in three spatial dimensions, in which a cold, ultrarelativistic, magnetized wind from a central pulsar terminates at a strong shock and inflates a magnetized bubble inside an expanding supernova ejecta. The wind is parameterized by a time-dependent spin-down luminosity L(t), a striped/toroidal magnetization parameter σ(θ,t), and a latitude-dependent energy flux. Inside the nebula, the magnetic field is allowed to evolve dynamically, including the development of large-scale current-driven (kink) instabilities of the toroidal field that drive turbulent magnetic dissipation and reconnection. Particles are injected at the termination shock with a broken power-law energy distribution, advected with the flow, and lose energy through adiabatic expansion, synchrotron radiation, and inverse-Compton scattering on the cosmic microwave background, far-infrared dust, and stellar/synchrotron photon fields. Run such a simulation for a physical time comparable to the age of the Crab Nebula (~10^3 yr), long enough that the system enters a self-similar expansion phase.

Determine whether there exists a choice of admissible wind and injection parameters (within ranges consistent with pulsar spin-down, multiwavelength constraints, and the total injected pair multiplicity) such that the resulting simulation simultaneously satisfies all of the following observational constraints for the Crab Nebula:

(i) the volume-averaged interior magnetic-field strength matches the observationally inferred value (≈ 100–300 μG) to within observational uncertainty;
(ii) the synthetic surface-brightness maps reproduce both the optical/X-ray torus and the polar jet at the observed luminosities and morphologies (in particular the torus is not under-luminous and the jets are not over-collimated);
(iii) the integrated photon spectrum from radio through gamma-rays, including the synchrotron component and the inverse-Compton component, agrees with measurements; and
(iv) the inferred total particle content (number of radiating leptons and implied pair multiplicity at the wind termination) is consistent with independent constraints from pulsar magnetospheric models.

State whether such a self-consistent three-dimensional RMHD model of the Crab Nebula exists, or prove that within the stated modeling framework no parameter choice can simultaneously meet (i)–(iv).

No published 3D simulation has simultaneously matched the magnetic-field strength, full jet/torus brightness, broadband synchrotron+IC spectrum, and pair-multiplicity constraints, so the question remains open.

paper_title: Crystal Nucleation in Liquids: Open Questions and Future Challenges in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
original_question: How can molecular dynamics simulations of crystal nucleation in liquids be made accurate enough for realistic systems of practical interest by improving both the interatomic potentials used to represent the system and the enhanced-sampling methods used to access rare nucleation events?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical molecular dynamics framework for studying crystal nucleation from the liquid phase. The system consists of N atoms or molecules whose configurations x ∈ R^{3N} evolve under Newtonian dynamics governed by an interatomic potential U(x), with the liquid maintained at thermodynamic conditions (temperature T, pressure P) where the crystalline phase is thermodynamically favored. Crystal nucleation is a rare event: the time scale for spontaneous formation of a critical crystalline nucleus typically exceeds by many orders of magnitude the time scales accessible to direct numerical integration of the equations of motion. To overcome this, enhanced-sampling techniques (e.g., metadynamics, umbrella sampling, forward flux sampling, transition path sampling, seeding) are used to bias or accelerate exploration of configuration space along chosen collective variables that distinguish liquid-like from crystal-like local environments.

Develop (a) systematically improved interatomic potentials U(x) — whether empirical, machine-learned, or otherwise — that quantitatively reproduce the thermodynamic, structural, and dynamical properties of real liquids and their crystalline polymorphs near coexistence (in particular melting temperatures, surface tensions, diffusion coefficients, and relative phase stabilities), and (b) enhanced-sampling algorithms together with collective variables that yield converged, statistically reliable estimates of nucleation free-energy barriers, nucleation rates J(T,P), and critical-nucleus structures for systems of practical interest (e.g., metals, water and ice polymorphs, molecular crystals, alloys), such that the resulting simulated nucleation rates and pathways agree quantitatively with experimental measurements.

Provide criteria, algorithms, and benchmarks under which both objectives can be met simultaneously for a chosen target liquid.
category_tag: molecular dynamics simulation of crystal nucleation
status_search_result: The problem is a broad open challenge in computational materials science. Recent literature (2020–2025) on machine-learning interatomic potentials and advanced enhanced-sampling methods reports continued progress but no general solution; quantitative agreement with experimental nucleation rates remains elusive for most realistic systems.

paper_title: Crystal Nucleation in Liquids: Open Questions and Future Challenges in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
original_question: In urea nucleation from solution, when the transition-state nucleus already has a fully crystalline core and the amorphous precursor clusters are unstable relative to the liquid phase rather than metastable states with their own free-energy basins, should this process still be classified as a two-step nucleation mechanism?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the homogeneous nucleation of urea crystals from a supersaturated solution, viewed as an activated process along a suitable reaction coordinate joining the homogeneous liquid solution to the crystalline phase. Suppose molecular-dynamics-style sampling of the free-energy landscape produces the following picture:

(i) Pre-critical configurations along the pathway contain disordered (amorphous) molecular aggregates ("precursor clusters") of solute molecules that are denser than the bulk liquid but lack long-range orientational/translational order.

(ii) These amorphous precursor clusters are unstable with respect to the homogeneous liquid: they do not occupy a distinct local minimum of the free energy as a function of the chosen order parameters, but rather lie on the uphill side of a single free-energy barrier.

(iii) The transition-state configuration (the saddle point of the free-energy landscape, i.e. the critical nucleus) already possesses a fully crystalline core surrounded by a thinner disordered shell.

The "two-step nucleation mechanism" is conventionally defined as a pathway in which the system first crosses a barrier into a metastable intermediate phase (e.g. a dense amorphous or liquid-like cluster occupying its own free-energy basin) and only subsequently crosses a second barrier from this intermediate into the crystalline phase.

Question: Under conditions (i)–(iii) above—where the critical nucleus is predominantly crystalline and the amorphous precursors do not constitute a metastable phase with its own free-energy basin but are merely unstable fluctuations of the liquid—does the urea nucleation pathway satisfy the definition of a two-step nucleation mechanism, or must it instead be classified as a single-step (classical-type) nucleation mechanism with a structured transition state? Provide a precise criterion, formulated in terms of the topology of the free-energy landscape (number and depth of intermediate basins along the minimum free-energy path), that unambiguously distinguishes two-step from one-step nucleation in this setting.
status_search_result: The literature on solution crystallization (including urea, glycine, NaCl, and proteins) continues to debate the classification boundary between one-step and two-step nucleation. Recent reviews (2019–2024) note that the distinction depends sensitively on whether amorphous precursors form a true metastable basin, and there is no consensus criterion when the critical nucleus is already crystalline while precursors are merely unstable fluctuations. The question is therefore conceptually open.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Orthogonal Polynomials on Fractals and Related Questions
original_question: Given a modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K such that the modulus of continuity of the Green function g_{C\K} of the complement of K is comparable to ω near 0. More precisely, one asks for a compact set K for which the modulus of continuity ω(g_{C\K}, ·) either coincides with ω along some null sequence or is weakly equivalent to ω in the sense that there exist constants C1, C2 > 0 such that C1 ω(δ) ≤ ω(g_{C\K}, δ) ≤ C2 ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.
self_contained_problem:
A modulus of continuity is a non-decreasing function ω : [0,∞) → [0,∞) with ω(0) = 0 and ω continuous at 0. For a non-polar compact set K ⊂ C whose complement Ω = C \ K is connected and regular for the Dirichlet problem, let g_Ω(z) denote the Green function of Ω with logarithmic pole at infinity (so g_Ω is harmonic on Ω, vanishes quasi-everywhere on K, and g_Ω(z) = log|z| + O(1) as |z| → ∞). The modulus of continuity of g_Ω is defined by
    ω(g_Ω, δ) := sup { |g_Ω(z) − g_Ω(w)| : z, w ∈ C, |z − w| ≤ δ },
for δ > 0 (with the convention g_Ω ≡ 0 on K).

Problem. Given an arbitrary modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K ⊂ C such that ω(g_{C\K}, ·) is "similar" to ω near 0, in either of the following senses:
(a) there exists a sequence δ_n ↘ 0 with ω(g_{C\K}, δ_n) = ω(δ_n) for every n; or
(b) ω(g_{C\K}, ·) is weakly equivalent to ω near 0, i.e., there exist constants C_1, C_2 > 0 and δ_0 > 0 such that
    C_1 ω(δ) ≤ ω(g_{C\K}, δ) ≤ C_2 ω(δ) for all 0 < δ ≤ δ_0.

Determine, for each given modulus of continuity ω, such a compact set K (or characterize the moduli ω for which such K exists).
category_tag: Green functions and potential theory on fractals
status_search_result: The problem appears to belong to an active line of research on smoothness of Green functions for Cantor-type compact sets, where weakly equilibrium Cantor-type sets are constructed to realize prescribed smoothness/Markov factor behavior. Partial results exist (e.g., for various Hölder and log-type moduli realized by Cantor-type sets), but a fully general construction matching an arbitrary modulus of continuity does not appear to be established. Status is best described as open in general, with partial constructions known.

original_question: Find a compact set K contained in the real line for which the Green function of the complement has matching Hölder upper and lower bounds near K. That is, determine whether there exists a compact set K ⊂ R, an exponent α > 0, and constants C1, C2 > 0 such that, whenever δ = dist(z, K) is sufficiently small, one has C1 δ^α ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2 δ^α.
self_contained_problem:
For a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ of positive logarithmic capacity, let $g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(z)$ denote the Green function of the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with logarithmic pole at infinity, extended by $0$ to $K$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, write $\delta = \operatorname{dist}(z,K)$.

Exhibit (or prove the existence of) a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$, an exponent $\alpha>0$, and constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that for all $z$ with $\delta=\operatorname{dist}(z,K)$ sufficiently small one has the matching two-sided Hölder bounds
$$ C_1\,\delta^{\alpha} \;\le\; g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(z) \;\le\; C_2\,\delta^{\alpha}. $$
status_search_result: Searches returned substantial work on Hölder continuity (upper bounds) of Green functions for complements of Cantor-type sets and Wiener-type characterizations, including results by Totik, Toókos, Goncharov and others. However, no source was found that exhibits a compact set on the real line achieving matching two-sided Hölder bounds with the same exponent, nor a proof that such a set cannot exist; the question appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Orthogonal Polynomials on Fractals and Related Questions
context_brief: Recurrence coefficients on generalized Julia sets
original_question: Let (f_n) be a regular polynomial sequence whose generalized Julia set J(f_n) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients of the monic orthogonal polynomials associated with the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} are asymptotically almost periodic.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of polynomials with $\deg f_n \ge 2$, and define the composition $F_n = f_n \circ f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1$. The generalized (autonomous-free) Julia set associated to $(f_n)$ is
$$J(f_n) = \partial\{z\in\mathbb{C} : (F_n(z))_{n\ge 1}\text{ is bounded}\}.$$
Assume that $J(f_n)\subset\mathbb{R}$ is a Cantor-type set (a totally disconnected, perfect, compact subset of the real line) and that $(f_n)$ is regular in the sense that $J(f_n)$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem and is regular in the sense of Stahl–Totik (so that the equilibrium measure $\mu_{J(f_n)}$ of $J(f_n)$ is well-defined).

Let $\{P_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials with respect to $\mu_{J(f_n)}$, satisfying the three-term recurrence
$$xP_n(x) = P_{n+1}(x) + b_{n+1}P_n(x) + a_n^2 P_{n-1}(x),\qquad n\ge 0,$$
with $P_{-1}=0$, $P_0=1$, and recurrence coefficients $\{a_n\}_{n\ge 1}\subset(0,\infty)$, $\{b_n\}_{n\ge 1}\subset\mathbb{R}$.

Recall that a bounded sequence $(c_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is called asymptotically almost periodic if there exist a Bohr almost periodic sequence $(c_n^*)$ and a sequence $(\varepsilon_n)$ with $\varepsilon_n\to 0$ such that $c_n = c_n^* + \varepsilon_n$.

Problem. Prove that the recurrence coefficients $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n\ge 1}$ associated with the monic orthogonal polynomials of the equilibrium measure $\mu_{J(f_n)}$ are asymptotically almost periodic.
status_search_result: A direct resolution of this conjecture for general regular polynomial sequences with real Cantor-type Julia sets does not appear in the literature surveyed. Related work (e.g., on the classical Cantor measure and on the APN class with asymptotically N-periodic recurrence coefficients) provides numerical evidence and partial results in special autonomous cases, but no complete proof of asymptotic almost periodicity of the recurrence coefficients in the generalized Julia set setting was found.

original_question: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of the real line that is regular for the Dirichlet problem, and let μ be a measure with essential support ess supp(μ) = K. Suppose that the isolated points {x_n} of supp(μ) satisfy Σ_n g_{C\K}(x_n) < ∞. If μ also satisfies the Szegő-type integrability condition ∫_K log(dμ/dμ_K) dμ_K(x) > -∞, where μ_K is the equilibrium measure on K, must it follow that the Widom condition limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ) > 0 or the stronger Widom condition 2 liminf_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ) > 0 holds? Conversely, does the Widom condition imply the Szegő-type integrability condition?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a non-polar compact set that is regular for the Dirichlet problem, and let $\mu_K$ denote the equilibrium measure of $K$. Let $g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}$ denote the Green function of the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. Let $\mu$ be a positive Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}$ whose essential support equals $K$, and assume that the isolated points $\{x_n\}$ of $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ satisfy
$$\sum_n g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(x_n) < \infty.$$
For $n\ge 0$, let $P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu)$ be the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$ with respect to $\mu$, and define the (squared) Widom factor by
$$W_n^2(\mu) \;=\; \frac{\|P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu)\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2}{\operatorname{Cap}(K)^{2n}},$$
where $\operatorname{Cap}(K)$ is the logarithmic capacity of $K$.

Consider the Szegő-type integrability condition
$$\textbf{(S)}\qquad \int_K \log\!\frac{d\mu}{d\mu_K}(x)\,d\mu_K(x) \;>\; -\infty,$$
the Widom condition
$$\textbf{(W1)}\qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty} W_n^2(\mu) \;>\; 0,$$
and the stronger Widom condition
$$\textbf{(W2)}\qquad \liminf_{n\to\infty} W_n^2(\mu) \;>\; 0.$$

Prove or disprove the following:

(a) Condition (S) implies condition (W1) (and possibly (W2)) under the above hypotheses on $K$ and on the isolated points of $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$.

(b) Conversely, condition (W1) (or (W2)) implies condition (S).
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., reviews of Widom factors and Szegő–Widom asymptotics, and 2020–2025 work on Widom factors for L^p extremal and orthogonal polynomials, including constructions of non-polar Cantor-type sets with unbounded L^2 Widom factors) continues to investigate the relationship between Szegő-type integrability and Widom-type lower bounds on general non-polar compacts. No source located clearly establishes both directions of the equivalence under the stated hypothesis on isolated points, so the problem appears to remain open or only partially understood.

original_question: Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of the real line, let α be the leftmost endpoint of K, and suppose that for every c in R \ K the equilibrium measure satisfies μ_K([α, c]) ∈ Q. What structural consequences does this rationality condition force on K? In particular, must K be a polynomial generalized Julia set? Does it imply the existence of a sequence of admissible polynomials (f_n)_{n=1}^∞ such that the sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence with K = ⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ of positive logarithmic capacity (i.e. non-polar), let $\mu_K$ denote its (logarithmic) equilibrium measure, that is, the unique Borel probability measure on $K$ minimizing the logarithmic energy $I(\mu)=\iint\log\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)$. The set $K$ is called regular if its associated Green function (with pole at infinity) is continuous on $\mathbb{C}$. A polynomial $f(z)=a_d z^d+\cdots$ of degree $d\ge 2$ is called admissible (in the real generalized-Julia-set sense) if $f^{-1}([-1,1])\subset\mathbb{R}$ and the preimage consists of $d$ disjoint closed intervals. Given a sequence of admissible polynomials $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$, set $F_n=f_n\circ f_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ f_1$. Then $K=\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty} F_n^{-1}([-1,1])$ (when this intersection is non-empty and the sets are nested decreasingly) is called a (real) polynomial generalized Julia set.
\medskip

Problem. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a regular non-polar compact set, and let $\alpha=\min K$ be its leftmost endpoint. Suppose that
$$\mu_K\bigl([\alpha,c]\bigr)\in\mathbb{Q}\qquad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb{R}\setminus K.$$
What structural properties must $K$ possess? In particular:

(i) Must $K$ be a polynomial generalized Julia set?

(ii) Must there exist a sequence of admissible polynomials $(f_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that the sets $F_n^{-1}([-1,1])$ form a decreasing sequence with
$$K=\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty} F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?$$
category_tag: Potential theory and orthogonal polynomials on Julia sets
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of this rationality-of-equilibrium-mass characterization problem. Related work by Goncharov, Alpan and others on weakly equilibrium Cantor-type sets and orthogonal polynomials on generalized Julia sets continues to develop, but no source identified establishes or disproves that the rationality condition on $\mu_K([\alpha,c])$ forces $K$ to be a polynomial generalized Julia set.

context_brief: Hausdorff dimension formulas for equilibrium measures
original_question: Is it possible to derive simple explicit formulas for the Hausdorff dimension dim(μ_{J(f_n)}) of the equilibrium measure of the generalized Julia set J(f_n) when (f_n) is a regular polynomial sequence?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of polynomials $f_n(z)=a_{n,d_n}z^{d_n}+\cdots+a_{n,0}$ with complex coefficients and $\deg f_n=d_n\ge 2$. For $n\ge 1$ set $F_n:=f_n\circ f_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ f_1$, and define the (generalized) filled-in Julia set and Julia set of the sequence by
$$K(f_n):=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:(F_n(z))_{n\ge 1}\text{ is bounded}\},\qquad J(f_n):=\partial K(f_n).$$
The sequence $(f_n)$ is called a regular polynomial sequence if there exist constants $A_n,\widetilde{A}_n>0$ and $L\ge 0$ with $\sup_n\widetilde{A}_n<\infty$ such that
$$|a_{n,d_n}|\,|z|^{d_n}\bigl(1-A_n|z|^{-1}\bigr)\le |f_n(z)|\le |a_{n,d_n}|\,|z|^{d_n}\bigl(1+\widetilde A_n|z|^{-1}\bigr)\quad(|z|\ge L\widetilde A_n),$$
together with the standard non-degeneracy conditions ensuring that $K(f_n)$ is a non-polar compact set. Under these conditions $K(f_n)$ admits a unique equilibrium measure (i.e., the measure of minimal logarithmic energy) $\mu_{J(f_n)}$, supported on $J(f_n)$.

Question. Find a simple explicit formula, in terms of the coefficients/degrees $\{a_{n,j},d_n\}$ of the polynomials $f_n$, for the Hausdorff dimension
$$\dim_H\bigl(\mu_{J(f_n)}\bigr):=\inf\{\dim_H(E):E\text{ Borel},\ \mu_{J(f_n)}(E)=\mu_{J(f_n)}(\mathbb{C})\}$$
of the equilibrium measure of the generalized Julia set $J(f_n)$ associated with an arbitrary regular polynomial sequence $(f_n)$.

status_search_result: Web searches returned related research on equilibrium measures and Hausdorff dimension of (random/composition) Julia sets for sequences of polynomials, but no source providing a simple explicit closed-form formula for the Hausdorff dimension of the equilibrium measure on $J(f_n)$ for general regular polynomial sequences was located. The status appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible by search.

original_question: For the complete graph K_n, does there exist a three-dimensional orthogonal cube-drawing in which each edge route has at most one bend and each vertex is represented by a cube whose surface area is O(n), equivalently a degree-restricted 1-bend cube-drawing for K_n?
self_contained_problem: A three-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ an axis-aligned box (a rectangular parallelepiped with integer coordinates) in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with pairwise disjoint interiors, and to each edge $\{u,v\}\in E$ an axis-parallel polygonal route from a point on the surface of the box of $u$ to a point on the surface of the box of $v$. Distinct edge routes may share points only at common endpoints on box surfaces, and an edge route may not pass through the interior of any box. A drawing is called \emph{1-bend} if every edge route consists of at most two axis-parallel segments (i.e., has at most one bend). A drawing is called a \emph{cube-drawing} if every vertex box is a cube. A cube-drawing is called \emph{degree-restricted} if for every vertex $v$ the surface area of its cube is $O(\deg(v))$; equivalently, for the complete graph $K_n$ this means each vertex cube has surface area $O(n)$ (so side length $O(\sqrt{n})$).\n\nQuestion: Does there exist, for every $n$, a 1-bend degree-restricted three-dimensional orthogonal cube-drawing of the complete graph $K_n$?
status_search_result: The problem is reported as resolved in the negative: $K_n$ does not admit a 1-bend degree-restricted cube-drawing, so no such drawing exists for sufficiently large $n$.

paper_title: THE DIFFUSE LIGHT OF THE UNIVERSE: On the microwave background before and after its discovery: open questions
context_brief: Distance and locality of the 3K radiation
original_question: At what distance, and with what spatial distribution of sources, is the observed 3 K microwave background actually produced? More specifically, is it only a very distant fossil background emitted in the early universe, or could it instead be a more universal radiation field produced partly or wholly locally and at long distances, given that its smooth blackbody spectrum does not itself provide a direct distance measurement?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an isotropic diffuse electromagnetic background that, when measured by an observer, exhibits a near-perfect Planck (blackbody) spectrum with characteristic temperature approximately 2.7 K (the so-called 3 K microwave background). Because a smooth blackbody spectrum carries no intrinsic distance information (no spectral lines, no parallax, no standard-candle structure), the spatial distribution of emitting sources along the line of sight cannot be inferred from the spectrum alone.

Determine, on the basis of independent physical arguments and observational constraints, the spatial origin of this radiation. Specifically:

(a) Is the observed 3 K background produced exclusively as a fossil relic emitted in the early universe at very large cosmological distances (i.e. on a last-scattering surface at high redshift), so that essentially none of the locally measured intensity originates from sources within the observable nearby universe?

(b) Or could a non-negligible fraction of the locally observed intensity be generated by sources distributed throughout space, including local and intermediate-distance regions, so that the 3 K background is a more universal radiation field filling space and produced both nearby and at large distances?

Provide quantitative bounds on the fraction of the observed 3 K intensity that may be attributed to local versus distant sources, using whatever constraints (anisotropy structure, polarization, Sunyaev–Zel'dovich distortions, spectral distortions, correlations with large-scale structure, etc.) can break the degeneracy left by the blackbody spectrum.
status_search_result: The mainstream cosmological consensus interprets the 3 K microwave background as a relic of the early universe emitted at the last-scattering surface (z≈1100), supported by its near-perfect blackbody spectrum, anisotropy spectrum, polarization, and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich measurements toward galaxy clusters (which place much of the radiation behind clusters). However, the precise question of whether a non-negligible local or intermediate-distance contribution can be ruled out in a model-independent way—given that a blackbody spectrum alone provides no distance measurement—remains a posed open question in the cited line of inquiry, and no rigorous quantitative upper bound on a possible local component is universally established outside the standard model assumptions.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Locally Finite or Locally Nilpotent Derivations and E-Derivations
original_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let δ be either an R-derivation of A or an R-E-derivation of A, where an R-E-derivation means an R-linear map of the form I − φ for some R-algebra endomorphism φ of A. For an R-subspace V of A, write r(V) for the set of elements a in A such that a^m lies in V for all sufficiently large m; and say that V is a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace when eventual membership of all powers a^m forces eventual membership of ba^m, a^mc, or ba^mc respectively. The LFNED problem asks for a description of r(δ(I)) for every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, asks which R-derivations and R-E-derivations of A have image Im δ = δ(A) that is a Mathieu subspace of the corresponding handedness, and asks which such maps send every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A to a Mathieu subspace of the corresponding handedness.
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and let $A$ be an associative (not necessarily commutative) $R$-algebra. An $R$-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map $\delta:A	o A$ satisfying $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)y+x\delta(y)$ for all $x,y\in A$. An $R$-E-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map of the form $\delta=\mathrm{Id}_A-\varphi$, where $\varphi:A	o A$ is an $R$-algebra endomorphism.

For an $R$-subspace $V\subseteq A$, define the radical of $V$ by
$$r(V)=\{a\in A : a^m\in V	ext{ for all sufficiently large }m\}.$$

Let $\vartheta\in\{	ext{left},	ext{right},	ext{two-sided}\}$. The $R$-subspace $V$ is called a $\vartheta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$ if, whenever $a\in A$ satisfies $a^m\in V$ for every integer $m\ge 1$, then for all $b,c\in A$:

(i) $ba^m\in V$ for all $m\gg 0$, when $\vartheta=	ext{left}$;
(ii) $a^mc\in V$ for all $m\gg 0$, when $\vartheta=	ext{right}$;
(iii) $ba^mc\in V$ for all $m\gg 0$, when $\vartheta=	ext{two-sided}$.

For every commutative ring $R$, every $R$-algebra $A$, and every $R$-derivation or $R$-E-derivation $\delta$ of $A$:

(A) Determine the radical $r(\delta(I))$ for every left, right, or two-sided ideal $I$ of $A$.

(B) Characterize those $\delta$ for which the image $\mathrm{Im}\,\delta=\delta(A)$ is a $\vartheta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$ (for each choice of $\vartheta$).

(C) Characterize those $\delta$ such that $\delta(I)$ is a $\vartheta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$ for every $\vartheta$-ideal $I$ of $A$ (for each choice of $\vartheta$).
status_search_result: The problem is a broad program with many cases; it remains open in general but several special cases have been settled. Affirmative answers are known, e.g., for rank-two locally nilpotent derivations of polynomial algebras, for rank-three homogeneous locally nilpotent derivations on three-variable polynomial rings, and for locally nilpotent derivations of bivariate polynomial algebras over one-dimensional UFDs. The full LFNED problem in its general formulation has not been resolved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Locally Finite or Locally Nilpotent Derivations and E-Derivations
original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let δ be either a locally nilpotent K-derivation of A or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation of A, where locally nilpotent means that for every a in A there exists m ≥ 1 with δ^m(a) = 0. For each choice of handedness ϑ ∈ {left, right, two-sided}, if I is a ϑ-ideal of A, must the image δ(I) always be a ϑ-Mathieu subspace of A?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be a $K$-algebra (not necessarily commutative or unital). 

A $K$-linear map $\delta : A \to A$ is called a $K$-derivation if $\delta(ab) = \delta(a)b + a\delta(b)$ for all $a,b \in A$, and a $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation if $\delta = \mathrm{Id}_A - \phi$ for some $K$-algebra endomorphism $\phi$ of $A$. The map $\delta$ is locally nilpotent if for every $a \in A$ there exists an integer $m \geq 1$ (depending on $a$) such that $\delta^m(a) = 0$.

For $\vartheta \in \{\text{left}, \text{right}, \text{two-sided}\}$, a $K$-subspace $V \subseteq A$ is called a $\vartheta$-Mathieu subspace ($\vartheta$-MS) of $A$ if it satisfies the following property: for every $a \in A$ such that $a^m \in V$ for all sufficiently large $m \geq 1$, and for every $b \in A$, one has
- $ba^m \in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, when $\vartheta = \text{left}$;
- $a^m b \in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, when $\vartheta = \text{right}$;
- $ba^m c \in V$ for all $b,c \in A$ and all sufficiently large $m$, when $\vartheta = \text{two-sided}$.

A $\vartheta$-ideal of $A$ means a left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal according to $\vartheta$.

Question: Let $\delta$ be either a locally nilpotent $K$-derivation or a locally nilpotent $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$. For each $\vartheta \in \{\text{left}, \text{right}, \text{two-sided}\}$ and every $\vartheta$-ideal $I$ of $A$, must the image $\delta(I)$ be a $\vartheta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$?
category_tag: Locally nilpotent derivations and Mathieu-Zhao subspaces
status_search_result: The general LNED conjecture remains open. Partial affirmative results are known: it has been verified for Laurent polynomial algebras, for algebraic algebras, for bivariate polynomial algebras over one-dimensional UFDs, and for various classes of locally nilpotent derivations of polynomial rings in three variables (rank-two, homogeneous rank-three, rank-one acting on principal ideals). No full resolution has been reported.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Locally Finite or Locally Nilpotent Derivations and E-Derivations
original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let (Λ, ∗) be a monoid with unit element e. Suppose A has a K-algebra grading A = ⊕_{λ∈Λ} A_λ such that each A_λ is a K-subspace of A and A_λ A_μ ⊆ A_{λ∗μ} for all λ, μ in Λ. Must the K-subspace formed by all non-unit homogeneous pieces, namely ⊕_{e≠λ∈Λ} A_λ, always be a Mathieu subspace of A?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero (not necessarily algebraically closed), let $A$ be a $K$-algebra, and let $(\Lambda,*)$ be a monoid with unit element $e$. Assume $A$ admits a $K$-algebra grading by $\Lambda$, that is, a decomposition
$$A=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda$$
into $K$-subspaces $A_\lambda$ satisfying $A_\lambda A_\mu\subseteq A_{\lambda*\mu}$ for all $\lambda,\mu\in\Lambda$.

Recall that a $K$-subspace $M\subseteq A$ is called a Mathieu subspace (or Mathieu–Zhao space) of $A$ if for every $a\in A$ such that $a^m\in M$ for all $m\geq 1$, and for every $b\in A$, there exists $N\geq 1$ (depending on $a,b$) such that $b\,a^m\in M$ for all $m\geq N$.

Question: Must the $K$-subspace
$$\bigoplus_{e\neq\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda$$
consisting of all homogeneous components of non-unit degree always be a Mathieu subspace of $A$?
status_search_result: The Grading Conjecture concerning Mathieu(–Zhao) subspaces of monoid-graded algebras was proposed as an open conjecture by Zhao. Web searches did not surface any published resolution; the broader program around Mathieu–Zhao spaces (linked to the Jacobian Conjecture) remains active, and no source claims a proof or counterexample to this particular grading conjecture.

paper_title: Two Open Problems in the Fixed Point Theory of Contractive Type Mappings on First-Countable Quasimetric Spaces
context_brief: Fixed points of contractions on complete quasimetric spaces
original_question: Let (X, d) be a complete quasimetric space, where d(x, z) ≤ d(x, y) + d(y, z) for all x, y, z in X and d(x, y) + d(y, x) = 0 holds only when x = y. If g : X → X is a contraction, meaning that there exists a constant λ with 0 ≤ λ < 1 such that d(g(x), g(y)) ≤ λ·d(x, y) for all x, y in X, must g have a fixed point?
self_contained_problem:
A quasimetric on a set X is a function d : X × X → [0, ∞) satisfying:
(i) d(x, z) ≤ d(x, y) + d(y, z) for all x, y, z ∈ X (triangle inequality);
(ii) d(x, y) + d(y, x) = 0 if and only if x = y (separation).
Note that d is not assumed to be symmetric. The pair (X, d) is called a quasimetric space. Topological notions such as convergence, Cauchy sequences and completeness can be defined using the forward topology generated by the forward balls B(x, r) = {y ∈ X : d(x, y) < r}; (X, d) is called complete if every (forward) Cauchy sequence converges.

A map g : X → X is called a contraction if there exists a constant λ ∈ [0, 1) such that
   d(g(x), g(y)) ≤ λ · d(x, y) for all x, y ∈ X.

Question: Must every contraction g : X → X on a complete quasimetric space (X, d) have a fixed point, i.e., a point x ∈ X with g(x) = x?
category_tag: fixed point theory on quasimetric spaces
status_search_result: The problem is resolved in the negative: there exist complete quasimetric spaces (X, d) and contractions g : X → X with empty fixed point set. Explicit counterexamples are constructed, showing that without additional hypotheses (such as d being an H-distance, or Smyth-completeness, or symmetry-type conditions), the Banach contraction principle fails on complete quasimetric spaces. Subsequent literature extends Banach's principle to quasimetric settings only under such extra conditions.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
original_question: How should vulnerability-analysis frameworks for unmanned aerial system (UAS) networks model the interactions among communications, computation, sensors, and physical airframe components so that UAS are not treated merely as ordinary mobile ad hoc networks or isolated subsystems, and so that vulnerabilities created by interactions among heterogeneous UAV subsystems can be identified?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a vulnerability-analysis framework for unmanned aerial system (UAS) networks that explicitly models a UAS as a cyber-physical system composed of four heterogeneous subsystems: (i) the communications subsystem (radio links, networking protocols, ground-control links, swarm communications), (ii) the computation subsystem (onboard processors, flight-control software, autopilot logic), (iii) the sensing subsystem (GPS, IMU, cameras, lidar, environmental sensors), and (iv) the physical airframe subsystem (motors, actuators, power, aerodynamic structure). The framework should satisfy the following requirements:

1. It must represent the cross-couplings and feedback interactions among the four subsystems above, rather than treating the UAS as a standard mobile ad hoc network or as a collection of independent subsystems analyzed in isolation.

2. It must support the identification of vulnerabilities that arise specifically from interactions between heterogeneous subsystems (i.e., vulnerabilities that are not present in any single subsystem in isolation but emerge from their coupling).

3. It must be sufficiently general to apply across the heterogeneous space of UAV architectures and capabilities (varying airframes, sensor suites, autonomy levels, and mission profiles), while still permitting concrete instantiation for a given platform.

Formally describe such a framework, give a rigorous notion of an "interaction-induced vulnerability" within it, and provide an analysis methodology that, given a specific UAS instantiation, enumerates or characterizes the set of interaction-induced vulnerabilities. Demonstrate that the framework captures vulnerabilities that pure ad hoc network models or single-subsystem models provably miss.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open interdisciplinary research challenge. While various UAS/UAV security threat models and surveys have appeared since, no single widely-adopted formal framework that simultaneously models communications, computation, sensing, and physical airframe interactions and rigorously identifies interaction-induced vulnerabilities across heterogeneous UAV architectures has been established. The problem appears to remain open as a general research goal.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
context_brief: Proactive spoofing-signal elimination for UAV navigation
original_question: Can proactive mechanisms that eliminate spoofing signals be made applicable to UAV sensory and navigation subsystems, and what design would make those mechanisms robust under the speed and spatial freedom of UAVs rather than relying only on reactive detection of navigation attacks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver and an inertial sensor suite, moving along an unconstrained three-dimensional trajectory with high translational and angular velocities. The receiver observes a superposition of authentic GNSS signals and adversarial spoofing signals injected by one or more ground- or air-based attackers, where the attacker may control signal power, code phase, Doppler shift, direction of arrival, and polarization. Existing reactive countermeasures (e.g., direction-of-arrival checks, polarization analysis, statistical signal-processing detectors, and beamforming-based suppression) typically rely on assumptions—such as a quasi-stationary platform, a known antenna orientation, or a stable multipath environment—that are violated by the high speeds and full spatial freedom of UAV motion.

Formulate and design a proactive anti-spoofing mechanism for the UAV sensory and navigation subsystem that actively eliminates (rather than merely detects) spoofing components from the received signal, subject to the following requirements:

1. The mechanism must remain valid under arbitrary UAV kinematics, including rapid changes in attitude, position, and velocity.
2. It must not depend on assumptions of antenna orientation stability, ground proximity, or static multipath geometry.
3. It must operate within the size, weight, power, and computational constraints of a typical small UAV platform.
4. It must guarantee, under a precisely stated adversary model (defining attacker power, number of spoofing transmitters, and degree of synchronization with authentic GNSS signals), bounded residual position and timing error after spoofing-signal elimination.

Provide such a design together with a rigorous analysis establishing the conditions on signal geometry, antenna configuration, and processing algorithm under which the proactive elimination is provably effective, or alternatively prove an impossibility result delimiting the regimes in which no such proactive mechanism can succeed.
status_search_result: GNSS spoofing countermeasures for UAVs remain an active research area as of 2026. Surveys and recent works continue to describe the design of UAV-suitable anti-spoofing techniques as an open problem, with proposed approaches (multi-antenna processing, cryptographic authentication via Galileo OSNMA, sensor fusion) addressing parts of the problem but no general proactive elimination scheme that is robust to full UAV kinematics has been established.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
context_brief: Secure UAV ADS-B and TCAS adaptation
original_question: How can UAV air-traffic-control and collision-avoidance systems based on ADS-B- or TCAS-like protocols be redesigned or secured so that unauthenticated broadcasts, false traffic-data injection, and intentionally orchestrated TCAS-induced collision scenarios do not create unsafe advisories in mission-critical UAS operations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an unmanned aerial system (UAS) network in which each aircraft participates in an air-traffic-control (ATC) and collision-avoidance subsystem modeled on ADS-B and TCAS. In the baseline model: (i) every aircraft periodically broadcasts in cleartext a state report containing its identifier, position, velocity, and altitude, with no cryptographic authentication or integrity protection; (ii) each aircraft runs a collision-avoidance logic that, upon receiving the broadcasts of nearby aircraft within a surveillance radius, issues resolution advisories (e.g., climb/descend) based only on instantaneous range, closure rate, and time-to-closest-approach thresholds, without forecasting the longer-term joint trajectories induced by the advisories themselves.

Consider an adversary that can (a) eavesdrop on all broadcasts, (b) inject forged broadcasts impersonating arbitrary aircraft identifiers, (c) jam or replay legitimate broadcasts, and (d) coordinate the timing and content of injected reports across multiple ghost tracks. Define a TCAS-induced collision as a configuration of (possibly partially adversarial) traffic such that the advisory logic, applied recursively, drives the legitimate aircraft into a state from which no admissible maneuver avoids loss of separation.

Design a redesigned ATC / collision-avoidance protocol for UAS, together with a precise threat model and formal safety property, satisfying the following requirements:

1. Authenticated broadcast: every state report accepted by a receiver is cryptographically bound to a legitimate aircraft identity, with bounded verification latency compatible with the surveillance update rate.
2. Injection and jamming resilience: under any polynomially bounded adversary of the type above, the probability that a forged or replayed report is accepted, or that suppression of legitimate reports causes an undetected loss of situational awareness, is negligible.
3. Advisory soundness against orchestrated geometries: the advisory-generation logic must incorporate a multi-step predictive model of joint trajectories such that, for any traffic configuration consistent with the authenticated inputs, the issued advisories provably do not drive participating aircraft into a TCAS-induced collision state, or else explicitly signal an unresolvable conflict.
4. Backward interoperability: the protocol must remain interoperable with legacy ADS-B/TCAS-equipped manned aircraft to a specified, precisely stated degree.

Provide the protocol specification, the formal adversary and safety definitions, and proofs (or impossibility results) establishing properties 1–4, including quantitative bounds on bandwidth, latency, and the maximum traffic density under which property 3 can be guaranteed.
status_search_result: The problem of securing ADS-B/TCAS for UAS against unauthenticated broadcasts, false-data injection, and TCAS-induced collisions remains an active and unresolved research area. Multiple proposals exist (lightweight authentication, PKI-based ADS-B, ADS-B encryption, formally verified ACAS X / ACAS Xu using machine-learned or verified lookup tables), but no single protocol has been adopted that simultaneously solves authentication, injection resilience, and provable avoidance of induced-collision geometries for UAS. ACAS Xu addresses some advisory-soundness concerns but not the underlying ADS-B authentication weaknesses.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
original_question: Under what conditions can an adversary defeat beamforming antenna arrays in a UAS network by deceiving direction-of-arrival estimation or manipulating distributed beamnulling so that legitimate links are nulled, and what countermeasures can prevent the beamnulling process from converging toward a disconnected network state?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a wireless network of $N$ nodes, each equipped with an antenna array of $M$ elements that performs both direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation and adaptive beamforming. Each node $i$ estimates the angles of arrival $\{\theta_{ij}\}$ of signals from neighbors $j$ using a standard subspace-based estimator (e.g. MUSIC or ESPRIT) applied to the spatial covariance matrix $R_i = \mathbb{E}[x_i x_i^H]$ of received snapshots $x_i \in \mathbb{C}^M$. After DoA estimation, the nodes collaboratively run a distributed beamnulling algorithm: each node $i$ chooses a complex weight vector $w_i \in \mathbb{C}^M$ that places nulls in the directions of identified interferers while maintaining unit gain toward intended neighbors, and these weights are iteratively updated across the network so that the joint pattern $\{w_i\}_{i=1}^N$ converges to a fixed point of the collective null-placement update map $T$.

Suppose an adversary injects jamming signals $s_a(t)$ from one or more locations and is able to shape $s_a(t)$ to mimic the waveform statistics of a chosen legitimate node, thereby contaminating the covariance estimates $R_i$ and influencing the DoA outputs and the inputs to $T$.

(a) Derive necessary and sufficient analytical conditions on (i) the jammer's transmit waveform second-order statistics, (ii) its spatial signature relative to legitimate nodes, and (iii) the array geometry and SNR, under which the adversary can cause each receiver's DoA estimator to either fail to detect a chosen legitimate transmitter or to produce a false DoA pointing at a chosen angle, with prescribed probability.

(b) Model the distributed beamnulling iteration as a discrete dynamical system $w^{(k+1)} = T(w^{(k)}; u^{(k)})$ where $u^{(k)}$ encodes adversarial perturbations to the DoA inputs. Determine feasibility criteria (in terms of the spectral properties of $T$, the perturbation budget $\|u^{(k)}\| \le \varepsilon$, and the network connectivity graph) under which an adversary can drive the trajectory $\{w^{(k)}\}$ toward a fixed point that nulls a maximal set of legitimate links, i.e. yields a maximally disconnected effective communication graph.

(c) Identify countermeasures — formulated as modifications of the update map $T$, of the DoA estimator, or of the protocol — that provably prevent convergence of the perturbed iteration to any fixed point whose induced communication graph is disconnected, and quantify the trade-off between robustness and beamforming gain.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning analytical feasibility criteria and countermeasures for adversarial DoA spoofing and distributed beamnulling attacks. Subsequent literature on adversarial beamforming, smart jamming of MUSIC/ESPRIT estimators, and resilient distributed null-steering has produced partial results in restricted models, but no comprehensive analytical characterization or provable countermeasure framework matching the full problem appears to have been established.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
original_question: How can real-time, distributed UAS formation-control algorithms minimize topological vulnerability to targeted jamming while retaining connectivity, especially when attack detection and localization may be unreliable and nodes must reform under mission-critical dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a network of $n$ mobile agents (e.g., unmanned aerial vehicles) operating in $\mathbb{R}^3$, whose positions $x_i(t)\in\mathbb{R}^3$ evolve according to single-integrator or double-integrator dynamics with bounded velocity and acceleration constraints. At each time $t$, the communication topology is modeled by a graph $G(t)=(V,E(t))$ where $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $(i,j)\in E(t)$ iff $\|x_i(t)-x_j(t)\|\le R$ for a fixed communication radius $R>0$. A targeted jamming attack is modeled as an adversary that, at time $t$, selects a set $S(t)\subseteq V$ of up to $k$ agents (or a spatial region of radius $\rho$) and removes all edges incident to $S(t)$ from $G(t)$; the attack set $S(t)$ is unknown to the agents and may only be partially observable through noisy local measurements (so detection and localization of the jammer are unreliable).

Define the topological vulnerability of $G(t)$ to $k$-targeted jamming as
$$V_k(G(t)) \;=\; \max_{S\subseteq V,\,|S|\le k}\bigl[\,c(G(t)) - c(G(t)\setminus S)\,\bigr],$$
where $c(\cdot)$ is a connectivity measure such as the algebraic connectivity $\lambda_2$ of the graph Laplacian, or the size of the largest connected component, and $G(t)\setminus S$ denotes removal of all edges incident to $S$.

Design a real-time distributed control law
$$\dot x_i(t) \;=\; u_i\bigl(\{x_j(t)\}_{j\in N_i(t)},\,m_i(t)\bigr),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where $N_i(t)$ is agent $i$'s current set of neighbors in $G(t)$ and $m_i(t)$ are local (possibly noisy or missing) attack-detection signals, such that:

(i) $G(t)$ remains connected for all $t\ge 0$ in the absence of attacks, and reconnects within a bounded reformation time after any attack;
(ii) the time-averaged vulnerability $\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T V_k(G(t))\,dt$ is minimized over admissible attack strategies $S(\cdot)$;
(iii) mission-level constraints (specified target waypoints or formation shapes for designated agents, kinematic limits, and inter-agent collision avoidance) are satisfied;
(iv) the law is fully distributed, requires no global knowledge of $S(t)$, and is robust to false positives and false negatives in the local detection signals $m_i(t)$.

Provide such an algorithm together with provable guarantees on the reformation time, the achieved vulnerability $V_k$, and the connectivity of $G(t)$, or establish fundamental impossibility/lower bounds relating $(n,k,R,\rho)$ to the achievable vulnerability and reformation time.
status_search_result: The problem of jointly minimizing topological vulnerability and ensuring distributed reformation under unreliable attack detection in UAV/multi-agent networks remains an active research direction. Subsequent work has produced partial results on resilient consensus (e.g., W-MSR-type filters), connectivity-preserving formation control, and robust graph design via algebraic connectivity maximization, but no general distributed algorithm with optimal vulnerability guarantees under unreliable jamming localization is established. The status appears to be open / partially addressed.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
context_brief: Security analysis of UAS routing mechanisms
original_question: How secure are proposed routing mechanisms for flying ad hoc or UAS networks that calculate paths in rapidly changing topologies under stringent latency constraints, and how should those methods be technically analyzed and compared for security-specific vulnerabilities rather than relying on inherited assumptions from MANET routing?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an unmanned aerial system (UAS) network, modeled as a flying ad hoc network (FANET): a finite set of mobile nodes (aerial vehicles) whose pairwise communication links evolve over time according to a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)), with high node mobility producing rapid topology changes and with strict end-to-end latency constraints on packet delivery. A routing mechanism is a distributed algorithm R that, at each time t and for each source–destination pair (s, d), computes a path P_R(s, d, t) ⊆ E(t) used to forward traffic.

Adopt a standard adversarial model in which an attacker controls a subset A ⊂ V of nodes (or can inject a bounded number of external nodes/links) and may perform routing-layer attacks such as black-hole, gray-hole, wormhole, sinkhole, Sybil, rushing, route falsification, and replay attacks. Define security metrics for R, for example:
  (i) packet delivery ratio under attack,
  (ii) probability that an attacker-controlled node lies on P_R(s, d, t),
  (iii) detection latency of malicious behavior,
  (iv) resilience to topology churn rate, defined as the maximum link-change rate per unit time tolerated while preserving (i)–(iii) above thresholds.

Problem. For the class of routing mechanisms proposed for FANET/UAS networks that compute paths in rapidly changing topologies under stringent latency constraints (as opposed to those designed for slower mobile ad hoc networks, MANETs), provide a rigorous, technical security analysis and comparison. Specifically:
  (a) Formalize a uniform threat model and a set of quantitative security metrics suitable to FANET conditions (high mobility, 3D topology, intermittent links, latency bounds).
  (b) For each candidate routing mechanism R, derive analytical or simulation-based bounds on the metrics (i)–(iv) under the threat model of (a), without simply inheriting security assumptions or guarantees established for MANET routing protocols.
  (c) Identify which mechanisms, if any, satisfy a prescribed security level (e.g., delivery ratio ≥ 1 − ε under up to k compromised nodes within latency L) and characterize the trade-offs between latency, mobility tolerance, and security.

Either exhibit such an analysis and comparison, or prove fundamental impossibility results showing that no FANET routing mechanism in a given class can simultaneously meet specified latency and security thresholds under the stated adversary.
status_search_result: The question is a broad open research challenge in UAS/FANET network security rather than a settled mathematical theorem. Surveys on FANET routing security through the mid-2020s continue to call for unified threat models and comparative security analyses of FANET-specific routing protocols, indicating the problem remains open.

paper_title: Cyber-Physical Attacks on UAS Networks–Challenges and Open Research Problems
context_brief: Routing convergence disruption in UAS networks
original_question: Can adversaries feasibly prevent or slow routing convergence in UAS networks by combining topological perturbation, jamming or adaptive-formation exploitation, and manipulation of node geographical-position knowledge, and what countermeasures can protect convergence in hostile airborne-network environments?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a network of unmanned aerial systems (UAS) modeled as a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)), where V is a set of mobile airborne nodes and E(t) is the set of communication links at time t, determined by node positions and a communication-range/channel model. Each node executes a mobile routing protocol that depends on (i) the current topology, (ii) channel availability, and (iii) reported geographical positions {p_i(t)}_{i in V} of all nodes (e.g., as required by position-based routing schemes), and that is designed to converge—within bounded time T*—to a routing state in which every source-destination pair has a valid forwarding path.

Suppose an adversary may simultaneously employ the following capabilities, subject to a budget B that bounds the total magnitude or rate of adversarial actions:
1. Topological perturbation: forcing a subset of nodes to alter their positions or links via exploitation of an adaptive formation-control mechanism (e.g., injecting bounded false control inputs that cause prescribed displacements of cooperating nodes).
2. Jamming: rendering a chosen subset J(t) ⊆ E(t) of links unusable during chosen time intervals.
3. Position-knowledge manipulation: replacing the reported positions p_i(t) of nodes in a chosen subset S ⊆ V by adversarially chosen values \tilde p_i(t) within an allowable deviation bound.

Formalize the following questions:

(a) Feasibility. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on (G(t), the routing protocol, the formation-control law, and the adversarial budget B) under which the adversary can construct a joint strategy combining (1)–(3) that prevents convergence of the routing protocol indefinitely, or that increases its convergence time beyond any prescribed multiple of T*.

(b) Quantitative lower bounds. Derive, as a function of B and structural parameters of G(t), a tight lower bound on the worst-case convergence time achievable by the adversary.

(c) Countermeasures. Design and prove correctness/optimality of a routing or control mechanism (possibly using authenticated position reporting, robust consensus, redundancy, or detection of formation-control anomalies) that guarantees convergence within a bounded time for every adversarial strategy of budget at most B, or characterize the maximal B for which such guarantees are achievable.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a forward-looking research challenge concerning the feasibility of combined topology, jamming, and position-spoofing attacks on routing convergence in airborne networks, and corresponding countermeasures. While related subproblems (jamming-resilient routing, secure geographic routing, formation-control attack detection) have been studied individually, no comprehensive feasibility characterization or optimal countermeasure for the combined attack model on UAS routing convergence has been established. The overall problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
context_brief: Intrinsic meaning of the corrected form-to-section map
original_question: What is the geometric meaning of the construction that sends a smooth differential k-form on a Riemannian manifold, together with the Levi-Civita connection, to two global sections J+ and J− of the chiral de Rham complex using local expressions built from the inverse metric, Christoffel symbols, Bessel-polynomial coefficients, ∂γ terms, and the local generators e_i^±? Equivalently, can the corrected normally ordered formula that glues local expressions into global chiral-de Rham sections be characterized by a more intrinsic geometric construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold equipped with the Levi-Civita connection, with Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$ in local coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$, and let $g^{ij}$ denote the inverse metric. Let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ be the chiral de Rham complex of $M$, the sheaf of vertex superalgebras locally generated, on a coordinate chart with coordinates $\gamma^i$ and conjugate fields $b_i,\varphi^i,\psi_i$ (bosonic and fermionic), in such a way that its weight-zero part recovers $\bigwedge^{\bullet} T^*M$. Define local odd generators
$$e_i^{\pm} \;=\; \psi_i \;\pm\; g_{ij}\,\varphi^{j},$$
and consider, for each smooth $k$-form $\omega \in C^{\infty}(M,\bigwedge^{k} T^*M)$ written locally as
$$\omega = \sum \omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\, dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k},$$
the local expressions
$$J^{\pm}(\omega) \;=\; :\!\omega_{i_1\dots i_k}\,e^{\pm}_{i_1}\cdots e^{\pm}_{i_k}\!: \;+\; (\text{correction terms}),$$
where the correction terms are normally ordered polynomials whose coefficients are given by Bessel-polynomial numbers and involve contractions of $g^{ij}$ with $\Gamma^{l}_{jk}\,\partial\gamma^{m}$ insertions, one such correction being inserted for every increase of two in the form-degree, so that on overlaps of charts the local pieces glue to globally defined sections of $\Omega^{ch}_M$, yielding two embeddings of sheaves of graded vector spaces
$$\bigwedge^{\bullet} T^*M \;\hookrightarrow\; \Omega^{ch}_M,\qquad \omega \mapsto J^{\pm}(\omega).$$

Problem: Provide an intrinsic geometric (coordinate-free) characterization of the maps $\omega \mapsto J^{\pm}(\omega)$. In particular, identify a natural construction—formulated solely in terms of $(M,g)$, the Levi-Civita connection, and the canonical structures of the chiral de Rham complex (such as its $N=1$ or $N=2$ supersymmetric vertex algebra structure, the de Rham/Dirac-type currents, or related geometric operators)—that produces the global sections $J^{\pm}(\omega)$ from $\omega$ without recourse to the explicit local formulas with Bessel-polynomial coefficients and $\Gamma^{l}_{jk} g^{jk}\partial\gamma^{l}$ correction terms.
status_search_result: A web search for follow-up work on the geometric meaning of the corrected form-to-section embeddings into the chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds returns the original constructions (Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine and related works on special holonomy and twisted/exotic versions) but no source providing an intrinsic, coordinate-free characterization of the map $\omega\mapsto J^{\pm}$ with Bessel-polynomial corrections. The question therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
context_brief: N=1 superconformal algebra generated by global G±
original_question: Whenever the local sections G+ and G− given by the curved formula with metric and Christoffel-symbol correction terms glue to global sections of the smooth chiral de Rham complex Ω_ch(M), do they generate two commuting copies of the N=1 superconformal algebra with central charge c = (3/2) dim_R M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of real dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb R}M$, and let $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$ denote the smooth chiral de Rham complex of $M$ (the sheaf of vertex superalgebras on $M$ obtained by gluing the local free $bc\beta\gamma$ vertex superalgebras associated with coordinate charts of $M$, using the smooth structure rather than the holomorphic one).

In a local coordinate chart with coordinates $x^i$, generators $b_i,c^i$ (odd) and $\beta_i,\gamma^i$ (even), and with the metric $g_{ij}$ and Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^k_{ij}$ of the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, define two local odd sections
$$G^+ = g_{ij}\,c^i\,\partial\gamma^j + \tfrac{1}{?}\,\Gamma\text{-correction terms},\qquad G^- = g^{ij}\,b_i\,\beta_j + \tfrac{1}{?}\,\Gamma\text{-correction terms},$$
given by the standard curved formulas in which the Christoffel-symbol correction terms render $G^\pm$ tensorial.

Suppose that for the given $(M,g)$ these local expressions $G^+$ and $G^-$ glue to globally defined sections of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$.

Question: Do $G^+$ and $G^-$ then generate, inside the vertex superalgebra of global sections of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$, two mutually commuting copies of the $N=1$ superconformal (Neveu–Schwarz) vertex algebra, each of central charge
$$c = \tfrac{3}{2}\,\dim_{\mathbb R} M\,?$$

paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
original_question: For a G2-holonomy manifold, after constructing a BRST-type cohomology of the smooth chiral de Rham complex with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces, what is the character of that cohomology, does it provide an analog of the elliptic genus for G2 manifolds, and does the resulting series converge and have modular properties?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact 7-manifold with holonomy group contained in $G_2$. Associated to $M$ is the smooth chiral de Rham complex $\Omega^{ch}(M)$, a sheaf of topological vertex algebras with a conformal grading by $L_0$-eigenvalues whose space of global sections $H = \Gamma(M, \Omega^{ch}(M))$ carries the action of an extended chiral algebra associated with $G_2$ holonomy. In particular, $H$ admits a distinguished odd "BRST-type" operator $Q^-_0$ with $(Q^-_0)^2 = 0$ and two commuting Virasoro fields $T^+$ and $X^+$ whose zero modes $L^+_0, X^+_0$ commute with $Q^-_0$.

Suppose one constructs the cohomology $\mathcal{H}(M) := H(H, Q^-_0)$ in such a way that each $L^+_0$-conformal-weight subspace of $\mathcal{H}(M)$ is finite-dimensional. Define the formal series
$$\chi_M(\tau) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{L^+_0}, \qquad q = e^{2\pi i \tau},$$
where $\mathrm{str}$ is the supertrace with respect to the fermionic grading, and the two-variable refinement
$$\chi_M(\tau, z) = q^{-21/48}\,\mathrm{str}_{\mathcal{H}(M)}\, q^{L^+_0} y^{X^+_0}, \qquad y = e^{2\pi i z},$$
obtained from the joint eigenspace decomposition under $L^+_0$ and $X^+_0$.

Determine $\chi_M(\tau)$ (and $\chi_M(\tau,z)$) explicitly in terms of topological invariants of $M$. Establish whether $\chi_M$ provides a $G_2$-analog of the elliptic genus, whether the series converges on the upper half plane $\{\Im\tau > 0\}$, and whether it possesses modular transformation properties under an appropriate subgroup of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (or, in the two-variable case, suitable Jacobi-modular properties).
category_tag: Chiral de Rham complex and G2 elliptic genus
status_search_result: Web searches on G2-manifold elliptic genera arising from the chiral de Rham complex did not surface a definitive computation of the character of the BRST cohomology of the smooth chiral de Rham complex on a G2 manifold, nor a proof of convergence and modularity of the associated supertrace. Related results exist for Calabi–Yau and generalized Calabi–Yau manifolds and for global sections on curves and locally symmetric spaces, but the G2 case appears to remain open.

context_brief: Spin(7) elliptic genus as topological-twist graded dimension
original_question: For a Spin(7)-holonomy manifold M, is its elliptic genus equal to the graded dimension of the BRST/topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) constructed from the conjectural left-moving SV^Spin7 structure, with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact $8$-dimensional manifold with holonomy group $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$, and let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ denote its chiral de Rham complex, viewed as a sheaf of vertex superalgebras whose space of global sections (using a smooth model) is $C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M)$. Assume that the parallel $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-invariant 4-form on $M$ induces, inside this vertex superalgebra, an action of the Shatashvili–Vafa $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ superconformal vertex algebra $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$, generated by the Virasoro field $L$, an $N=1$ supercurrent, and the additional currents associated with the $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ structure. Let $Q^-_0$ be the zero mode of the BRST current arising from the topological twist of the left-moving $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$ algebra (the standard $A$-type twist analogue for the Shatashvili–Vafa $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ algebra), so that $(Q^-_0)^2 = 0$, and form the cohomology
$$H\bigl(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),\,Q^-_0\bigr).$$
Let $c$ denote the central charge of the left-moving copy of $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$ and let $L_0$ be the energy operator. Decide whether the following statements hold:
(a) The graded dimension
$$\mathrm{tr}_{H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),\,Q^-_0)}\, q^{L_0 - c/24}$$
is well-defined, i.e.\ each conformal-weight eigenspace of $H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),\,Q^-_0)$ is finite-dimensional.
(b) This graded dimension equals the elliptic genus of $M$.
