paper_title: Unsolved problems in particle physics
original_question: At what momentum-transfer scales does perturbative QCD become reliable for exclusive hadronic observables such as pion form factors, and why do measurements up to roughly 2–4 GeV fail to show a clear approach to perturbative predictions?
self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD), exclusive hadronic observables such as the electromagnetic form factor $F_\pi(Q^2)$ of the pion and the pion–photon transition form factor $F_{\pi\gamma}(Q^2)$ are predicted, in the asymptotic limit $Q^2 \to \infty$, by collinear factorization theorems combined with perturbative QCD (pQCD). In particular, leading-order pQCD predicts $Q^2 F_\pi(Q^2) \to 8\pi \alpha_s(Q^2) f_\pi^2$ and $Q^2 F_{\pi\gamma}(Q^2) \to \sqrt{2}\, f_\pi$ (with $f_\pi \approx 92$ MeV the pion decay constant), with corrections governed by the pion light-cone distribution amplitude $\varphi_\pi(x,\mu)$ which evolves toward its asymptotic form $\varphi_\pi^{\rm asy}(x) = 6x(1-x)$.

Provide a quantitative answer to the following:

(a) Determine the threshold momentum-transfer scale $Q_*^2$ above which pQCD factorization gives reliable predictions for the exclusive form factors $F_\pi(Q^2)$ and $F_{\pi\gamma}(Q^2)$, in the sense that the leading-twist, leading-order pQCD result agrees with the true form factor to within a specified accuracy (e.g. 10\%) up to calculable higher-twist and higher-order corrections.

(b) Explain, in terms of the underlying nonperturbative structure (higher-twist contributions, transverse-momentum/end-point effects, the precise shape of $\varphi_\pi(x,\mu)$, and soft/Feynman mechanisms), why measured pion form factors in the momentum-transfer range $Q^2 \approx 2$–$4\ \mathrm{GeV}^2$ exhibit no clear convergence toward the asymptotic pQCD prediction, and quantify when convergence should set in.
category_tag: Perturbative QCD and exclusive form factors
status_search_result: The question of where perturbative QCD becomes quantitatively reliable for exclusive pion form factors remains an active and contested research topic. The BaBar–Belle tension in the pion–photon transition form factor has not been resolved: different theoretical approaches (nonlocal QCD sum rules, light-cone sum rules, dispersive analyses, intrinsic-transverse-momentum-enhanced pQCD) give conflicting conclusions and cannot simultaneously accommodate all data. Recent works (e.g., 2025) continue to propose mechanisms (such as iTMD-enhanced pQCD) to extend pQCD applicability down to a few GeV², but no consensus on the onset scale exists.

paper_title: Unsolved problems in particle physics
original_question: Can one prove that the continuum limit of lattice QCD exists, is independent of the way the lattice size tends to infinity and the lattice spacing tends to zero, and coincides with continuum QCD despite theoretical differences such as the treatment of instantons and chiral fermions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as a non-abelian gauge theory with gauge group SU(3) coupled to quark fields, formulated on a four-dimensional Euclidean hypercubic lattice $\Lambda_{a,L} = (a\mathbb{Z})^4 \cap [-L/2, L/2]^4$ with lattice spacing $a > 0$ and side length $L$. On such a lattice, gauge fields are realized as SU(3)-valued link variables, the gauge action is given by a Wilson-type plaquette action, and quark fields are realized by some lattice fermion discretization (e.g. Wilson, staggered, domain-wall, or overlap fermions). Let $\langle \mathcal{O} angle_{a,L}$ denote the expectation values of gauge-invariant local observables computed in this lattice theory with bare couplings tuned along a renormalization-group trajectory.

Prove the following:

1. (Existence of the continuum limit.) The limit
$$\langle \mathcal{O} \rangle_{\mathrm{cont}} \;=\; \lim_{\substack{a \to 0 \\ L \to \infty}} \langle \mathcal{O} \rangle_{a,L}$$
exists for all gauge-invariant local observables $\mathcal{O}$.

2. (Independence of the limiting procedure.) The limit does not depend on the joint manner in which $a \to 0$ and $L \to \infty$, nor on the choice of lattice fermion discretization, provided the bare parameters are tuned along an appropriate renormalization-group trajectory.

3. (Agreement with continuum QCD.) The resulting collection of correlation functions defines a quantum field theory satisfying the Osterwalder–Schwinger axioms whose Wightman functions coincide with those of continuum QCD, despite the structural differences between the lattice and the continuum formulations (for example, the fact that continuum instantons giving rise to nontrivial vacuum topology are not always stable lattice configurations, and that the implementation of chiral fermions on the lattice requires non-trivial constructions such as the Ginsparg–Wilson relation).
category_tag: Lattice gauge theory and continuum limit of QCD
status_search_result: The rigorous construction of four-dimensional non-abelian Yang–Mills theory (and QCD) and the proof that lattice regularizations have a well-defined continuum limit equivalent to a continuum quantum field theory satisfying the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schwinger axioms remains one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems and is widely regarded as open. No accepted solution exists; partial progress includes constructions in lower dimensions, results on stochastic quantization, and recent work by Chatterjee and others on lattice gauge theory, but the full continuum-limit problem for QCD is unresolved.

paper_title: Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities
original_question: Given positive semidefinite matrices A and B and positive real numbers p and q, is it always true for every unitarily invariant norm that |||A^(p+q)+B^(p+q)||| ≤ |||(A^p+B^p)(A^q+B^q)|||? The paper notes that one may reduce without loss of generality to 0≤p≤1 and q=1-p by absorbing the (p+q)-th powers into A and B.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A, B$ be positive semidefinite complex matrices of the same size, and let $p, q > 0$ be real numbers. A norm $\vertiii{\cdot}$ on the space of complex matrices is said to be unitarily invariant if $\vertiii{UXV} = \vertiii{X}$ for all matrices $X$ and all unitary matrices $U, V$ of compatible sizes. Determine whether the inequality
$$\vertiii{A^{p+q} + B^{p+q}} \;\le\; \vertiii{(A^p + B^p)(A^q + B^q)}$$
holds for every unitarily invariant norm $\vertiii{\cdot}$, every pair of positive semidefinite matrices $A, B$, and all $p, q > 0$. (By absorbing the $(p+q)$-th powers into $A$ and $B$, the question reduces without loss of generality to the case $0 \le p \le 1$ and $q = 1-p$.)
status_search_result: The inequality, posed by Bourin, remains open in full generality. Affirmative answers are known in several special cases: for the trace norm and Hilbert–Schmidt norm (Hayajneh–Kittaneh), for commuting positive semidefinite matrices and all unitarily invariant norms (Audenaert), and for parameters $p \in [1/4, 3/4]$ (Kittaneh–Ricard). Recent work (2022–2024) extends these partial results to noncommutative symmetric spaces and $\tau$-measurable operators, but the general matrix conjecture is not fully resolved.

paper_title: Some Open Problems in Topological Algebra
original_question: If G is a bounded semitopological group, or more generally a bounded quasitopological group, must G have countable cellularity? Here a semitopological group is a group whose topology is invariant under both left and right shifts, a quasitopological group is a semitopological group with continuous inversion, and bounded means both left bounded and right bounded.
self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A semitopological group is a group $G$ equipped with a topology such that for every $a\in G$ both left translation $x\mapsto ax$ and right translation $x\mapsto xa$ are continuous (equivalently, multiplication is separately continuous). A quasitopological group is a semitopological group in which the inversion map $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ is also continuous. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called left bounded if for every neighborhood $U$ of the identity $e$ there exists a finite subset $F\subseteq G$ such that $A\subseteq FU$; right bounded is defined symmetrically with $A\subseteq UF$. The group $G$ is called bounded if $G$ itself is both left bounded and right bounded. The cellularity (Souslin number) of a topological space $X$ is the supremum of cardinalities of families of pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of $X$; $X$ has countable cellularity if this supremum is at most $\aleph_0$.

Question. Must every bounded semitopological group have countable cellularity? More generally, must every bounded quasitopological group have countable cellularity?
status_search_result: Web search did not return a published resolution of Protasov's question on whether bounded semi/quasitopological groups must have countable cellularity. The problem appears in surveys on topological algebra and combinatorics of groups, but no source explicitly affirms or refutes it; the current status is unclear.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: How can closure approximations for time-dependent one- and two-body reduced density matrices be designed so that the propagated density matrices remain positive semidefinite and also satisfy fermionic occupation constraints, meaning natural orbital occupation numbers stay between zero and one, while avoiding unphysical negative local densities or divergent densities during electron dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-electron quantum system whose state is described by a sequence of reduced density matrices (RDMs). For p = 1, 2, the p-body reduced density matrix γ_p(t) is the trace over N − p particles of the full N-fermion density operator, regarded as a self-adjoint operator on the antisymmetric p-particle Hilbert space. The exact time evolution of {γ_p}_{p=1,...,N} is governed by the BBGKY hierarchy

  i ∂_t γ_p(t) = [H_p, γ_p(t)] + Tr_{p+1}[V_{p,p+1}, γ_{p+1}(t)],

which couples γ_p to γ_{p+1}. A "closure" at the two-body level is any prescription γ_3 ≈ Φ[γ_1, γ_2] that produces a closed system of evolution equations for (γ_1(t), γ_2(t)).

Required physical constraints to be preserved for all t ≥ 0 along the closed evolution:

(i) Positive semidefiniteness: γ_1(t) ⪰ 0 and γ_2(t) ⪰ 0 as operators.
(ii) Fermionic occupation bounds: every eigenvalue n_i(t) of γ_1(t) (the natural occupation number) satisfies 0 ≤ n_i(t) ≤ 1.
(iii) Physical local densities: the diagonal ρ(x,t) := γ_1(x,x;t) remains nonnegative and finite (no negative or divergent local densities) throughout the dynamics.
(iv) Consistency between γ_1 and γ_2: γ_1(t) = (N − 1)^{-1} Tr_2 γ_2(t) and the appropriate trace normalization is preserved.

Problem. Construct a nontrivial closure functional Φ[γ_1, γ_2] (going beyond the trivial mean-field/Hartree–Fock factorization) such that the resulting closed evolution equations for (γ_1(t), γ_2(t)) provably preserve conditions (i)–(iv) for arbitrary admissible initial data and for general one- and two-body Hamiltonian terms describing electron dynamics. Equivalently, identify structural conditions on Φ that are sufficient to guarantee these preservation properties, or prove that no such closure exists within a specified class.
status_search_result: No closure approximation for the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy at the 1- and 2-RDM level is known to provably preserve positive semidefiniteness together with the fermionic occupation-number bounds 0 ≤ n_i ≤ 1 and nonnegative local densities throughout electron dynamics. Recent literature on N-representability and 2-RDM methods (variational SDP-based ground-state methods, machine-learning approaches, and contracted Schrödinger-equation methods) addresses related representability constraints but does not provide a general dynamical closure with these guarantees, indicating the problem remains open.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
original_question: Can a variational or related time-propagation method impose positive semidefiniteness on the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3), and on the resulting one- and two-body reduced density matrices γ and Γ, despite the fact that approximate truncation can break the trace relations connecting these density matrices?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of N identical fermions evolving under a time-dependent many-body Hamiltonian. For each time t, let Γ^{(p)}(t) denote the p-body reduced density matrix (p-RDM), defined as the partial trace over N−p particles of the full N-body density operator, with normalization Tr Γ^{(p)} = N!/(N−p)!. Write γ := Γ^{(1)} and Γ := Γ^{(2)}. The time evolutions of γ, Γ, and Γ^{(3)} are linked by the BBGKY-type hierarchy, in which the equation of motion for Γ^{(p)} depends on Γ^{(p+1)}. Truncating this hierarchy at the three-body level requires approximating Γ^{(3)} as a functional of γ and Γ; such approximations generically break the exact contraction (trace) identities

  Tr_{p+1} Γ^{(p+1)} = (N−p) Γ^{(p)},

so that even if the approximate Γ^{(3)} is positive semidefinite, the propagated γ and Γ need not be.

Problem. Devise a variational (or otherwise constrained) time-propagation scheme for the truncated BBGKY hierarchy at the three-body level which, for all t ≥ 0, maintains simultaneously:

 (i) Γ^{(3)}(t) ⪰ 0,
 (ii) Γ(t) ⪰ 0, and
 (iii) γ(t) ⪰ 0,

despite the fact that the contraction identities relating Γ^{(3)}, Γ, and γ may fail under the chosen truncation. Equivalently, determine whether positive semidefiniteness of all three reduced density matrices can be enforced as a dynamical constraint along the evolution, and exhibit such a method, or prove that no such scheme can exist within a specified class of approximations.

status_search_result: Subsequent work on time-dependent 2RDM methods has addressed the positive-semidefiniteness/N-representability issue partially via purification schemes (e.g., projective purification of correlated RDMs and TD2RDM stabilization), which restore N-representability of the 2RDM in many regimes. However, a fully variational time-propagation method that simultaneously enforces positive semidefiniteness of Γ^{(3)}, Γ, and γ under generic three-body truncations does not appear to be definitively established; the issue remains an active research direction.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Extension beyond the Hubbard-model test case
original_question: Do the instability, density-divergence, and fermionic-constraint-violation phenomena observed for BBGKY truncations in a finite Hubbard model persist in small molecules and more complex correlated-electron systems, and how can the proposed partial remedies be validated in those settings?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of N interacting fermions evolving under a (possibly time-dependent) Hamiltonian, and let ρ_p(t) denote the p-body reduced density matrix at time t. The exact dynamics is governed by the BBGKY hierarchy, in which the time evolution of ρ_p couples to ρ_{p+1}. A standard truncation closes the hierarchy at second order by approximating ρ_3 as a functional of ρ_1 and ρ_2 (e.g., via cluster-expansion-type ansätze that preserve particle number and total energy), yielding coupled equations of motion for ρ_1(t) and ρ_2(t).

When this truncated scheme is applied to the few-site Hubbard model (a finite lattice with on-site Coulomb repulsion U and nearest-neighbor hopping), three pathologies have been documented:
(i) numerical/dynamical instability of the propagation;
(ii) divergence of local densities at finite times;
(iii) violation of the N-representability/fermionic constraints, namely the requirement that ρ_2 (and the contracted ρ_1) remain Hermitian, antisymmetric, positive semidefinite, and satisfy the correct partial-trace and eigenvalue bounds (0 ≤ eigenvalues of ρ_1 ≤ 1).

Several partial remedies have been proposed, including purification/positivity-restoration projections of ρ_2 during propagation and modified closure functionals designed to enforce contraction consistency.

Question: Do the three pathologies (i)–(iii) above persist when the same BBGKY truncation schemes are applied to genuine small-molecule electronic systems (i.e., ab initio Hamiltonians for atoms and small molecules with realistic Coulomb interactions and basis sets) and to other complex correlated-electron systems beyond the Hubbard test case? Furthermore, can the proposed partial remedies be rigorously validated as cures (or systematic mitigations) of these pathologies in those more general settings?
category_tag: BBGKY hierarchy and reduced density matrices
status_search_result: The phenomena (instability, density divergence, and N-representability violations) are documented for BBGKY truncations in finite Hubbard test systems, and preliminary indications suggest similar issues arise in small molecules. Subsequent literature continues to investigate positivity-preserving and contraction-consistent closures for the time-dependent two-body reduced density matrix, but no comprehensive validation establishing that the proposed partial remedies cure these pathologies across small molecules and general correlated-electron systems has been found. The question therefore appears still open.

original_question: How can the BBGKY reduced-density-matrix approach be developed in linear response theory for optical spectra, where nonlinearities in the time-dependent hierarchy are removed by construction and may therefore avoid some of the divergence mechanisms seen in nonlinear propagation?
category_tag: BBGKY hierarchy and reduced density matrices
status_search_result: The problem of building linear-response BBGKY truncations for optical spectra that avoid the divergences known in nonlinear time-dependent reduced-density-matrix propagation is a programmatic open research direction. Standard low-order linear-response schemes (RPA, second RPA) exist, but a systematic linear-response BBGKY truncation with proven boundedness, sum-rule preservation, and a controlled spectrum at general order p_0 has not been established in the literature, and work in this direction is described as ongoing without a definitive resolution.

paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
context_brief: Reliability of propagating only the second BBGKY equation
original_question: Is it possible to make propagation based only on the second BBGKY equation for the two-body reduced density matrix into a generally reliable approach, given that approximate closures can produce large total-energy fluctuations and can still diverge even when compatibility between the first and second hierarchy equations is no longer the immediate issue?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite, non-relativistic many-fermion quantum system whose state is described by a time-dependent density matrix on Fock space. For each integer $p\ge 1$, let $ho_p(t)$ denote the $p$-body reduced density matrix obtained by partial trace, normalized so that $\mathrm{Tr}\,ho_p =  inom{N}{p}$ where $N$ is the particle number. With a Hamiltonian containing one-body kinetic terms and a two-body interaction, the time-dependent reduced density matrices satisfy the BBGKY hierarchy
$$ i\hbar\,\partial_t ho_p(t) = [H_p,ho_p(t)] + \mathrm{Tr}_{p+1} igl[V_{p,p+1},ho_{p+1}(t) igr], $$
which couples $ho_p$ to $ho_{p+1}$. A "second-equation propagation scheme" consists of choosing a closure functional $ho_3[ho_1,ho_2]$ (e.g. cumulant expansions, the 3b-NIA approximation, or weak-coupling/WC truncations) and then evolving only $ho_2(t)$ via
$$ i\hbar\,\partial_t ho_2(t) = [H_2,ho_2(t)] + \mathrm{Tr}_{3} igl[V_{2,3},\,ho_3[ho_1(t),ho_2(t)] igr], $$
with $ho_1(t)$ obtained by contraction from $ho_2(t)$.

It is known that for typical closures (i) the total energy $E(t)=\mathrm{Tr}(Hho(t))$, while formally conserved, can in numerical simulations exhibit large fluctuations in time, and (ii) the propagated $ho_2(t)$ may fail to remain positive semidefinite or representable, leading to divergences in finite time, even in regimes where the compatibility relation $ho_1 = 	frac{1}{N-1}\mathrm{Tr}_2 ho_2$ between the first and second hierarchy levels is not violated.

Problem. Determine whether there exists a closure $ho_3[ho_1,ho_2]$ such that the resulting second-equation propagation scheme is generally reliable, in the sense that for a broad class of finite fermionic systems and initial data the propagated $ho_2(t)$ (a) remains positive semidefinite and $N$-representable for all $t\ge 0$, (b) conserves total energy with bounded long-time fluctuations, and (c) does not diverge in finite time. Equivalently, either construct such a closure together with a proof of these properties, or prove that no closure depending only on $ho_1$ and $ho_2$ can simultaneously satisfy (a)–(c) uniformly.
status_search_result: No published resolution was identified. The reliability of two-body BBGKY truncation schemes for time-dependent reduced density matrices remains an active research problem in many-body quantum dynamics, with ongoing work on cumulant closures, N-representability constraints, and energy conservation, but no general construction or impossibility result is known.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is unimodal.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_r]$. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite, nonempty collection of monomials in $R$ such that whenever $M \in X$ and $N$ divides $M$, then $N \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is called pure if all of its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same degree. The pure $O$-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ counts the monomials of degree $i$ in $X$ and $e$ is the common degree of the maximal monomials. Equivalently, pure $O$-sequences coincide with the Hilbert functions of Artinian level monomial $k$-algebras. The codimension of $h$ is $h_1$, and the type of $h$ is $h_e$ (the number of maximal monomials, equivalently the socle dimension of the corresponding level algebra). The sequence $h$ is unimodal if there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

Problem. For each fixed integer $r \ge 1$, determine the largest integer $t = t(r)$ with the property that every pure $O$-sequence of codimension $r$ and type $t$ is unimodal.
status_search_result: The general problem of determining, for fixed codimension $r$, the largest type $t$ guaranteeing unimodality of pure $O$-sequences remains open. Partial results are known: pure $O$-sequences of codimension $\le 2$ are always unimodal; in codimension 3, type 2 is unimodal (over any field), and Boyle (Illinois J. Math., 2014) proved unimodality for type 3 in three variables. Non-unimodal examples in codimension 3 are known starting at relatively large types (e.g., type 14), but the precise threshold is not established. No general formula or value for $t(r)$ for $r \ge 3$ has been determined.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Determine the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4.
self_contained_problem:
A pure order ideal is a finite, nonempty collection X of monomials in a polynomial ring k[y_1,...,y_r] (over a field k) that is closed under divisibility (if m ∈ X and m' divides m, then m' ∈ X) and whose maximal monomials with respect to divisibility all have the same total degree. The pure O-sequence associated to X is the integer vector h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e), where h_i is the number of monomials of total degree i in X. The integer e is called the socle degree of h, and r is called its codimension. The sequence h is unimodal if there is an index j with h_0 ≤ h_1 ≤ ... ≤ h_j ≥ h_{j+1} ≥ ... ≥ h_e; otherwise it is nonunimodal.

Determine the smallest positive integer r such that there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence h = (1, h_1, h_2, h_3, h_4) of socle degree 4 and codimension r.
status_search_result: Web searches surface the survey listing this as an open problem and related work on pure O-sequences and on Gorenstein h-vectors (Stanley's (1,13,12,13,1) example shows codimension 13 suffices in the more restrictive Gorenstein/symmetric case). No source located states a resolution of the pure O-sequence version specifically for socle degree 4. Status appears unresolved based on available search evidence.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Determine the smallest number n of variables for which there exists a nonunimodal pure f-vector, equivalently a nonunimodal f-vector of a pure simplicial complex. The paper notes this after recalling Stanley's original nonunimodal example and later bounds for special cases.
self_contained_problem:
A simplicial complex Δ on vertex set {1,2,…,n} is called pure if all of its facets (inclusion-maximal faces) have the same dimension. Its f-vector is f(Δ)=(f_{-1},f_0,f_1,…,f_{d}), where f_i is the number of i-dimensional faces of Δ and d=dim Δ. A finite sequence (a_0,a_1,…,a_d) of nonnegative integers is called unimodal if there exists an index j with a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_j ≥ a_{j+1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_d, and nonunimodal otherwise.

Determine the smallest positive integer n such that there exists a pure simplicial complex on n vertices whose f-vector (f_0,f_1,…,f_d) is nonunimodal.
status_search_result: No source establishes the exact minimum number of vertices needed for a nonunimodal pure f-vector. Known partial results give a sharp lower bound of n=328 in the Cohen–Macaulay socle-degree-5 case (Tahat) and examples with n as low as 39 in higher socle degree, but the general pure case remains unresolved in the literature found.

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? More generally, for each fixed codimension, which socle types force unimodality of all pure O-sequences in that codimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite, nonempty set of monomials of $R$ such that whenever $M \in X$ and $N$ is a monomial dividing $M$, also $N \in X$. The order ideal $X$ is called pure of type $t$ if the set of maximal monomials of $X$ (those not properly dividing any other element of $X$) has cardinality $t$ and all of these maximal monomials have the same degree. The pure O-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$, where $h_i$ is the number of monomials of $X$ of degree $i$ and $e$ is the common degree of the maximal monomials; equivalently, pure O-sequences are exactly the Hilbert functions of monomial Artinian level algebras. The codimension of $h$ is $r$ (the number of variables actually appearing). A finite sequence $(h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ of nonnegative integers is unimodal if there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

(a) Prove or disprove: every pure O-sequence of type $2$ is unimodal, in arbitrary codimension $r$.

(b) More generally, for each fixed codimension $r$, determine the set of socle types $t$ such that every pure O-sequence of codimension $r$ and type $t$ is unimodal.
status_search_result: The unimodality of all pure O-sequences of type 2 is established for codimensions r = 2, 3, and 4, but for arbitrary codimension (in particular r ≥ 5) the question appears to remain open. The general question of which (codimension, type) pairs force unimodality is still only partially understood: known positive cases include (r,1) for all r and (3,2), (3,3), (4,2), while non-unimodal examples exist for (r,t) with r ≥ 4 and certain t. Related log-concavity problems also remain open in case (3,2).

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4, 5, 21)? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?
self_contained_problem:
A Steiner system S(t, k, v) is a pair (X, B), where X is a set of v points and B is a collection of k-element subsets of X (called blocks), such that every t-element subset of X is contained in exactly one block of B. Equivalently, S(t, k, v) exists if and only if one can choose a family of k-subsets of a v-set such that every t-subset lies in exactly one chosen k-subset.

Question: Does there exist a Steiner system S(4, 5, 21)? That is, does there exist a collection B of 5-element subsets of a 21-element set X such that every 4-element subset of X is contained in exactly one member of B?

(Equivalently, in terms of pure O-sequences: a finite sequence (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) of positive integers is called a pure O-sequence if there exists a monomial Artinian level algebra A = R/I, with R = k[x_1, ..., x_n] over a field k and I a monomial ideal, whose Hilbert function equals (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) and whose socle is generated by monomials all of the same degree e. Determine whether the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) is a pure O-sequence.)
status_search_result: The existence of a Steiner system S(4,5,21) appears to remain open. Nonexistence has been established for S(4,5,15) and S(4,5,17), and v=21 is cited as the smallest open case. No source found establishing existence or nonexistence of S(4,5,21).

paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
original_question: Is every matroid h-vector a pure O-sequence? Equivalently, does Stanley's conjecture hold for all matroid complexes, beyond the low-dimensional cases proved in the paper and cited work?
self_contained_problem:
Let M be a (finite) matroid with ground set E, and let Δ(M) be its independence complex (the simplicial complex whose faces are the independent sets of M). Denote by h(M) = (h_0, h_1, …, h_d) the h-vector of Δ(M), defined from the f-vector (f_{-1}, f_0, …, f_{d-1}) of Δ(M) (where d = rank(M)) by

  Σ_{i=0}^{d} h_i t^i = Σ_{i=0}^{d} f_{i-1} t^i (1 - t)^{d-i}.

A finite, nonempty set X of monomials in the polynomial ring k[x_1, …, x_n] (k a field) is called an order ideal if it is closed under taking divisors: whenever m ∈ X and m' divides m, then m' ∈ X. The order ideal X is pure if all of its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same total degree. The pure O-sequence associated to a pure order ideal X is the vector (F_0, F_1, …, F_e), where F_i is the number of monomials in X of total degree i and e is the common degree of the maximal monomials.

Prove or disprove: for every matroid M, the h-vector h(M) is a pure O-sequence, i.e., there exists a pure order ideal X whose pure O-sequence equals h(M).
status_search_result: Stanley's 1977 conjecture that every matroid h-vector is a pure O-sequence remains open in general. It has been verified for several classes, including matroids of rank at most 3, co-rank at most 2, paving, cographic, cotransversal, and lattice path matroids, all matroids on at most nine elements, and (more recently, 2021–2023) positroids. No counterexample is known and no full proof exists.

paper_title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions
context_brief: Correlation bounds for low-degree F2 polynomials
original_question: Does there exist an explicit function f : F2^n -> F2, computable in NP, such that for every F2-polynomial p : F2^n -> F2 of degree at most log_2 n, the correlation satisfies |E_x[(-1)^{f(x)+p(x)}]| <= 1/n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ denote the field with two elements. For functions $f, g : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$, define their correlation by
$$\mathrm{Corr}(f,g) \;=\; \Big| \mathbb{E}_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n}\big[ (-1)^{f(x)+g(x)} \big] \Big|,$$
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. An $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial of degree at most $d$ is a polynomial $p(x_1,\dots,x_n) \in \mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i)$ such that every monomial involves at most $d$ variables.

Construct an explicit family of functions $\{f_n : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2\}_{n \ge 1}$, where "explicit" means that the language $\{(n,x) : f_n(x) = 1\}$ lies in the complexity class $\mathsf{NP}$, such that for all sufficiently large $n$ and for every $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial $p : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$ of degree at most $\log_2 n$,
$$\mathrm{Corr}(f_n, p) \;\le\; \frac{1}{n}.$$

Equivalently: exhibit such an explicit $f$ achieving correlation at most $1/n$ with every $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial of degree $\le \log_2 n$.
status_search_result: Proving a correlation bound of $1/n$ against $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomials of degree $\log_2 n$ for any explicit function remains a well-known open problem in circuit complexity. Recent surveys and papers (e.g., Viola's "Correlation bounds against polynomials" survey, and 2024–2025 works such as Ivanov–Pavlovic–Viola "On correlation bounds against polynomials" and Blasiok et al. on Fourier growth of structured $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomials) explicitly identify this as a central open question. The best known explicit correlation bounds for degree $\log n$ polynomials are still far from $1/n$ (often only $1/\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ or worse for specific structured classes).

paper_title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions
original_question: Fix a possibly infinite collection of affine constraints over F2, written as pairs (M_i, sigma_i) where each M_i is a matrix over F2 and sigma_i is a 0/1 pattern. For a single pair (M, sigma) with M in F2^{m x k} and sigma in {0,1}^k, say that f : F2^n -> {0,1} is (M, sigma)-free if there do not exist row vectors x^(1), ..., x^(k) in F2^n such that M X = 0 for X = (x^(1), ..., x^(k)) and f(x^(j)) = sigma_j for every j in [k]. For each n, let P_n be the property of functions f : F2^n -> {0,1} that are (M_i, sigma_i)-free for every i. Must P_n always have a one-sided-error, constant-query property-testing algorithm?
self_contained_problem:
Work over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_2$. For positive integers $m,k$, let $M\in\mathbb{F}_2^{m\times k}$ be a matrix and let $\sigma\in\{0,1\}^k$ be a pattern. Given $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{0,1\}$, say that $f$ is $(M,\sigma)$-free if there do not exist vectors $x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(k)}\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that, writing $X$ for the $k\times n$ matrix whose $j$-th row is $x^{(j)}$, one has $MX=0$ (the zero $m\times n$ matrix) and $f(x^{(j)})=\sigma_j$ for every $j\in\{1,\dots,k\}$.

Fix a possibly infinite collection $\{(M_i,\sigma_i)\}_{i\ge 1}$ of such pairs. For each $n\ge 1$, define $P_n$ to be the property of all functions $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{0,1\}$ that are $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free for every $i\ge 1$.

A property $P_n$ admits a one-sided-error, constant-query property-testing algorithm if there exists a function $q:(0,1)\to\mathbb{N}$ and a randomized algorithm that, given oracle access to $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{0,1\}$ and a parameter $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, queries $f$ at most $q(\varepsilon)$ times (independent of $n$), accepts with probability $1$ whenever $f\in P_n$, and rejects with probability at least $2/3$ whenever $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far in Hamming distance from every member of $P_n$.

Question: must the property $P_n$ defined above always admit such a one-sided-error, constant-query property-testing algorithm?
status_search_result: Subsequent work on linear-invariant property testing established the central conjecture in the area: a linear-invariant property of Boolean functions on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is testable (with one-sided error and constant query complexity) if and only if it is semi subspace-hereditary. Properties defined by forbidding induced affine constraints $(M_i,\sigma_i)$ as above are subspace-hereditary, and have been shown to admit one-sided constant-query testers, resolving the question affirmatively.

paper_title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions
context_brief: Gaussian simplex partitions and noise stability
original_question: Fix 0 <= rho <= 1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, where 3 <= q <= n+1, is the maximum noise stability at rho achieved by a standard simplex partition, meaning a partition A_1, ..., A_q satisfying A_i superseteq {x in R^n : <a_i,x> > <a_j,x> for every j != i} for unit vectors a_1, ..., a_q with <a_i,a_j> = -1/(q-1) whenever i != j? In addition, for -1 <= rho <= 0, does the standard simplex partition minimize noise stability at rho?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma_n$ denote the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. For $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the noise stability at level $\rho$ of a measurable partition $\{A_1,\dots,A_q\}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is
$$\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(A_1,\dots,A_q)=\sum_{i=1}^q \Pr[X\in A_i,\;Y\in A_i],$$
where $(X,Y)$ is a pair of jointly Gaussian random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_jY_k]=\rho\,\delta_{jk}$.

Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $q$ with $3\le q\le n+1$. A standard simplex partition of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a partition $\{A_1,\dots,A_q\}$ of equal Gaussian measure $\gamma_n(A_i)=1/q$ such that
$$A_i\supseteq\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle a_i,x\rangle>\langle a_j,x\rangle\text{ for all }j\ne i\},$$
where $a_1,\dots,a_q$ are unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $\langle a_i,a_j\rangle=-1/(q-1)$ for all $i\ne j$.

Prove or disprove the following two claims.

(a) For every $\rho\in[0,1]$, every measurable partition $\{A_1,\dots,A_q\}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\gamma_n(A_i)=1/q$ for all $i$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(A_1,\dots,A_q)\le \mathrm{Stab}_\rho(S_1,\dots,S_q),$$
where $\{S_1,\dots,S_q\}$ is a standard simplex partition.

(b) For every $\rho\in[-1,0]$, every measurable partition $\{A_1,\dots,A_q\}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\gamma_n(A_i)=1/q$ for all $i$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{Stab}_\rho(A_1,\dots,A_q)\ge \mathrm{Stab}_\rho(S_1,\dots,S_q).$$
status_search_result: The conjecture (the Standard Simplex Conjecture of Isaksson–Mossel) is partially resolved. The maximization part (a) is known for $q=3$ and $0<\rho<\rho_0(3,n)$ (Heilman, 2014). The minimization part (b), and the conjecture for unequal measures, was disproved by Heilman–Mossel–Nayar (2014/2016), who showed that standard simplex partitions are not the most noise stable when measures are unequal and that the minimization claim fails in general; the equal-measure maximization conjecture remains open in general.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: How can one formulate the thermodynamics of feedback-controlled systems in a way that explicitly accounts for the thermodynamic consequences of information transfer between the system and the controller, so that quantities such as entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency are treated within a consistent thermodynamic framework?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical or quantum thermodynamic system in contact with one or more heat reservoirs, together with an external controller (a "demon") that performs measurements on the system and applies a feedback protocol whose form depends on the measurement outcomes. Let the joint dynamics of system and controller be specified, with the controller possessing a memory register that stores measurement outcomes and is reset between protocol runs.

Develop a consistent thermodynamic framework for such feedback-controlled systems that explicitly incorporates the thermodynamic role of information transfer between the system and the controller. Concretely, the framework should:

1. Define the relevant information-theoretic quantities (e.g., the mutual information acquired by measurement and any QC-mutual or transfer-entropy-type generalizations) entering the thermodynamic balance.

2. Derive a generalized second law of the form
   ⟨ΔS_sys⟩ + ⟨ΔS_bath⟩ ≥ −I,
   (and the corresponding bound on extractable work ⟨W_ext⟩ ≤ −ΔF + k_B T · I) that holds for arbitrary feedback protocols, where I is the chosen information measure.

3. Establish a fluctuation theorem (Jarzynski/Crooks-type identity) for trajectories that incorporates the information exchanged between system and controller.

4. Account for the thermodynamic cost of the controller's measurement and memory erasure (Landauer's principle), so that the total entropy balance over system + controller + reservoirs is consistent with the ordinary second law.

5. Define and bound the efficiency of feedback-driven heat engines (e.g., Maxwell-demon-type cycles) in terms of the information acquired, identifying when and how the conventional Carnot bound is modified.

The problem is to construct such a framework in full generality (covering classical stochastic, classical Hamiltonian, and quantum settings, with discrete or continuous measurements and feedback) and to identify the tightest universal information-thermodynamic inequalities governing entropy reduction, extractable work, and efficiency.
status_search_result: A substantial information-thermodynamics framework has been developed since 2008. Sagawa and Ueda derived generalized second laws and Jarzynski-type fluctuation theorems incorporating mutual information for both classical and quantum feedback control, establishing bounds on extractable work and efficiency that account for measurement and erasure costs. Subsequent work (fluctuation theorems with information exchange, transfer-entropy bounds, experimental verification via the Maxwell-demon photon experiment, and recent results on universal validity of the second law of information thermodynamics, e.g. 2023–2024) has extended and refined these results. The core programme is thus largely realized, although fully general formulations (continuous measurement, strong coupling, non-Markovian and fully quantum regimes) remain active research areas, so the broader programme is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: Can the entropy-reduction results obtained for correlated repeated feedback actuation be applied or extended to derive quantitative bounds for additional performance measures of feedback-controlled systems, in particular the maximum attainable flux or the maximum attainable power?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled stochastic system in contact with a thermal reservoir at temperature T, whose dynamics are repeatedly modulated by a controller that performs successive measurements on the system and applies control protocols based on the measurement outcomes. Let the sequence of measurement outcomes be {m_1, m_2, …, m_N}, generally correlated across time, and let H({m_i}) denote the Shannon entropy of this sequence. Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, the entropy reduction of the system due to feedback obeys quantitative bounds expressed in terms of the mutual information (or Shannon entropy) of the correlated measurement record, and the minimum energetic cost of erasing the controller's memory imposes a corresponding limit on the maximum extractable work.

Question: Develop quantitative thermodynamic bounds, derived from (or extending) the entropy-reduction results for correlated repeated feedback actuation, on the following performance measures of such feedback-controlled systems:

(a) the maximum attainable steady-state probability flux J (e.g., the average net particle or charge current that the feedback can sustain across the system per unit time), and

(b) the maximum attainable power P (e.g., the rate of work extraction, or the rate of free-energy production, achievable by the feedback protocol).

Specifically, express upper bounds on J and P in terms of the temperature T, the rate of information acquisition by the controller (the entropy rate of the correlated measurement sequence), and the relevant timescales of the controlled dynamics, and determine the conditions under which these bounds are saturated.
status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem regarding the extension of entropy-reduction bounds for correlated repeated feedback to performance measures such as flux and power. While the field of stochastic thermodynamics with feedback has developed substantially, with various information-theoretic bounds (e.g., generalized Jarzynski/Sagawa–Ueda relations, thermodynamic uncertainty relations) emerging, it is not clear from the search whether the specific question of tight bounds on maximum attainable flux and power in correlated repeated feedback systems—as posed here—has been definitively resolved. Status remains unclear from available sources.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, can the general thermodynamic results of [13] be applied to determine the maximum entropy reduction these ratchets can achieve and to establish a full thermodynamic description of such systems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet: a Brownian particle in contact with a thermal bath at temperature $T$ moves in one dimension under a spatially periodic, asymmetric potential $V(x)$ that can be switched on and off in time. A controller observes the position of the particle (either continuously or at discrete sampling times) and, based on the measurement outcomes, decides whether to keep the potential on or off, with the aim of rectifying thermal fluctuations into directed motion.

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics for feedback-controlled systems, the second law must be modified to incorporate the information acquired by the controller: for a feedback protocol acting on a stochastic system, one has a generalized inequality of the form
$$\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle \le -\Delta F + k_B T\, I,$$
where $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle$ is the mean work extracted, $\Delta F$ is the free-energy change, and $I$ is an information-theoretic quantity (a mutual information / entropy reduction) characterizing the controller's measurements and actions. Equivalently, the entropy production of the controlled system is bounded below by $-I$, so $I$ plays the role of a maximum attainable "entropy reduction" induced by the feedback protocol.

Problem. Apply this general thermodynamic framework explicitly to the feedback flashing ratchet:
(a) Define the appropriate information quantity $I$ for an arbitrary measurement-and-switching protocol (continuous or discrete-time) acting on a flashing ratchet, taking into account the non-Markovian sequence of control actions generated by the controller.
(b) Determine the maximum entropy reduction $I_{\max}$ achievable by any such feedback protocol on the flashing ratchet, and exhibit (or bound) protocols saturating it.
(c) Use the result to give a complete thermodynamic description of feedback flashing ratchets, including tight upper bounds on extracted work, output power, and efficiency in terms of $I$, and identify the protocols that saturate these bounds.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has substantially developed the thermodynamic and information-theoretic description of feedback flashing ratchets. In particular, "Information in feedback ratchets" (Phys. Rev. E 108, 034112, 2023) computes the entropy reduction from the non-Markovian sequence of control actions and provides bounds (including a quasi-Markovian limit) on the entropy reduction, and a 2024 work gives a Markovian description of a class of feedback-controlled systems applied to the feedback flashing ratchet. These results realize much of the program (information quantity, bounds, role in the second law), although a fully tight characterization of the maximum attainable entropy reduction over all protocols is still being refined, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
context_brief: Implications for nano and biological systems
original_question: What concrete limitations do information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems impose on the operation and achievable performance of nanotechnology devices and biological systems in which one subsystem uses bidirectional interaction with another subsystem to improve that subsystem's performance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a composite stochastic system consisting of two interacting subsystems A and B, where B acts as a controller that observes A through a noisy measurement channel and applies a feedback action to A in order to improve some performance measure of A (for example, to extract work, reduce entropy, or stabilize a target state). Let I denote the mutual information acquired by B about A per unit time, let W denote the average work extracted (or analogous performance gain) by the feedback protocol, let ΔS denote the entropy production of the joint system, and let kT be the thermal energy scale. Generalized second-law inequalities of the Sagawa–Ueda type assert that the achievable performance is bounded by information-theoretic quantities, e.g. ⟨W⟩ ≤ −ΔF + kT·I, with related bounds on entropy reduction and control accuracy.

Problem: Derive the concrete, quantitative limitations that such information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for bidirectional feedback-controlled systems place on the operation and achievable performance of physical realizations relevant to nanotechnology devices and biological systems (e.g., molecular motors, ion channels, sensory adaptation networks, single-electron transistors with feedback). Specifically, identify the optimal trade-offs between (i) the rate of information acquisition by the controller, (ii) the energetic/dissipative cost of measurement and feedback, and (iii) the resulting performance gain of the controlled subsystem, and characterize attainability of these bounds in concrete model classes.
status_search_result: The general program of deriving information-thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems has seen substantial progress since 2012 (Sagawa–Ueda inequalities, thermodynamics of information, work extraction by Maxwell demons, bounds on biochemical sensing such as Lan–Sartori–Tu, thermodynamic uncertainty relations). However, the broad question of pinning down the concrete operational limitations these bounds impose on real nanoscale and biological devices, including attainability and tightness in physically realistic models, remains an active and largely open research direction with no single definitive resolution.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Topology of the admissible representation space
original_question: Fix a closed hyperbolic surface S of genus at least 2. Let Adm(S) be the space of admissible pairs (j,ρ) of representations π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) with j Fuchsian and such that the induced action on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact. How many connected components does Adm(S) have, and what is its topology?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, with fundamental group $\pi_1(S)$. Identify the three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ with the Lie group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ endowed with (a multiple of) its Killing form, so that the isometry group of $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ contains $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ acting by left and right multiplication.

A pair $(j,\rho)$ of representations $j,\rho : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is called admissible if:
(i) $j$ is Fuchsian, i.e. discrete and faithful; and
(ii) the diagonal action of $\pi_1(S)$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ defined by $\gamma \cdot x = j(\gamma)\, x\, \rho(\gamma)^{-1}$ is free, properly discontinuous, and cocompact.

Let $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ denote the space of all such admissible pairs $(j,\rho)$, equipped with the topology induced from $\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(S),\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R}))^2$.

Determine the number of connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ and describe its topology.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. Barbot (J. Diff. Geom. 2015, arXiv:1301.4309) showed that the connected component of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ containing Fuchsian pairs consists exactly of quasi-Fuchsian (Anosov) representations, extending earlier work of Barbot–Mérigot. Tholozan and subsequent authors have shown that $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ is disconnected and identified admissible representations distributed among multiple components (with counts of order $4g-5$ noted in related settings). However, a complete enumeration of the connected components of $\mathrm{Adm}(S)$ together with a full description of its topology does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Bending laminations determine GHMC AdS structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let M = S × R, and let l_- and l_+ be two measured laminations on S that fill S. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations exactly l_- and l_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $M$ contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$ and is maximal (with respect to isometric embeddings) among such spacetimes. Each GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ admits a convex core, the smallest non-empty closed convex subset whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence; when this convex core is not a totally geodesic surface, its boundary consists of two spacelike pleated surfaces (the "upper" and "lower" components), each carrying a transverse measured geodesic lamination on $S$, called the measured bending lamination. Two measured laminations $\ell_-, \ell_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every nontrivial simple closed curve $\gamma$ on $S$, the sum of geometric intersection numbers $i(\gamma, \ell_-) + i(\gamma, \ell_+)$ is strictly positive.

Question: Given any two measured laminations $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has $\ell_-$ as the measured bending lamination of its lower component and $\ell_+$ as the measured bending lamination of its upper component?
status_search_result: Existence of a GHMC AdS structure realizing a pair of filling measured laminations as bending laminations of the convex core boundary has been established (notably by Bonsante–Schlenker for small multiples, and further work on realization). Rigidity (uniqueness) near the Fuchsian locus has been obtained by Prosanov (JLMS 2026), but the full uniqueness statement for arbitrary filling pairs appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Convex-core boundary metrics determine GHMC structure
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let T be its Teichmüller space, and let m_- and m_+ be two points of T. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M = S × R such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of the convex core are m_- and m_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\mathcal{T}(S)$ denote its Teichmüller space, i.e., the space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structure on $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ is a Lorentzian metric $h$ on $M$ of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $(M,h)$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $S \times \{0\}$, the inclusion of any Cauchy surface induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and $(M,h)$ is maximal among such structures (it admits no isometric extension to a larger spacetime with the same property). Each such GHMC anti-de Sitter spacetime contains a convex core, the smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset that is a deformation retract of $M$; when the holonomy is not Fuchsian, the boundary of the convex core has two connected components, each a pleated spacelike surface whose induced metric is a hyperbolic metric on $S$, defining a point in $\mathcal{T}(S)$.

Question: Given any two points $m_-, m_+ \in \mathcal{T}(S)$, does there exist a unique GHMC anti-de Sitter structure $h$ on $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ (up to isotopy) such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of its convex core are exactly $m_-$ and $m_+$?
status_search_result: The existence part of this conjecture (every pair $(m_-,m_+)$ is realized) was established by Diallo. Uniqueness (rigidity) is known only near the Fuchsian locus: Bonsante–Schlenker proved rigidity near the Fuchsian locus in the context of pleating laminations, and recent work by Prosanov (2025/2026) establishes rigidity of GHMC AdS (2+1)-spacetimes with convex boundary near the Fuchsian locus, including induced-metric rigidity for smooth/polyhedral strictly convex boundaries with holonomy close to Fuchsian. The full uniqueness (rigidity) part of the conjecture remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Smooth strictly convex AdS boundary metrics
original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be two metrics on S with curvature strictly less than -1 everywhere. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter 3-manifold N with smooth, space-like, strictly convex boundary such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are h_- and h_+, respectively?
self_contained_problem:

original_question: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold M = S × R with closed surface S of genus at least 2, is either the total volume V(M) or the convex-core volume V(C(M)) quasi-equivalent to a natural distance, such as the Teichmüller distance or the Weil–Petersson distance, between the induced metrics on the convex-core boundary or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$ carry a globally hyperbolic maximal Cauchy-compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter Lorentzian structure. The manifold $M$ has finite total Lorentzian volume $V(M)$, and contains a smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset $C(M) \subset M$, the convex core, whose boundary (when $M$ is non-Fuchsian) consists of two spacelike pleated surfaces inducing two hyperbolic metrics $m^+, m^-$ on $S$; let $V(C(M))$ denote its volume.

Endow the Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(S)$ with the Teichmüller distance $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}$ and with the Weil–Petersson distance $d_{\mathrm{WP}}$. Recall that two non-negative functions $F, G$ on the same space are said to be quasi-equivalent if there exist constants $A \geq 1$ and $B \geq 0$ with
$$\tfrac{1}{A} G - B \leq F \leq A\, G + B.$$

Is either $V(M)$ or $V(C(M))$, viewed as a function on the deformation space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on $S \times \mathbb{R}$, quasi-equivalent to one of the distances $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}(\mu_\ell, \mu_r)$, $d_{\mathrm{WP}}(\mu_\ell, \mu_r)$, $d_{\mathrm{Teich}}(m^+, m^-)$, or $d_{\mathrm{WP}}(m^+, m^-)$?

$$F_1 : \mathcal{T}(S) \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, \quad h_r \mapsto V(M(h_l, h_r)),$$
$$F_2 : \mathcal{T}(S) \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}, \quad h_r \mapsto V(C(M(h_l, h_r))).$$

(a) convex with respect to the Weil–Petersson (or some natural) structure on $\mathcal{T}(S)$;
(b) proper as a function on $\mathcal{T}(S)$;
(c) endowed with a unique minimum, attained at $h_r = h_l$ (i.e., the Fuchsian locus).

original_question: Is every globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold a deformation of a GH-standard anti-de Sitter manifold, namely one obtained from a quotient Γ\Ω with Γ contained in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q) ⊂ SO(2,n) for some p + q = n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and consider the model anti-de Sitter space $\mathrm{AdS}^{1,n}$, the Lorentzian symmetric space of constant sectional curvature $-1$, realized as a quadric in $\mathbb{R}^{2,n}$ with isometry group $\mathrm{SO}(2,n)$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter manifold is a Lorentzian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that is globally hyperbolic, admits a compact Cauchy hypersurface, and is maximal among such manifolds with respect to isometric embeddings.

Call a GHMC anti-de Sitter manifold $M$ \emph{GH-standard} if it is isometric to a quotient $\Gamma\backslash\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset \mathrm{AdS}^{1,n}$ is an open domain and $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(2,n)$ contained in a subgroup of the form $\mathrm{SO}(1,p)\times \mathrm{SO}(1,q)\subset \mathrm{SO}(2,n)$ with $p+q=n$, acting properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\Omega$.

original_question: Let S be the interior of a compact surface with boundary, let h_l and h_r be complete convex cocompact hyperbolic metrics on S, and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) be the corresponding holonomies. Let $S$ be the interior of a compact orientable surface with non-empty boundary, and let $h_l$ and $h_r$ be two complete convex cocompact hyperbolic metrics on $S$ (so each $(S,h_\bullet)$ is the interior of a compact convex core inside a convex cocompact hyperbolic surface with funnels). $$(\rho_l, \rho_r)(\gamma)\cdot x = \rho_l(\gamma)\, x\, \rho_r(\gamma)^{-1}, \qquad \gamma \in \pi_1(S).$$

For each metric $h_\bullet$ ($\bullet \in \{l,r\}$), the boundary $\partial C_\bullet$ of the convex core of $(S,h_\bullet)$ carries an induced hyperbolic metric on its boundary components, together with a measured bending lamination $\beta_\bullet$ on these components.

Question: Give a geometric criterion, expressed purely in terms of either
(a) the induced hyperbolic metrics on the boundary components of the convex cores of $(S,h_l)$ and $(S,h_r)$, or
(b) the bending laminations $\beta_l$ and $\beta_r$ of these convex cores,
which determines whether the action of $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\pi_1(S))$ on $\mathrm{AdS}^3$ is properly discontinuous.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let GH be the space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structures on a closed surface bundle M = S × R. Using the maximal-surface parameterization GH ≅ T*Teich(S) and the left-right parameterization GH ≅ Teich(S) × Teich(S), one gets a map φ : T*Teich(S) → Teich(S) × Teich(S). Is φ symplectic, in the sense that the pullback of the difference of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms equals, up to a constant, the canonical cotangent symplectic structure on T*Teich(S)?

Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. Denote by $\mathcal{GH}(M)$ the deformation space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter structures on $M$, i.e., maximal globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metrics of constant sectional curvature $-1$ on $M$ admitting a Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$, considered up to isotopy.

There are two classical parameterizations of $\mathcal{GH}(M)$:

(i) Krasnov–Schlenker maximal-surface parameterization: every class in $\mathcal{GH}(M)$ contains a unique embedded spacelike maximal Cauchy surface $\Sigma$. Its induced conformal class $[g]$ defines a point in the Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(S)$, and its second fundamental form is the real part of a holomorphic quadratic differential $q$ on $(\Sigma,[g])$. The map $[(M,h)] \mapsto ([g], q)$ is a diffeomorphism
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{ms}} : \mathcal{GH}(M) \longrightarrow T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S).$$

(ii) Mess left–right parameterization: holonomy considerations identify the holonomy of an AdS GHMC manifold with a pair $(\rho_{\ell},\rho_{r})$ of Fuchsian representations of $\pi_1(S)$, giving a diffeomorphism
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{Mess}} : \mathcal{GH}(M) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S).$$

Let $\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$ denote the Weil–Petersson symplectic form on $\mathcal{T}(S)$, and equip $\mathcal{T}(S)\times\mathcal{T}(S)$ with the difference symplectic form $\omega_{-} := \pi_{1}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}} - \pi_{2}^{*}\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}$. Equip $T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S)$ with its canonical (Liouville) cotangent symplectic form $\omega_{\mathrm{can}}$. Define
$$\varphi := \Phi_{\mathrm{Mess}} \circ \Phi_{\mathrm{ms}}^{-1} : T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S) \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S).$$

Question. Is $\varphi$ symplectic up to a constant? That is, does there exist a nonzero constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\varphi^{*}\omega_{-} \;=\; c\,\omega_{\mathrm{can}} \quad\text{on } T^{*}\mathcal{T}(S)?$$

status_search_result: The question appears to have been answered affirmatively. Scarinci and Schlenker ("Symplectic Wick rotations between moduli spaces of 3-manifolds", 2018) proved that the natural maps between moduli spaces of GHMC AdS 3-manifolds and related Teichmüller-type spaces are symplectic with respect to the canonical symplectic structures, in particular obtaining symplecticity of the Mess parameterization with respect to the difference of Weil–Petersson forms. Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant curvature $-1$ that is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface homeomorphic to $S$, and that is maximal among such structures (no isometric extension exists). For any GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$, the convex core is the smallest non-empty closed convex subset of $(M,h)$ whose preimage in the universal cover is convex; its boundary has two connected components (upper and lower), each carrying an induced hyperbolic metric and pleated along a measured geodesic lamination $\ell_+$ and $\ell_-$ on $S$, called the upper and lower measured bending laminations. A weighted multicurve on $S$ is a finite formal sum $\sum_i a_i \gamma_i$, with $a_i > 0$ and $\gamma_i$ pairwise disjoint simple closed geodesics, regarded as a measured lamination. A pair $(\ell_-, \ell_+)$ of measured laminations is said to fill $S$ if every essential simple closed curve on $S$ has positive total intersection number with $\ell_- + \ell_+$.

Question: Suppose $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ are weighted multicurves on $S$ that together fill $S$. Does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure $h$ on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations equal to $\ell_-$ (lower) and $\ell_+$ (upper)?

The general uniqueness question for arbitrary filling weighted multicurves does not appear to be resolved in the literature as of 2026.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, and assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Under this extra topological hypothesis, is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A three-dimensional anti-de Sitter (AdS) manifold is a Lorentzian 3-manifold of constant sectional curvature -1, locally modelled on AdS_3 = SO(2,2)/SO(1,2). A tachyon singularity along a spacelike line in an AdS 3-manifold is a cone-type singularity whose holonomy around a small meridian loop is a boost (a hyperbolic one-parameter subgroup of the isometry group fixing the singular line); the boost parameter m > 0 is called the mass of the tachyon and is a real-valued local invariant of the singularity.

Let N be a closed 3-manifold equipped with an AdS structure that is smooth off a link L ⊂ N (the singular locus) along which the structure has tachyon singularities, with prescribed masses m = (m_1, …, m_k) on the components of L. Assume in addition the topological condition that the complement N ∖ L is atoroidal, i.e. every π_1-injective embedded torus in N ∖ L is boundary-parallel.

Question. Under this atoroidality assumption, is the AdS structure on N rigid relative to the tachyon masses? That is, is every continuous deformation of the AdS-with-tachyons structure on (N, L) that keeps the masses (m_1, …, m_k) fixed necessarily trivial (i.e. obtained by pullback via isotopies)?
status_search_result: A University of Vienna research project (active, post-2022) explicitly lists rigidity/flexibility of closed AdS 3-manifolds with link-type tachyons as an ongoing line of investigation, indicating the question has not been settled. No published paper resolving rigidity under the atoroidal hypothesis was found.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Equivariant spacelike surfaces in complex AdS space
original_question: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(C) be quasi-Fuchsian representations. Does there exist a ρ_l-ρ_r-equivariant spacelike embedding of the universal cover S~ into the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C = O(4,C)/O(3,C)? If such an embedding exists, can one choose one of constant curvature?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $\tilde{S}$ denote its universal cover. Consider the complex anti-de Sitter space
$$X_{\mathbb{C}} = O(4,\mathbb{C})/O(3,\mathbb{C}),$$
viewed as a complex homogeneous space carrying its natural holomorphic pseudo-Riemannian structure. There is a natural identification of the identity component of the isometry group of $X_{\mathbb{C}}$ (modulo center) with $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$, so any pair of representations $\rho_l, \rho_r : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ defines an action of $\pi_1(S)$ on $X_{\mathbb{C}}$. A smooth embedding $f : \tilde{S} \to X_{\mathbb{C}}$ is called $(\rho_l,\rho_r)$-equivariant if $f(\gamma \cdot x) = (\rho_l(\gamma),\rho_r(\gamma)) \cdot f(x)$ for every $\gamma \in \pi_1(S)$ and $x \in \tilde{S}$, and is called spacelike if the pullback of the ambient pseudo-Riemannian metric to $\tilde{S}$ is a (real) Riemannian metric.

Recall that a representation $\rho : \pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ is quasi-Fuchsian if it is faithful, discrete, and its limit set on the Riemann sphere is a Jordan curve.

Assume $\rho_l$ and $\rho_r$ are quasi-Fuchsian representations.

(a) Does there exist a $(\rho_l,\rho_r)$-equivariant spacelike embedding $\tilde{S} \to X_{\mathbb{C}}$?

(b) If such an embedding exists, can it be chosen so that the induced Riemannian metric on $\tilde{S}$ has constant Gaussian curvature?

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
context_brief: Proper domains for convex cocompact complex AdS actions
original_question: Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(M) → PSL_2(C) be convex cocompact representations. Is there a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(M)) acts properly discontinuously? What is the topology of the quotient, and how can one recognize geometrically whether the action is proper or non-proper?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a hyperbolic 3-manifold with fundamental group $\Gamma=\pi_1(M)$, and let
$$\rho_l,\rho_r:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$$
be two convex cocompact representations. Consider the diagonal homomorphism
$$(\rho_l,\rho_r):\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}),$$
and let this product group act on the complex anti-de Sitter space
$$X_{\mathbb{C}}=\bigl(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\bigr)\big/\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\;\cong\;\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}),$$
where $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ acts by $(g,h)\cdot x=gxh^{-1}$.

Address the following:

(a) Does there exist a maximal open subset $\Omega\subset X_{\mathbb{C}}$, invariant under $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\Gamma)$, on which the action of $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\Gamma)$ is properly discontinuous?

(b) When such a domain $\Omega$ exists, determine the topology of the quotient manifold $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\Gamma)\backslash\Omega$.

(c) Provide a geometric criterion, in terms of $\rho_l$ and $\rho_r$ (e.g., comparison of their associated convex cores, limit sets, or contraction/expansion behavior on $\partial\mathbb{H}^3$), that characterizes when the action of $(\rho_l,\rho_r)(\Gamma)$ on $X_{\mathbb{C}}$ (or on a candidate invariant open set) is properly discontinuous versus non-proper.
category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry and proper actions
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the maximal-domain/quotient/properness criterion question for convex cocompact pairs $(\rho_l,\rho_r)$ acting on complex AdS space. paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
context_brief: Admissible walks with bounded even step sizes
original_question: For a fixed positive integer m, let F_m be the set of all nonzero even integers j with |j| <= m. A walk x from -n to n is a finite sequence of nonzero even steps x(t) whose total sum is 2n; writing the intermediate vertices as j(0) = -n and j(t) = -n + sum_{i=1}^t x(i), the walk is admissible when j(t) is never equal to ±n for 1 <= t <= ν, where ν + 1 is the number of steps. Let X_n^+(F_m) be the set of admissible walks from -n to n that use only positive steps from F_m, and for each such walk define h(x) = (∏_{t=1}^ν [n^2 - j(t)^2]^{-1})(∏_{t=1}^{ν+1} V(x(t))). For z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) ∈ C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x). Determine these polynomials P_{m,n}(z), and/or determine their asymptotic behavior for fixed m as n → ∞.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $m$ and let $F_m = \{j \in 2\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\} : |j|\le m\}$. Fix a positive integer $n$ and complex numbers $V(2), V(4), \ldots, V(2m)$, and write $z = (V(2),V(4),\ldots,V(2m)) \in \mathbb{C}^m$.

A walk from $-n$ to $n$ with positive steps from $F_m$ is a finite sequence $x = (x(1),x(2),\ldots,x(\nu+1))$ with each $x(t) \in F_m \cap \mathbb{Z}_{>0} = \{2,4,\ldots,m\}$ (so $m\ge 2$ for the set to be nonempty; assume $m$ is even for convenience) such that
$$\sum_{t=1}^{\nu+1} x(t) = 2n.$$
Define the intermediate vertices by $j(0) = -n$ and $j(t) = -n + \sum_{i=1}^{t} x(i)$ for $1\le t \le \nu+1$ (so $j(\nu+1)=n$). The walk is called admissible if
$$j(t) \neq \pm n \quad\text{for all } 1 \le t \le \nu.$$
Let $X_n^+(F_m)$ denote the set of all such admissible walks.

For $x \in X_n^+(F_m)$, define
$$h(x) = \left(\prod_{t=1}^{\nu}\frac{1}{n^2 - j(t)^2}\right)\left(\prod_{t=1}^{\nu+1} V(x(t))\right),$$
and define the polynomial in $z$
$$P_{m,n}(z) = \sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x).$$

Problem: For each fixed $m$, give an explicit description (closed form) of the polynomials $P_{m,n}(z)$ in the variables $V(2),V(4),\ldots,V(2m)$, and determine their asymptotic behaviour as $n\to\infty$ with $m$ fixed.
category_tag: Admissible walks and Hill operator identities
status_search_result: Djakov–Mityagin posed several combinatorial questions arising from spectral decompositions of Hill operators; one identity in this circle was given a direct combinatorial proof (e.g. by Borisov and Zagier-style arguments), but explicit closed-form expressions and asymptotics for the polynomials $P_{m,n}(z)$ associated with admissible positive-step walks for general $m$ do not appear to be established in the literature found. Status appears unresolved in general.

paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
original_question: Let W = { z : C(z) = ∞ } be the exceptional set associated with the comparison inequality ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| <= C(z) * |∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)| from the preceding question. Determine the structure of this exceptional set W inside C^m.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers m ≥ 1 and consider parameters z = (V_1, V_2, …, V_m) ∈ C^m. For each integer n ≥ 1, let X_n^+ = X_n^+(F_m) denote the (combinatorially defined) finite index set of "positive" walks of weighted length n associated with the m-parameter family F_m (the index set arising in the eigenfunction expansions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials of m terms, so that each x ∈ X_n^+ is a finite sequence of admissible jumps and h(x) = h(x; z) is a rational function of z whose factors are products of the coordinates V_j and reciprocals of small denominators built from the jumps in x).

Define
  C(z) := sup_n  ( ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)| ) / | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |  ∈ [0, ∞],
the smallest (possibly infinite) constant for which the comparison inequality
  ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x; z)|  ≤  C(z) · | ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x; z) |
holds simultaneously for every n ≥ 1.

Let W := { z ∈ C^m : C(z) = ∞ } be the associated exceptional set. Determine the structure of W as a subset of C^m: in particular, decide whether W is a (countable union of) proper analytic / algebraic subvarieties of C^m, describe its dimension and irreducible components, and decide whether C^m \ W has full Lebesgue measure (i.e. whether the comparison inequality holds for almost every z ∈ C^m).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem by Djakov and Mityagin (2012) concerning the structure of the exceptional set in C^m on which a comparison inequality between the absolute and signed sums over walk-type combinatorial objects fails. Subsequent literature on combinatorial identities of Djakov–Mityagin and on convergence/divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials addresses related identities and special cases (e.g. two-term potentials), but no source found resolves the description of the exceptional set W = {z : C(z) = ∞} in general. The problem appears to remain open.
