paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in Rn , n ≥ 2, with the property that there exists α in (0, π] such that for every point y in ∂Ω there is an open truncated cone with vertex y and angle α contained in Ω. Is there some positive number p = p(α) such that every positive superharmonic function in Ω belongs to Lp (Ω)? If so, can such a p be characterised in terms of α? (D. H. Armitage)
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain. Assume that there exists $\alpha\in(0,\pi]$ such that for every boundary point $y\in\partial\Omega$ there is an open truncated cone with vertex $y$ and aperture (opening angle) $\alpha$ that is contained in $\Omega$. (Here a truncated open cone of vertex $y$ and angle $\alpha$ means a set of the form $\{x : 0<|x-y|<r,\ \angle(x-y,v)<\alpha/2\}$ for some unit vector $v$ and some $r>0$.)

A function $u:\Omega\to(-\infty,\infty]$ is superharmonic if it is lower semicontinuous, not identically $+\infty$, and satisfies the super-mean-value inequality $u(x)\geq \frac{1}{|B(x,r)|}\int_{B(x,r)} u\,dm$ for every closed ball $\overline{B(x,r)}\subset\Omega$.

Determine whether there exists a positive number $p=p(\alpha)>0$, depending only on $\alpha$ (and the dimension $n$), such that every positive superharmonic function $u$ on $\Omega$ belongs to $L^p(\Omega)$. If such a $p$ exists, characterise the supremum of admissible exponents $p$ in terms of $\alpha$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has established Lp-integrability of positive superharmonic functions on broad classes of domains satisfying interior geometric conditions: Aikawa and others proved that on bounded John domains (which include domains with the uniform interior cone property) positive superharmonic functions belong to Lp for some p>0, and quantitative bounds on the exponent in terms of cone aperture have been obtained (e.g., L1-integrability when cos ψ > 1/√n). However, a sharp characterisation of the optimal exponent p(α) purely in terms of α appears not to be definitively settled in the literature, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Let {zn }, 1 ≤ n < ∞ be an infinite sequence such that |zn | = 1. Define n Y An = max |z − zi |. |z|=1 i=1 Is it true that lim supn→∞ An = ∞, and if so, how quickly must An tend to infinity? We may define zn inductively as follows, z1 = 1, z2 = −1 and if zν has already been defined for 1 ≤ ν ≤ 2k , then we define for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2k ,  πi  zp+2k = zp exp k . With this definition, we easily see that An ≤ n + 1, with equality if, and only if, n = 2k − 1 for some integer k. Is this example extreme? (P. Erdös)
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{z_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be an infinite sequence of complex numbers with $|z_n|=1$ for every $n$. For each $n\ge 1$ define
$$A_n \;=\; \max_{|z|=1}\,\prod_{i=1}^{n} |z-z_i|.$$
(a) Is it true that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} A_n = \infty$ for every such sequence?  If so, determine how quickly $A_n$ must tend to infinity (i.e. find the optimal lower bound, valid for every choice of $\{z_n\}$, on the growth of $\limsup_{n\to\infty} A_n$).

(b) Consider the explicit sequence defined inductively by $z_1=1$, $z_2=-1$, and, once $z_\nu$ has been defined for $1\le\nu\le 2^k$, by setting
$$z_{p+2^k} \;=\; z_p\,\exp\!\Bigl(\frac{\pi i}{k}\Bigr), \qquad 1\le p\le 2^k.$$
For this sequence one has $A_n\le n+1$, with equality if and only if $n=2^k-1$ for some integer $k\ge 0$. Is this example extremal in the sense that for every sequence $\{z_n\}$ with $|z_n|=1$ one has $\limsup_{n\to\infty} A_n/n \le 1$ (or, more precisely, that no sequence produces faster growth than this one)?
status_search_result: The first part of the question (whether $\limsup A_n=\infty$) was answered affirmatively by G. Wagner, who showed $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log A_n/\log\log n>0$. J. Beck, in "The modulus of polynomials with zeros on the unit circle: A problem of Erdős" (Annals of Math. 134 (1991), 609–651), substantially improved this lower bound. However, the precise rate of growth of $A_n$ and the question of whether the explicit dyadic example is genuinely extremal remain unresolved.

paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Let PN (z) be a polynomial with N terms, satisfying |PN (z)| ≤ 1 on |z| = 1. How large can Pn (z) be if Pn (z) is a partial sum of PN (z)? (P. Erdös)
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $N$, let
$$P_N(z) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} a_k z^{n_k}$$
be a complex polynomial having exactly $N$ nonzero terms (with distinct nonnegative integer exponents $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_N$ and complex coefficients $a_k \neq 0$), and assume that
$$\sup_{|z|=1} |P_N(z)| \leq 1.$$
For an integer $1 \leq n \leq N$, call any polynomial of the form
$$P_n(z) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k z^{n_k}$$
a partial sum of $P_N$. Determine the best possible upper bound, as a function of $N$ (and possibly $n$), for the quantity
$$\sup_{|z|=1} |P_n(z)|$$
taken over all such polynomials $P_N$ and all partial sums $P_n$ of $P_N$. Equivalently, find the order of growth of
$$f(N) = \sup \bigl\{\, \|P_n\|_{\infty,|z|=1} : P_n \text{ is a partial sum of some } P_N \text{ with } \|P_N\|_{\infty,|z|=1} \leq 1 \,\bigr\}.$$
status_search_result: Web searches for this Erdős problem on the size of partial sums of an $N$-term polynomial bounded by $1$ on the unit circle did not return a definitive resolution. Related literature on lacunary polynomials and partial sums exists, but no clearly matching solved-status reference was located.

paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Let P (z) be a polynomial whose zeros z1 , z2 , . . . , zn lie in |z| ≤ 1. Is it true that P ′ (z) always has a zero in |z − z1 | ≤ 1? (Bl. Sendov)
self_contained_problem: Let $P(z)$ be a polynomial of degree $n \geq 2$ with complex coefficients whose zeros $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ (listed with multiplicity) all lie in the closed unit disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \leq 1\}$. Prove or disprove: for every such polynomial and for every choice of a zero $z_1$ of $P$, the derivative $P'(z)$ has at least one zero in the closed disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - z_1| \leq 1\}$.
status_search_result: Known as Sendov's conjecture. It is established for polynomials of degree n ≤ 8 (Brown–Xiang and others), and Terence Tao (arXiv:2012.04125, published in Acta Mathematica, 2022) proved it for all sufficiently large degrees n ≥ n₀. The conjecture remains open for the intermediate range of degrees, so it is not fully resolved.

paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Let f (z) = z n + a1 z n−1 + . . . + an be a polynomial of degree n. Cartan (n) [146] proved that the set |f (z)| ≤ 1, which we call Ef can always be covered by discs, the sum of whose radii is at most 2e. It seems likely that 2e can be replaced by (n) 2. If Ef is connected, this was proved by Pommerenke [642], who also proved the general result, with 2.59 instead of 2.
self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z) = z^n + a_1 z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_n$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with complex coefficients, and let
$$E_f = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |f(z)| \leq 1\}$$
denote its filled lemniscate. A classical theorem of H. Cartan states that $E_f$ can always be covered by a finite union of open discs the sum of whose radii is at most $2e$. Pommerenke improved this constant to $2.59$, and showed that when $E_f$ is connected the sharp bound is $2$ (attained by $f(z) = z^n$).

Prove or disprove: for every monic polynomial $f$ of degree $n \geq 1$, the set $E_f$ can be covered by finitely many discs whose radii sum to at most $2$.
status_search_result: Searches confirm the classical Cartan bound of $2e$ and Pommerenke's improvements (2.59 in general, 2 in the connected case), but no source found establishes or refutes the conjectured bound of $2$ in the general case. The status appears to remain open, but no recent definitive resolution was located.

paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
original_question: Is it true that the length of the curve |fn (z)| = 1 is maximal for fn (z) = z n − 1? (P. Erdös)
self_contained_problem:
For a monic polynomial $f_n(z) = z^n + a_{n-1}z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0$ of degree $n \ge 2$ with complex coefficients, let $L(f_n)$ denote the total arc length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of the lemniscate
$$\Lambda(f_n) = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |f_n(z)| = 1\}.$$
Prove or disprove: among all monic polynomials of degree $n$, the length $L(f_n)$ is maximized by $f_n(z) = z^n - 1$.
status_search_result: Known as the Erdős–Herzog–Piranian lemniscate length conjecture. Fryntov and Nazarov (2008) showed z^n − 1 is a local maximizer and proved the asymptotic bound L(f_n) ≤ 2n + O(n^{7/8}). A 2025 preprint by Tao establishes the conjecture for all sufficiently large n. The conjecture for all n ≥ 2 (in full generality) does not yet appear to be completely settled in the literature.

original_question: How restrictive is the condition that the characteristic curves on a smooth hypersurface in standard symplectic space are planar?
self_contained_problem:
Equip $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (with $n \geq 2$) with the standard symplectic form $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n dx_i \wedge dy_i$. Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be a smooth hypersurface (or a germ thereof). The restriction $\omega|_M$ has a one-dimensional kernel at every point of $M$, and the integral curves of this kernel distribution are called the characteristic curves of $M$. A characteristic curve is said to be planar if its image is contained in some affine 2-plane of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

Determine how restrictive the condition is that every characteristic curve on $M$ is planar. More precisely, classify (or otherwise describe) all smooth hypersurface germs $M$ in the standard symplectic space $(\mathbb{R}^{2n}, \omega)$ for which all characteristic curves are planar.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. No published classification or solution describing exactly which smooth hypersurfaces in the standard symplectic space have all-planar characteristic curves was located. Related work on characteristic foliations on hypersurfaces in holomorphic symplectic manifolds exists but addresses different settings.

original_question: Prove Ivrii's conjecture for 3-periodic multidimensional outer symplectic billiards with respect to a strictly convex closed hypersurface.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ ($n\ge 2$) be a smooth strictly convex closed hypersurface bounding a convex domain, and let $\omega$ denote the standard symplectic form on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. The outer symplectic billiard map associated with $M$ is defined as follows: for a point $x\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ outside $M$, consider the characteristic line through a tangency point $y\in M$ such that the chord $xy$ is tangent to $M$ at $y$ along a direction in the kernel of $\omega|_{T_yM}$ (the symplectic characteristic direction); the image $T(x)$ is the point obtained by reflecting $x$ through $y$, i.e. $T(x)=2y-x$. A point $x$ is called $3$-periodic if $T^3(x)=x$ but $T(x)\ne x$.

Prove that the set of $3$-periodic points of the outer symplectic billiard map associated with any smooth strictly convex closed hypersurface $M\subset\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ has Lebesgue measure zero (Ivrii's conjecture for 3-periodic orbits of multidimensional outer symplectic billiards).
status_search_result: Recent work (2024) gives geometric proofs of Ivrii's conjecture for 3- and 4-periodic orbits of planar outer billiards and of symplectic billiards, and extends the symplectic-billiard case to higher dimensions. However, the multidimensional outer symplectic billiard case for 3-periodic orbits with respect to a strictly convex closed hypersurface does not appear to be settled in the available literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: How can one characterize the optical symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines, namely the local symplectic transformations realizable by finite collections of mirrors, inside the full space of symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be Euclidean space and let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the space of oriented lines (light rays) in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The space $\mathcal{L}$ has dimension $2n-2$ and inherits a canonical symplectic structure from the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{R}^n$ via symplectic reduction (identifying an oriented line with the equivalence class of unit covectors along it).

A smooth hypersurface $M \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (locally the graph of a smooth function of $n-1$ variables) defines a billiard (optical) reflection map: an oriented line that hits $M$ transversally is sent to its reflection across the tangent hyperplane at the point of incidence. This reflection is a local symplectomorphism of $(\mathcal{L}, \omega)$.

Define the set of optical symplectic transformations $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathrm{Symp}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{L})$ to be the set of local symplectic transformations of $\mathcal{L}$ obtainable as finite compositions of billiard reflections in smooth mirrors.

Since a generic local symplectic transformation of $\mathcal{L}$ depends on a smooth function of $2n-2$ variables (e.g., a generating function or Hamiltonian), while a mirror is determined by a smooth function of $n-1$ variables, one expects $\mathcal{O}$ to be a proper, "small" subset of $\mathrm{Symp}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{L})$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the set $\mathcal{O}$ of optical symplectic transformations inside the full group of local symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines. That is, find necessary and sufficient conditions on a local symplectomorphism $\Phi : \mathcal{L} \dashrightarrow \mathcal{L}$ for it to be expressible as a finite composition of billiard reflections in smooth hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published characterization of the optical (mirror-realizable) subset inside the full group of local symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines. The problem is posed in surveys of open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry, and no resolution was located in the literature, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Anomalous transport in the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model: a review and open problems
original_question: For nonequilibrium heat-transport studies of Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains, how do choices in thermostatting protocol—especially the number of thermostatted oscillators and the bath coupling strength—control finite-size corrections and the rate at which the measured flux approaches the asymptotic anomalous-scaling regime, and what simulation procedures remain reliable as the system size changes?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou (FPUT) chain of N classical oscillators with Hamiltonian
  H = Σ_{i=1}^{N} p_i^2/2 + Σ_{i=0}^{N} [ (1/2)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^2 + (α/3)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^3 + (β/4)(q_{i+1}-q_i)^4 ],
with fixed boundary conditions q_0 = q_{N+1} = 0. To drive the chain out of equilibrium, attach to a set of N_L oscillators on the left end a thermostat at temperature T_L and to a set of N_R oscillators on the right end a thermostat at temperature T_R < T_L (e.g. Langevin baths with friction γ, Nosé–Hoover baths, or stochastic collision baths characterized by a bath–chain coupling strength γ). Define the steady-state heat flux J(N; γ, N_L, N_R, protocol) measured by averaging the local current j_i = (1/2)(p_i + p_{i+1})·V'(q_{i+1}-q_i) in the bulk.

It is known that for such chains the finite-size thermal conductivity κ(N) = J(N) N/(T_L−T_R) diverges as N^α with an anomalous exponent α ∈ (0,1) in the asymptotic limit N → ∞.

Problem. Quantitatively characterize how the choice of thermostatting protocol — specifically the number N_L, N_R of thermostatted oscillators, the bath–chain coupling strength γ, and the type of thermostat — controls the finite-size corrections to the asymptotic scaling J(N) ~ N^{α−1}. In particular:
(a) Derive (analytically or via a controlled hydrodynamic/boundary-resistance analysis) the leading correction term in an expansion J(N) = N^{α−1}[A(γ, N_L, N_R) + B(γ, N_L, N_R) N^{−δ} + …], identifying δ > 0 and the dependence of A, B on the thermostat parameters.
(b) Determine which simulation protocols (choices of γ, N_L, N_R, and thermostat type) minimize finite-size corrections so that the asymptotic anomalous regime is reached at the smallest N, and prove that the extracted exponent α is independent of the protocol.
(c) Establish a procedure that remains reliable uniformly as N varies over several orders of magnitude.
category_tag: Anomalous heat transport in FPUT chains
status_search_result: Searches indicate that while many partial results exist — hydrodynamic analyses of boundary conditions, studies showing strong dependence of boundary thermal resistance on thermostat parameters and system size for β-FPU, and comparisons of Langevin vs Nosé–Hoover baths — there is no comprehensive, quantitative theory characterizing how thermostat protocol choices control the convergence rate to the anomalous scaling regime across system sizes. The question of an optimal, size-uniform protocol remains open.

paper_title: Anomalous transport in the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model: a review and open problems
original_question: For Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains close to an integrable limit, such as perturbations of the Toda chain or the harmonic chain, what are the characteristic length scales that determine when transport crosses over from ballistic motion to a kinetic or apparently diffusive finite-size regime and finally to the asymptotic anomalous regime, and how do those scales depend on the strength of the integrability-breaking perturbation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional chain of N classical particles with unit mass and nearest-neighbor interaction, governed by the Hamiltonian
  H = sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i^2/2 + sum_{i} V(q_{i+1} - q_i),
where the pair potential V is taken close to an integrable limit. Two canonical near-integrable settings are:
 (a) a perturbed harmonic chain, V(r) = (1/2) r^2 + epsilon U(r), with U a generic anharmonic potential and epsilon a small parameter;
 (b) a perturbed Toda chain, V(r) = V_Toda(r) + epsilon W(r), where V_Toda(r) = (a/b) e^{-b r} + a r (up to constants) is the integrable Toda potential and W is a generic non-Toda perturbation.
Place the chain in contact with two heat baths at temperatures T_L and T_R = T_L + Delta T at its ends, and let J(L) denote the steady-state heat flux as a function of the chain length L = N a (a the lattice spacing).

It is expected that, as L is increased, three regimes appear:
 (i) Ballistic regime for L < ell(epsilon): J is essentially independent of L.
 (ii) Kinetic / apparently diffusive finite-size regime for ell(epsilon) < L < ell_c(epsilon): J ~ 1/L (Fourier-like behavior).
 (iii) Asymptotic anomalous regime for L > ell_c(epsilon): the anomalous component J_A ~ L^{delta - 1} dominates, with some exponent delta in (0,1) characteristic of the universality class of FPUT-type chains.

The problem is to determine the two characteristic crossover length scales ell(epsilon) and ell_c(epsilon) and their dependence on the strength epsilon of the integrability-breaking perturbation, in both settings (a) and (b). In particular:
 1. Derive ell(epsilon), interpreted as a typical mean free path of the relevant quasiparticles (phonons in case (a), Toda solitons in case (b)), as a function of epsilon (e.g. determine whether ell(epsilon) ~ epsilon^{-alpha} for some alpha and identify alpha).
 2. Derive the second crossover scale ell_c(epsilon) > ell(epsilon) at which the anomalous hydrodynamic contribution overtakes the apparent diffusive behavior, again as a function of epsilon.
 3. Identify conditions under which the intermediate diffusive window (ii) is absent, so that the system crosses over directly from ballistic to anomalous transport.
category_tag: Anomalous heat transport in near-integrable chains
status_search_result: The question of the crossover length scales between ballistic, kinetic/diffusive, and anomalous regimes in near-integrable FPUT-type chains is treated as an open problem in current reviews. paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
original_question: Suppose one learns a holomorphic operator by empirical risk minimization using a neural operator whose trainable component is a fully trainable network, with particular interest in the noiseless case. Can such fully trainable ERM schemes achieve sample-complexity rates faster than the Monte Carlo rate, rather than being limited to roughly n^{-1/2} behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be (complex) Banach spaces and let $U \subset X$ be an open set. Consider an unknown operator $F : U \to Y$ that is holomorphic, i.e., Fréchet-differentiable in the complex sense on $U$, and assume $F$ lies in a suitable class $\mathcal{H}(U,Y)$ of bounded holomorphic operators. Given i.i.d. samples $\{(x_i, F(x_i))\}_{i=1}^n$ drawn from a probability measure $\mu$ on $U$ (the noiseless setting, i.e., outputs are observed exactly), one constructs an estimator $\widehat{F}_n$ via empirical risk minimization (ERM) over a hypothesis class $\mathcal{N}$ of neural operators of the form $\widehat{F} = \mathcal{D} \circ \Psi_\theta \circ \mathcal{E}$, where $\mathcal{E} : X \to \mathbb{R}^{d_E}$ is an encoder, $\mathcal{D} : \mathbb{R}^{d_D} \to Y$ is a decoder, and $\Psi_\theta : \mathbb{R}^{d_E} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_D}$ is a fully trainable feed-forward neural network whose every weight and bias is a free parameter optimized during training (as opposed to schemes in which $\Psi_\theta$ is partially fixed or only certain layers are trainable). The estimator solves
$$\widehat{F}_n \in \arg\min_{\widehat{F} \in \mathcal{N}} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \|\widehat{F}(x_i) - F(x_i)\|_Y^2.$$
Define the worst-case expected $L^2(\mu;Y)$ generalization error
$$R_n := \sup_{F \in \mathcal{H}(U,Y)} \mathbb{E}\, \|\widehat{F}_n - F\|_{L^2(\mu;Y)}^2.$$
Question: Does there exist a choice of architecture $\mathcal{N}$ (with size possibly depending on $n$) such that the fully trainable ERM scheme achieves a convergence rate strictly faster than the Monte Carlo rate, i.e.,
$$R_n = o(n^{-1/2}) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty,$$
or is every fully trainable ERM scheme limited to a rate no faster than $n^{-1/2}$ on the class of holomorphic operators in the noiseless regime?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on operator learning theory. Known results establish faster-than-Monte Carlo rates for holomorphic operator learning with partially trainable / sparse-recovery-based schemes, while general lower and upper bounds matching for fully trainable ERM in the noiseless regime do not appear to be established in the literature as of the search date. No publication resolving this specific question for fully trainable neural-operator ERM was identified.

paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
original_question: Let K be a class of target operators and compare the noiseless minimax sampling width s_n(K)_X with the noisy statistical nonlinear sampling width s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X for operator learning. Can one obtain a sharp characterization of operator-learning minimax rates that explicitly tracks the noise level σ, analogous to the known noise-aware theory for classical function approximation?
self_contained_problem:
Let X and Y be separable Banach spaces and let K be a class of (possibly nonlinear) target operators F : X → Y. For an integer n ≥ 1 define the noiseless nonlinear sampling width

  s_n(K)_X := inf_{φ_1,…,φ_n ∈ X*, R : ℝ^n → Y} sup_{F ∈ K} sup_{x ∈ B_X} ‖F(x) − R(φ_1(x),…,φ_n(x); x)‖_Y,

where the infimum is over all choices of n bounded linear measurement functionals on X and all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps R, and B_X is the unit ball of X.

For a noise level σ ≥ 0 and tail parameter η ∈ (0,1), define the noisy statistical nonlinear sampling width s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X as the smallest ε > 0 such that there exist measurement functionals φ_1,…,φ_n ∈ X* and a (possibly randomized) reconstruction map R̂ for which, given noisy measurements y_i = φ_i(x) + σ ξ_i with ξ_i i.i.d. standard noise (e.g. N(0,1)) and any input x ∈ B_X, one has

  sup_{F ∈ K} sup_{x ∈ B_X} Pr[ ‖F(x) − R̂(y_1,…,y_n; x)‖_Y > ε ] ≤ η.

The problem is to obtain a sharp two-sided characterization (matching upper and lower bounds, up to absolute constants) of the noisy minimax operator-learning rate s̃_n^η(K; σ)_X in terms of the noiseless width s_n(K)_X, the noise level σ, the sample size n, and the geometric/complexity parameters of the class K. In particular, identify the explicit dependence on σ that interpolates between the noiseless rate (σ = 0) and the noise-dominated regime, in analogy with the noise-aware minimax theory available for classical function approximation.
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly identified as open in the source: a noise-level-aware sharp characterization of minimax rates for operator learning, paralleling the classical function-approximation theory, has not been established. No subsequent work establishing such a characterization was located.

paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
context_brief: Sharp noisy widths for holomorphic classes
original_question: For the holomorphic operator classes studied in Theorems 1 and 2, can one prove sharp bounds for the statistical nonlinear sampling n-width s̃_n^η(K; σ) in L^2_ϱ? In particular, can such bounds determine whether suitably noisy operator-learning problems for these holomorphic classes still allow faster-than-Monte Carlo rates?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable Hilbert spaces and let $\varrho$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{X}$. For an operator $F:\mathcal{X}	o\mathcal{Y}$ define the $L^2_\varrho$-norm by $\|F\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 := \int_{\mathcal{X}} \|F(x)\|_{\mathcal{Y}}^2\, d\varrho(x)$.

Let $K\subset L^2_\varrho(\mathcal{X};\mathcal{Y})$ be a compact class of operators. Consider an i.i.d. noisy sampling model: a learner queries inputs $x_1,\dots,x_n$ drawn i.i.d. from $\varrho$ and receives observations $y_i = F(x_i) + \xi_i$, where $\xi_i$ are i.i.d. centered noise variables on $\mathcal{Y}$ with noise level $\sigma>0$ (e.g.\ Gaussian with covariance $\sigma^2 I$). Allowing arbitrary (possibly nonlinear and randomized) reconstruction maps $\Phi_n$ that produce an estimator $\widehat F = \Phi_n((x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n)$, define the statistical nonlinear sampling $n$-width
$$	ilde s_n^{\eta}(K;\sigma)_{L^2_\varrho} := \inf_{\Phi_n}\sup_{F\in K}  ig(\mathbb{E}\,\|F-\widehat F\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 ig)^{1/2},$$
where $\eta$ encodes the noise model.

Now let $K$ be a holomorphic operator class of the following type. Fix a sequence $ oldsymbol{b}=(b_j)_{j\ge 1}\in \ell^p(\mathbb{N})$ for some $0<p<1$, and let $K=K( oldsymbol{b},\mathcal{Y})$ consist of all operators $F:\mathcal{X}	o\mathcal{Y}$ that admit a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein-type polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{ oldsymbol{ho}}\supset \mathcal{X}$ with parameters controlled by $ oldsymbol{b}$, and that are uniformly bounded on this polyellipse. (These are the standard $( oldsymbol{b},\varepsilon)$-holomorphic classes for which deterministic adaptive $n$-widths in $L^2_\varrho$ are known to decay at rate $n^{-(1/p-1/2)}$, faster than the Monte-Carlo rate $n^{-1/2}$.)

In particular, decide whether, in the presence of nontrivial sampling noise of level $\sigma>0$, the rate of $	ilde s_n^{\eta}(K;\sigma)_{L^2_\varrho}$ can still be strictly faster than the Monte-Carlo rate $n^{-1/2}$, or whether noise forces the rate to be $\Omega(n^{-1/2})$.

paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
original_question: Beyond classical operator classes defined by regularity assumptions such as smoothness or holomorphy, can one develop and analyze architecture-oriented classes of target operators whose definition is tied to approximation by specific neural-operator architectures, and use them as a mathematically meaningful alternative foundation for operator-learning theory?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces (for instance, function spaces on bounded domains in Euclidean space), and let $\mathcal{F}\subset\{G:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}\}$ denote a target class of nonlinear operators. Classical operator-learning theory studies classes $\mathcal{F}$ defined through regularity assumptions on $G$, such as Lipschitz continuity, $C^k$-smoothness, Sobolev/Besov regularity on suitable encodings, or holomorphic/analytic dependence on parameters; for such classes one derives quantitative approximation rates and statistical learning bounds for neural-operator surrogates (e.g. DeepONet, Fourier neural operators, PCA-net, random feature operators).

Define an "architecture-oriented" operator class as follows. Fix a parametric family of neural-operator architectures
$$\mathcal{N} = \{\Phi_\theta:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y} \mid \theta\in\Theta_n,\ n\in\mathbb{N}\},$$
indexed by a complexity parameter $n$ (e.g. number of parameters, width, depth, or number of trunk/branch basis functions), and a complexity functional $C:\mathcal{N}\to[0,\infty)$. For an admissible compact input set $K\subset\mathcal{X}$, a norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{Y}}$, and a rate function $\rho:\mathbb{N}\to(0,\infty)$ with $\rho(n)\to 0$, define
$$\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K) \;=\; \Big\{\, G:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}\ :\ \exists\,\{\Phi_{\theta_n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset\mathcal{N},\ C(\Phi_{\theta_n})\le n,\ \sup_{u\in K}\|G(u)-\Phi_{\theta_n}(u)\|_{\mathcal{Y}}\le \rho(n)\,\Big\}.$$

Develop a mathematical theory of such classes $\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K)$ as a foundation for operator-learning theory. Concretely, provide:

(a) Intrinsic, architecture-independent characterizations of $\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K)$ for the principal neural-operator architectures (e.g. DeepONet, FNO, PCA-net, averaging neural operators), in the spirit of approximation-space characterizations in classical approximation theory; in particular identify whether $\mathcal{A}_\rho$ is a quasi-Banach space and determine its interpolation and embedding relations with classical regularity classes.

(b) Sharp two-sided approximation rates: for $G\in\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K)$ establish matching upper and lower bounds on $\inf_{\Phi\in\mathcal{N},\,C(\Phi)\le n}\sup_{u\in K}\|G(u)-\Phi(u)\|_{\mathcal{Y}}$, and prove or disprove that these rates can break the curse of dimensionality that affects classical smoothness-based classes.

(c) Statistical learning rates: given i.i.d. samples $(u_i,G(u_i))_{i=1}^N$ from a probability measure $\mu$ on $K$, derive minimax rates of convergence for empirical-risk-minimization estimators over $\mathcal{N}$ when the truth $G$ is assumed to lie in $\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K)$, and compare these rates with those obtainable under classical regularity hypotheses.

The problem is to determine whether such architecture-oriented operator classes $\mathcal{A}_\rho(\mathcal{N},K)$ admit a mathematically coherent theory along the lines of (a)–(c), and whether they constitute a meaningful alternative foundation for operator-learning theory in place of classes based on smoothness or holomorphy.
status_search_result: The question is a programmatic open direction in operator-learning theory. While there are recent results characterizing approximation and statistical rates for specific neural-operator architectures (DeepONet, FNO, PCA-net) under classical regularity assumptions, no comprehensive theory of architecture-oriented operator classes (analogues of approximation spaces) appears in the literature, and the direction is repeatedly listed among open questions in recent surveys.

paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
original_question: For operator learning in L^2_ϱ, how can one further separate the minimax behavior of holomorphic classes H(b)∘ι from the architecture-based classes K_FNO^α? Concretely, can one either prove stronger lower bounds on the sampling widths of K_FNO^α or show that operators in H(b)∘ι are themselves well approximated by Fourier neural operators, thereby clarifying whether the two classes have genuinely different sample-complexity behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $\varrho$ be a Borel probability measure on a separable Hilbert space $X$ of input functions on $D$ (the "data distribution"). For a target Banach space $Y$ of output functions on $D$, consider nonlinear operators $\Psi:X\to Y$, evaluated in the loss
$$\|\Psi-\widehat\Psi\|_{L^2_\varrho}^2 \;=\; \int_X \|\Psi(u)-\widehat\Psi(u)\|_Y^2\,d\varrho(u).$$

Two model classes of operators are of interest.

(1) Holomorphic class $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$. Fix a sequence $\boldsymbol b=(b_j)_{j\ge 1}\in\ell^p$ for some $p\in(0,1)$, and an affine parametrization $\iota:U=[-1,1]^{\mathbb{N}}\to X$ with $\iota(\boldsymbol y)=\bar u+\sum_{j\ge 1} y_j\,\psi_j$, where $\|\psi_j\|_X\le b_j$. The class $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)$ consists of maps $f:U\to Y$ that admit a bounded holomorphic extension to a $(\boldsymbol b,\varepsilon)$-admissible Bernstein polyellipse around $U$, with uniform bound $\le 1$. Set $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota=\{f\circ\iota^{-1}:f\in\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\}$.

(2) Fourier neural operator class $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$. For $\alpha>0$, $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ denotes the class of operators realizable as Fourier neural operators (a finite composition of affine lifting/projection layers and "Fourier layers" $v\mapsto\sigma(Wv+\mathcal{F}^{-1}(R\cdot\mathcal{F}v))$ with activation $\sigma$) whose architectural complexity (depth, width, number of retained Fourier modes, weight norms) is bounded by a budget controlled by a smoothness parameter $\alpha$.

Sampling width. For a class $\mathcal{K}$ of operators $X\to Y$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the order-$n$ sampling width in $L^2_\varrho$ by
$$s_n(\mathcal{K})_{L^2_\varrho} \;=\; \inf_{u_1,\dots,u_n\in X}\;\inf_{R}\;\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal{K}}\,\|\Psi-R(\Psi(u_1),\dots,\Psi(u_n))\|_{L^2_\varrho},$$
where $R$ ranges over all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps from $Y^n$ to operators $X\to Y$.

Problem. Establish a quantitative separation between the minimax behavior of $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$ and $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ in $L^2_\varrho$. Specifically, accomplish at least one of:

(a) Prove a lower bound on $s_n(\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}})_{L^2_\varrho}$ that is strictly larger (in its dependence on $n$) than the known upper bound on $s_n(\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota)_{L^2_\varrho}$, thereby exhibiting a genuine sample-complexity gap; or

(b) Show that every operator in $\mathcal{H}(\boldsymbol b)\circ\iota$ can be approximated, with quantitative rates in $n$, by a Fourier neural operator from $\mathcal{K}^\alpha_{\mathrm{FNO}}$ (for an appropriate $\alpha=\alpha(\boldsymbol b)$), thereby showing that the FNO class essentially contains the holomorphic class.

In either case, decide whether the two classes exhibit genuinely different sample-complexity behavior in $L^2_\varrho$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction in the operator-learning literature on minimax/sampling-width comparisons between holomorphic operator classes and Fourier neural operator classes. No published lower bounds on sampling widths of FNO classes nor a quantitative FNO-approximation theorem for holomorphic operator classes resolving this separation could be located, so the status is treated as open.

paper_title: A note on the convergence of RED algorithms under minimal hypotheses and open questions
context_brief: Classical RED convergence under RIC and restricted Lipschitz hypotheses
original_question: Consider the same inverse problem y = A x̂ + e with x̂ in a model set Σ, and let P_Σ be a generalized projection onto Σ. Classical regularization by denoising (RED) uses the iteration x_{n+1} = x_n − μAᵀ(Ax_n − y) − λ(x_n − P_Σ(x_n)). Assume the measurement operator satisfies a restricted isometry condition on the secant set Σ − Σ, and assume P_Σ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz condition with respect to Σ. Is it possible to prove convergence of the classical RED iterations in this RIC-and-restricted-Lipschitz theoretical setup under conditions less restrictive than the quasi-non-expansiveness route discussed in the source, which in the orthogonal-projection and atomic-norm setting leads to a sufficient-looking condition of the form δ(μ/(λ+θ) AᵀA)β + (θ/(λ+θ))δ(μ/θ AᵀA)C_Σ ≤ 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^m$ be a linear measurement operator and let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a (not necessarily convex) model set. Consider the inverse problem $y = A\hat x + e$, where $\hat x\in\Sigma$ and $e\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is a noise vector. Let $P_\Sigma:\mathbb{R}^N\to\Sigma$ be a generalized projection onto $\Sigma$ (a map satisfying $P_\Sigma(x)\in\Sigma$ for all $x$, and $P_\Sigma(x)=x$ for $x\in\Sigma$).

Define the secant set $\Sigma-\Sigma = \{x_1-x_2 : x_1,x_2\in\Sigma\}$. A linear operator $B$ is said to have restricted isometry constant $\delta(B)\in[0,1)$ on $\Sigma-\Sigma$ if 
$$\|(I-B)(x_1-x_2)\|^2 \le \delta\,\|x_1-x_2\|^2 \quad \text{for all } x_1,x_2\in\Sigma.$$
The projection $P_\Sigma$ is said to satisfy a restricted Lipschitz condition with respect to $\Sigma$ if there exists a constant $C_\Sigma\ge 0$ such that 
$$\|P_\Sigma(x) - P_\Sigma(x')\|\le C_\Sigma\|x-x'\| \quad \text{for appropriate pairs }(x,x'),$$
together with auxiliary control constants $\beta,\theta>0$ governing the interaction of $P_\Sigma$ with $\Sigma-\Sigma$.

Given step sizes $\mu,\lambda>0$, the classical Regularization by Denoising (RED) iterations are
$$x_{n+1} = x_n - \mu A^\top(Ax_n - y) - \lambda(x_n - P_\Sigma(x_n)).$$

Question: Under the standing assumptions that $A^\top A$ has a restricted isometry constant on $\Sigma-\Sigma$ and that $P_\Sigma$ satisfies a restricted Lipschitz property with respect to $\Sigma$, prove convergence of the RED iterates $\{x_n\}$ to a neighborhood of $\hat x$ (controlled by $\|e\|$) under hypotheses strictly less restrictive than the quasi-non-expansiveness sufficient condition
$$\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\lambda+\theta}A^\top A\right)\beta + \tfrac{\theta}{\lambda+\theta}\,\delta\!\left(\tfrac{\mu}{\theta}A^\top A\right)C_\Sigma \le 1.$$
Equivalently, identify a weaker sufficient condition (or prove that none is needed beyond the RIC and restricted Lipschitz assumptions) guaranteeing convergence of the classical RED iteration in this non-convex model-set setting.
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open question regarding convergence of classical RED under RIC and restricted Lipschitz hypotheses in non-convex model-set recovery. No published resolution was located; existing RED convergence results rely on stronger conditions such as quasi-non-expansiveness or convex regularizers.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can multiparty quantum key agreement protocols—protocols in which at least three mutually distrustful parties use quantum and authenticated classical channels to establish one common secret key collectively—be given a composable security framework comparable to modern quantum key distribution, in which the security definitions and proofs simultaneously capture external secrecy, fairness of all parties’ key contributions, and insider collusion, and in which the generated keys can be safely used inside arbitrary larger cryptographic systems?
self_contained_problem:
A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol is a cryptographic protocol in which n ≥ 3 mutually distrustful parties P_1, …, P_n, connected by quantum channels and by authenticated classical channels, jointly perform local quantum operations, measurements, and classical communication so as to produce a common bit string K ∈ {0,1}^ℓ, with the requirements that:

(i) Correctness: with high probability all honest parties output the same key K.
(ii) Fairness of contribution: every party contributes equally to K, in the sense that no proper subset S ⊊ {P_1, …, P_n} of (possibly dishonest) participants can, by itself, fix or bias the value of K beyond a negligible advantage.
(iii) External secrecy: any external eavesdropper interacting with the quantum and classical channels obtains only negligible information about K.
(iv) Robustness against insider collusion: even when up to t < n parties collude (and may share entanglement and arbitrary side information), they cannot determine, predict, or bias K beyond negligible advantage.

The problem is the following. Develop a composable security framework for MQKA, comparable in rigor and scope to the abstract-cryptography / Universal Composability style frameworks now standard for two-party quantum key distribution, satisfying all of the following:

(a) Define an ideal MQKA resource (functionality) that simultaneously formalizes external secrecy, fairness of contribution among all n parties, and resistance to arbitrary insider collusion of any subset of participants.

(b) Provide security definitions for concrete MQKA protocols expressed as the indistinguishability (in a suitable simulation-based or distinguishing-advantage sense) between the real protocol execution and the ideal MQKA resource, against adversaries that may corrupt any chosen subset of the n parties as well as the channels.

(c) Establish a composition theorem proving that any MQKA protocol meeting the above security definition can be safely used as a subroutine inside arbitrary larger cryptographic protocols, so that the resulting agreed key may be consumed by any subsequent protocol with at most a negligible loss in overall security.

(d) Exhibit at least one explicit MQKA protocol that provably realizes the ideal MQKA resource within this framework, with an explicit quantitative security bound.

Does such a composable security framework, together with a protocol realizing it, exist?
status_search_result: The question of giving MQKA a composable security treatment that simultaneously captures external secrecy, fairness, and insider collusion, with a composition theorem and an explicit realizing protocol, is identified in the source as an open problem; standard MQKA security analyses in the literature remain stand-alone rather than composable. No published work establishing such a full framework was located.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can bosonic quantum error-correcting encodings such as GKP, cat, and binomial codes be integrated into multiparty quantum key agreement so that key agreement is performed at the logical-qubit level on protected continuous-variable modes, while preserving distributed-protocol compatibility, fault-tolerant logical operations, compatible syndrome extraction, acceptable resource overheads, and fairness and security guarantees?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol in which N ≥ 3 spatially separated parties jointly generate a shared secret bit string K ∈ {0,1}^L through exchange of quantum states over noisy continuous-variable (CV) bosonic channels and authenticated classical communication. The protocol must satisfy:

(i) Correctness: with probability at least 1 − ε_c, all honest parties output the same key K.
(ii) Fairness: every honest party contributes equally to K, in the sense that no proper subset of parties can bias any bit of K.
(iii) Security: against any coalition of up to t < N dishonest parties and any external eavesdropper, the trace distance between the joint state of the key and the adversary's quantum side information and the ideal uniform-and-independent state is at most ε_s.

Bosonic encodings. For each CV mode, fix one of the following logical-qubit encodings into a single harmonic oscillator with quadratures (q̂, p̂):
 • GKP code: code states are (regularized) +1 eigenstates of the stabilizers e^{i 2√π q̂} and e^{i 2√π p̂}.
 • Cat code: even/odd superpositions of coherent states (|α⟩ ± |−α⟩)/N_±.
 • Binomial code: finite superpositions Σ_k √(C(N,k))/2^{N/2} |k(S+1)⟩ in the Fock basis with appropriate parameters (N, S).

Question. Does there exist an MQKA protocol with the following properties simultaneously?

(a) Logical-level execution: every key-generation operation (state preparation, entangling gate, measurement) is performed on logical qubits encoded in CV modes by one of the bosonic codes above.

(b) Fault tolerance: the logical Clifford operations and measurements used by the protocol admit a fault-tolerant implementation on the chosen bosonic code, with a syndrome-extraction circuit whose physical error per round is below the code's threshold.

(c) Distributed compatibility: the protocol remains executable when the N parties are connected by a network of lossy bosonic channels (transmissivity η < 1, thermal noise n̄ ≥ 0) together with local operations and classical communication, with no requirement of a central trusted node.

(d) Resource overhead: the number of physical bosonic modes, photons, and ancillas per generated secret bit is polynomial in N, log(1/ε_c), and log(1/ε_s).

(e) Fairness and security: properties (ii) and (iii) above hold with the stated parameters under a fully quantum adversary.

Provide such a protocol together with a proof of (a)–(e), or prove that no protocol simultaneously satisfying (a)–(e) exists for any of the three bosonic encodings.
status_search_result: No published construction integrates GKP/cat/binomial bosonic codes into a fully fault-tolerant multiparty quantum key agreement protocol with proven fairness, security, and polynomial overhead. The question is posed as a forward-looking open direction, and a targeted search did not surface a complete solution.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can multiparty quantum key agreement be integrated into quantum-internet control and networking stacks so that software-defined quantum networks can automatically select, route, schedule, and synthesize appropriate MQKA protocols based on the current network topology, available quantum resources, participant latency, security, and fairness requirements, device heterogeneity, and historical performance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a software-defined quantum network modeled as a time-varying graph G(t) = (V, E(t)) whose vertices V represent quantum-capable nodes (each with a heterogeneous device profile specifying available qubit registers, gate sets, memory coherence times, measurement bases, and entanglement-generation rates) and whose edges E(t) carry quantum and classical channels with time-dependent capacities, fidelities, and latencies. A multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol for a participant set S ⊆ V is an interactive procedure that outputs a common secret key k_S known to every member of S such that (i) every participant contributes equally to k_S (fairness), (ii) k_S is information-theoretically secret against any external eavesdropper and against any proper subset of dishonest insiders up to a specified threshold t < |S|, and (iii) the protocol terminates within a prescribed latency bound τ_S using only resources available on the induced subnetwork.

Let Π = {π_1, π_2, …} be a (possibly infinite) library of MQKA protocols, each π_i specified by its participant-size range, required topology (e.g. star, ring, complete, GHZ-distribution tree), per-round quantum and classical resource cost, achievable fairness model, security threshold, and latency profile.

Design a control-plane decision procedure A that, given as input
  • the current network state G(t) together with per-node device profiles,
  • a request (S, τ_S, σ_S, φ_S) consisting of a participant set S, a latency budget τ_S, a security level σ_S, and a fairness requirement φ_S,
  • a history H of past protocol executions with measured performance metrics,
outputs in polynomial time
  (a) a selected protocol π* ∈ Π (or a synthesized protocol expressed as a circuit/message-flow program),
  (b) a routing assignment of the quantum and classical messages of π* onto the edges of G(t),
  (c) a schedule that coexists with all other concurrently admitted MQKA sessions without enabling key-reuse attacks or violating resource contention constraints,
such that the realized execution of π* on G(t) provably satisfies the requested fairness, security threshold, and latency bound, and is competitive (within a guaranteed multiplicative factor) with the optimal offline choice over Π for the same request.

Does such a decision procedure A exist, and if so, what are the achievable competitive ratios and complexity bounds? In particular, is the joint problem of automated MQKA selection, routing, scheduling, and on-the-fly protocol synthesis decidable, and is it tractable under realistic resource and adversary models?
status_search_result: No published work demonstrates an automated control-plane procedure that selects, routes, schedules, and synthesizes MQKA protocols in software-defined quantum networks under the joint constraints described. Existing literature on quantum network control planes (e.g., QNodeOS, SeQUeNCe, NetSquid orchestration) and MQKA protocol design treats these problems separately, and rapid automated synthesis of MQKA protocols is generally identified as a future-research direction rather than an accomplished result.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can twin-field multiparty quantum key agreement, in which multiple parties send phase-encoded weak coherent pulses to a central interference station so that the final key depends symmetrically on all users’ phases, be scaled beyond small groups of three or four users while preserving strong fairness, handling multi-photon events from several parties, and securing the central station as an untrusted relay?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a twin-field multiparty quantum key agreement (TF-MQKA) protocol defined as follows. Let n ≥ 3 mutually distrustful parties P_1, …, P_n each prepare phase-encoded weak coherent pulses |α e^{iϕ_k}⟩ with chosen phases ϕ_k ∈ [0, 2π), and transmit them through lossy quantum channels to a single central interference (measurement) station, treated as an untrusted relay. The station performs single-photon interference measurements whose detection statistics depend on the global phase combination e^{i(ϕ_1 + ⋯ + ϕ_n)}, and announces classical outcomes from which the parties distill a shared secret key K such that K is a symmetric function of (ϕ_1, …, ϕ_n).

Call the protocol strongly fair if no proper subset S ⊊ {1, …, n} of colluding parties can bias, predetermine, or learn nontrivial information about the final key K beyond what a single honest party contributes; that is, the distribution of K conditioned on any choice of inputs by S remains uniformly determined by the contributions of the honest parties. Call the protocol secure under an untrusted relay if no strategy by the central station (including arbitrary measurements and classical announcements) leaks information about K to an eavesdropper above a vanishing bound, and call it robust to multi-photon events if the security and key-rate analysis remains valid when two or more parties simultaneously contribute photons to the interference.

Problem: Construct, for arbitrary n, a TF-MQKA protocol of the above form that simultaneously
(i) achieves strong fairness against any coalition of up to n − 1 dishonest parties,
(ii) is provably secure against an untrusted central station,
(iii) correctly accounts for multi-photon contributions from multiple parties in its security proof, and
(iv) preserves the single-photon-interference distance-scaling advantage of two-party twin-field QKD (i.e. key rate scaling as O(√η) in the total channel transmittance η rather than O(η)),
or else prove that no such protocol can satisfy all four properties for sufficiently large n.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2024 preprint on twin-field-based multi-party quantum key agreement and reviews of MQKA architectures) indicates that existing TF-MQKA frameworks demonstrate feasibility only for three or four users, with explicit remarks that extending to N > 3 parties is nontrivial due to misalignment issues and exponential growth in combinatorics of participant choices. Strong fairness, untrusted-relay security, and rigorous handling of multi-photon contributions for general n have not been jointly resolved, so the problem appears open.

paper_title: Multiparty Quantum Key Agreement: Architectures, State-of-the-art, and Open Problems
original_question: Can high-dimensional multiparty quantum key agreement protocols that replace qubits with d-level qudits realize higher information density and key rates in noisy multiparty networks while still preserving fairness and security, given the engineering difficulty of generating high-quality d-dimensional entangled states, performing stable d-ary encodings, and measuring in high-dimensional bases?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multiparty quantum key agreement (MQKA) protocol involving N ≥ 3 parties who wish to jointly establish a shared secret key such that (i) every participant contributes equally to the final key (fairness: no proper subset of parties can predetermine the key), and (ii) the protocol is secure against both external eavesdroppers and dishonest internal participants (with security quantified, e.g., by an exponentially small trace distance between the real protocol output and an ideal uniformly random key conditioned on the adversary's quantum side information). Standard MQKA protocols use qubit (d = 2) carriers. A high-dimensional MQKA protocol replaces these qubits with d-level qudits (d ≥ 3), encoding key information in mutually unbiased bases of ℂ^d and distributing multipartite entangled qudit states (e.g., generalized GHZ states |GHZ_d^N⟩ = (1/√d) Σ_{j=0}^{d-1} |j⟩^{⊗N}) among the N parties.

Problem. Design and rigorously analyze a high-dimensional MQKA protocol with the following properties, or prove that no such protocol exists under reasonable physical assumptions:

(a) For a fixed number M of transmitted quantum carriers and a fixed channel noise model (e.g., depolarizing channel with single-qudit error rate p, or a multipartite analogue), the asymptotic secret-key rate R(d, N, p) (bits of secure shared key per transmitted carrier) strictly exceeds the corresponding rate R(2, N, p) achievable by any qubit-based MQKA protocol on the same network, for some non-trivial regime of p.

(b) The protocol satisfies fairness in the above sense, with composable security against coalitions of up to N − 1 dishonest participants colluding with an external adversary.

(c) Quantify the threshold noise level p*(d, N) below which positive secret-key generation is possible, and determine how p*(d, N) scales with d and N.

Establish such a protocol together with its security proof and rate analysis, or provide an impossibility result delimiting the achievable trade-off between dimension d, fairness, and noise tolerance in multiparty networks.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in multiparty quantum key agreement. While individual high-dimensional QKD and some bipartite/multiparty qudit-based key agreement schemes have been proposed in the literature, no comprehensive, fairness-preserving, composably secure high-dimensional MQKA protocol with a proven advantage in noise tolerance and key rate over qubit MQKA appears to be established. The status is best described as open.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: If G is an Erdős–Rényi random graph distributed as G(n, 1/2), is its Lovász number asymptotically equal to √n in expectation, namely E[ϑ(G)] = (1 + o(1))√n as n → ∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$ denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph on the vertex set $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which every edge of the complete graph $K_n$ is included independently with probability $1/2$. For a finite simple graph $H = (V, E)$, the Lovász theta number $\vartheta(H)$ is defined by
$$\vartheta(H) = \max \sum_{i,j \in V} \langle u_i, u_j \rangle,$$
where the maximum ranges over all unit vectors $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and families $(u_i)_{i \in V}$ of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for any dimension $d \ge 1$) satisfying $\langle u_i, u_i \rangle = \langle c, u_i \rangle$ for every $i \in V$ and $\langle u_i, u_j \rangle = 0$ for every edge $\{i,j\} \in E$. Equivalently, $\vartheta(H)$ is the optimum of the standard semidefinite program associated with the Lovász number.

Prove or disprove the following asymptotic: as $n \to \infty$,
$$\mathbb{E}\,\vartheta(G) = (1 + o(1))\sqrt{n}.$$
status_search_result: The precise asymptotics of $\mathbb{E}\,\vartheta(G(n,1/2))$ remain open. Juhász established the order $\Theta(\sqrt{n/p})$ for a wide range of $p$, and recent work (e.g., on random circulant graphs and partial bounds) has narrowed the upper bound to $O(\sqrt{n}\log\log n)$ with matching lower bound up to constants, but the conjectured sharp constant $1$ in front of $\sqrt{n}$ has not been confirmed.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Fix M and let N = 4M − 5. Draw a complex matrix A ∈ C^{N×M} at random so that im(A) is uniformly distributed over the Grassmannian of M-dimensional subspaces of C^{4M−5} (for example, A may have i.i.d. Gaussian entries). If p_M denotes the probability that the phaseless measurement map x mod 𝕋 ↦ |Ax|^2 is injective, must one have (a) p_M < 1 for every M and (b) p_M → 0 as M → ∞?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer M ≥ 2 and set N = 4M − 5. Let A ∈ C^{N×M} be a random complex matrix whose image im(A) is distributed according to the unique unitarily invariant (Haar) probability measure on the Grassmannian of M-dimensional complex subspaces of C^{N} (equivalently, A may be taken to have i.i.d. complex Gaussian entries). Consider the phaseless measurement map

  Φ_A : C^M / 𝕋 → R^N,  [x] ↦ (|(Ax)_1|^2, …, |(Ax)_N|^2),

where 𝕋 = {e^{iθ} : θ ∈ R} acts on C^M by global phase. Let

  p_M := Pr(Φ_A is injective on C^M / 𝕋).

Prove or disprove the following two claims:
(a) p_M < 1 for every M ≥ 2.
(b) lim_{M→∞} p_M = 0.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture on the Randomstrasse101 open-problems list (Stable Phase Retrieval, Problems 19–21). It is known in the complex case that 4M−4 generic measurements suffice for injectivity, but at the threshold N = 4M−5 the probability of generic injectivity is conjectured to be strictly less than 1 and to tend to 0 as M → ∞. No proof or disproof has been located in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: If A is a real matrix with i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries in the phase-retrieval setting above, what is the typical value of the stability quantity ω(A) = min_{S ⊆ [N] : rank(A_{S^c}) < M} σ_M(A_S)? In particular, does ω(A) satisfy a bound of the type conjectured above, and if so, what exponent β is valid?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a real matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times M}$ with rows $A_1,\dots,A_N$, and for any subset $S\subseteq [N]:=\{1,\dots,N\}$, let $A_S\in\mathbb{R}^{|S|\times M}$ denote the submatrix of rows indexed by $S$, and let $\sigma_M(A_S)$ denote its smallest (i.e., $M$-th) singular value (with $\sigma_M(A_S)=0$ when $|S|<M$). Define the stability quantity
$$\omega(A)\;=\;\min_{\substack{S\subseteq[N]\\ \operatorname{rank}(A_{S^c})<M}}\sigma_M(A_S),$$
where $S^c=[N]\setminus S$.

Specialize to $N=2M-1$, and consider the conjecture: there exist universal constants $C>0$ and $0<\beta<1$ such that for every $M\ge 2$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ in which every $M$ rows are linearly independent,
$$\omega(A)\;\le\;C\,\max_{k\in[N]}\|A_k\|\,\beta^M.$$

Question. Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{(2M-1)\times M}$ have i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. Determine the typical value (e.g., the order of magnitude with high probability as $M\to\infty$) of $\omega(A)$. In particular, decide whether $\omega(A)$ satisfies a bound of the form $\omega(A)\le C\,\max_k\|A_k\|\,\beta^M$ with high probability, and if so identify the optimal admissible exponent $\beta\in(0,1)$.
status_search_result: The problem is presented as an open question with no known resolution; the typical value of ω(A) for Gaussian matrices and the optimal β in the associated stability conjecture for N=2M−1 phase retrieval do not appear to have been determined in the literature. Recent surveys on phase retrieval stability (e.g., 2024–2025) discuss the conjecture but do not report a solution.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Can one prove nonexistence of seven mutually unbiased bases in C^6 using a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares certificate? Equivalently, is there a degree-4 SoS proof that no collection of 7 × 6 vectors in C^6 can satisfy the mutually unbiased basis constraints for seven bases?
self_contained_problem:
A set of orthonormal bases $B_1, \dots, B_m$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$, with $B_k = \{v_1^{(k)}, \dots, v_d^{(k)}\}$, is called a collection of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if for every pair of distinct bases $k \ne \ell$ and every pair of indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, d\}$,
$$|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{d}.$$
For $d = 6$, it is a long-standing open question whether more than three MUBs can exist; in particular, no seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ are known. Encode the existence of seven MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$ as a system of polynomial equations in the real and imaginary parts of the entries of $7 \times 6$ vectors of $\mathbb{C}^6$, consisting of:
(i) the unit-norm and orthogonality constraints making each of the seven sets of six vectors an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^6$, and
(ii) the unbiasedness constraints $|\langle v_i^{(k)}, v_j^{(\ell)} \rangle|^2 = 1/6$ for all $k \ne \ell$ and all $i,j$.

A degree-$2t$ Sum-of-Squares (SoS) refutation of this system is an identity
$$-1 = \sigma_0(x) + \sum_a \sigma_a(x)\, p_a(x),$$
where $\{p_a = 0\}$ are the polynomial constraints above (or their natural reformulation), each $\sigma_a$ is a sum of squares of real polynomials, and the total degree of every term $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_a p_a$ is at most $2t$.

Question: Does there exist a degree-$4$ Sum-of-Squares refutation certifying that no seven mutually unbiased bases exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$?
category_tag: Sum-of-Squares hierarchy and mutually unbiased bases
status_search_result: The problem appears open. Prior work has shown that degree-2 SoS / low-level relaxations cannot rule out 7 MUBs in dimension 6, and numerical evidence in related work suggests SoS refutations for stronger statements (e.g. >3 MUBs) may require very high degree (≥12). Whether a degree-4 SoS certificate suffices to refute 7 MUBs in C^6 has not been resolved in the literature found.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Let G_p be the Paley graph on a prime number p ≡ 1 (mod 4), and let ω(G_p) be its clique number. Is ω(G_p) bounded by a polylogarithmic function of p, i.e. does ω(G_p) = O(polylog(p)) hold?
self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, the Paley graph $G_p$ is the graph whose vertex set is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$, with two distinct vertices $x,y \in \mathbb{F}_p$ joined by an edge if and only if $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo $p$ (this relation is symmetric because $-1$ is a square modulo $p$). Let $\omega(G_p)$ denote the clique number of $G_p$, i.e. the largest size of a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ such that $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue for every pair of distinct elements $x, y \in S$.

Determine whether $\omega(G_p)$ grows at most polylogarithmically in $p$. Specifically, do there exist absolute constants $C > 0$ and $k \geq 1$ such that
$$\omega(G_p) \leq C (\log p)^k$$
for every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$? Equivalently, is $\omega(G_p) = O(\mathrm{polylog}(p))$?
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. The best known unconditional upper bound is $\omega(G_p) \leq (1+o(1))\sqrt{p/2}$ due to Hanson and Petridis (2021), far from polylogarithmic. Recent work by Kunisky and Yu (2023) shows the degree-4 sum-of-squares relaxation has value at least $\Omega(p^{1/3})$, so SOS-based methods alone cannot establish a polylog bound at low degree. No proof or refutation of the polylogarithmic conjecture has been reported.

paper_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
original_question: Let G_{p,2} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to both 0 and 1 (the 2-localization). For sufficiently large primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4), is its Lovász theta number at most (2/3)√p, i.e. does ϑ(G_{p,2}) ≤ (2/3)√p hold?
self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $G_p$ denote the Paley graph on vertex set $\mathbb{F}_p$, in which two distinct vertices $x,y$ are adjacent iff $x-y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue in $\mathbb{F}_p$. Define the 2-localization $G_{p,2}$ to be the induced subgraph of $G_p$ on the set of vertices that are adjacent (in $G_p$) to both $0$ and $1$. Let $\vartheta(H)$ denote the Lovász theta number of a graph $H$.

Prove or disprove: there exists $p_0$ such that for every prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ with $p \geq p_0$,
$$\vartheta(G_{p,2}) \leq \tfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{p}.$$

original_question: Consider the Paley equiangular tight frame associated with a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4). Does this deterministic frame satisfy a restricted isometry property beyond the square-root bottleneck: namely, is there some ε > 0 such that for m ≍ p^{1/2+ε}, every submatrix formed by choosing m distinct frame vectors has condition number bounded by a constant independent of p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and let $\chi$ denote the quadratic (Legendre) character on $\mathbb{F}_p$, extended by $\chi(0)=0$. The Paley equiangular tight frame is the collection of $N=p$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{C}^n$ (with $n=(p-1)/2$, or equivalently the $p\times n$ Paley ETF matrix obtained by an explicit normalization of rows of the Paley conference matrix) such that the inner product of any two distinct vectors has modulus exactly $\sqrt{(N-n)/(n(N-1))}=1/\sqrt{p}$ and the frame is tight.

Equivalently, form the $n \times p$ matrix $\Phi$ whose columns are these unit vectors. For an integer $m \le p$ and a subset $S \subset \{1,\dots,p\}$ with $|S|=m$, let $\Phi_S$ denote the $n \times m$ submatrix of $\Phi$ with columns indexed by $S$, and let $\kappa(\Phi_S)$ denote its condition number (the ratio of its largest to its smallest singular value).

$$\kappa(\Phi_S) \le C ?$$

Equivalently, does the Paley equiangular tight frame satisfy the restricted isometry property at sparsity $m \asymp p^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, breaking the square-root bottleneck?

context_brief: Sharp asymptotics for graph matrix norms
original_question: Fix a finite shape α and let M_α be the associated graph matrix built from injective realizations of α into [n], with entries given by products of the corresponding edge-sign variables ε_{i,j}. Do there exist functions f(α) and g(α), depending only on α, such that the expected operator norm satisfies E||M_α|| = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)})? In particular, can one determine the correct polynomial exponent and the correct polylogarithmic factor for every fixed shape α?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite "shape" α, defined as a graph on a vertex set partitioned into two ordered tuples (left and right boundary vertices) U_α and V_α together with additional internal vertices W_α, with edge set E(α). For each integer n ≥ 1 let {ε_{i,j} : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n} be independent ±1 (or independent standard Gaussian) random variables, with ε_{j,i}=ε_{i,j}. The graph matrix M_α associated to α is the matrix whose rows are indexed by injective tuples I ∈ [n]^{|U_α|} and columns by injective tuples J ∈ [n]^{|V_α|}, with entry
   (M_α)_{I,J} = Σ_{φ} ∏_{{u,v} ∈ E(α)} ε_{φ(u),φ(v)},
where the sum runs over all injective maps φ from the vertex set of α into [n] that extend the given assignments on U_α and V_α, and the entry is 0 unless I and J are disjoint as required.

Question: For every fixed shape α, do there exist constants f(α) ∈ ℝ and g(α) ∈ ℝ, depending only on α, such that the expected operator (spectral) norm satisfies
   E‖M_α‖ = Θ(n^{f(α)} (log n)^{g(α)})
as n → ∞? Equivalently, determine the exact polynomial exponent f(α) and the exact polylogarithmic exponent g(α) for every fixed shape α.

The conjecture of sharp Θ(n^{f(α)}(log n)^{g(α)}) asymptotics appears to remain open in general.

original_question: Describe the divisors of the following subclasses of finite 0-simple semigroups: (1) finite Brandt semigroups; and (2) finite 0-simple semigroups given in Rees matrix form by a matrix whose entries are only 0 and 1.
self_contained_problem:
A finite semigroup S with zero is called 0-simple if S^2 ≠ {0} and S has no two-sided ideals other than {0} and S. By the Rees theorem every finite 0-simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup M^0(G; I, Λ; P) over a finite group G, with index sets I and Λ and a regular Λ×I sandwich matrix P with entries in G ∪ {0}. A finite Brandt semigroup is a finite 0-simple inverse semigroup; equivalently, it is a Rees matrix semigroup M^0(G; I, I; P) with P the I×I identity matrix over G.

Recall that a semigroup T is called a divisor of a semigroup S if T is a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup of S. For a class K of semigroups let D(K) denote the class of all divisors of members of K, i.e. all semigroups isomorphic to a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup of some S ∈ K.

(1) K is the class of all finite Brandt semigroups.

(2) K is the class of all finite 0-simple semigroups whose sandwich matrix in some Rees matrix representation has all entries equal to 0 or 1 (i.e. M^0({1}; I, Λ; P) with P a 0–1 matrix, viewed as a Rees matrix semigroup over the trivial group).

original_question: Describe the identities satisfied by the full transformation semigroup T(n) on an n-element set.
self_contained_problem:

The set of all identities satisfied by $T(n)$ generates the equational theory (variety) of $T(n)$.

original_question: Let c(u) be the number of distinct letters occurring in a non-blocking word u, and let m(u) be the smallest alphabet size for which there exists an infinite word avoiding all substitution images of u. Determine m(u) for a non-blocking word u containing c(u) letters.

A word $u \in A^+$ is called blocking if every sufficiently long word over any finite alphabet contains a substitution image of $u$ (equivalently, no infinite word over any finite alphabet avoids all substitution images of $u$); otherwise $u$ is called non-blocking.

original_question: Determine when a system of identical inequalities, also called identical relations of precedence, is equivalent to a system of identities for ordered semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(S,\cdot,\le)$ be an ordered semigroup, i.e. a semigroup equipped with a partial order $\le$ that is compatible with multiplication: $a\le b$ implies $ca\le cb$ and $ac\le bc$ for all $a,b,c\in S$. 

For variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$, an identical inequality (also called an identical relation of precedence) on a class $\mathcal{K}$ of ordered semigroups is an expression $u(x_1,\dots,x_n)\le v(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, where $u,v$ are semigroup words, that holds in every $S\in\mathcal{K}$ for every substitution of $x_i$ by elements of $S$. An identity is an expression $u=v$ that holds for every such substitution. A system $\Sigma$ of identical inequalities is said to be equivalent to a system $\mathcal{I}$ of identities (over the class of all ordered semigroups) if a given ordered semigroup satisfies all members of $\Sigma$ if and only if it satisfies all members of $\mathcal{I}$.

Problem: Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a system $\Sigma=\{u_i\le v_i : i\in I\}$ of identical inequalities under which there exists a system of identities equivalent to $\Sigma$ in the class of ordered semigroups. (The case $|I|=1$, i.e. systems consisting of a single identical inequality, is known to be settled.)

paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
context_brief: Sublattice and upper-semilattice behavior of inclusive varieties
original_question: Describe: (1) classes of semigroups in which elementary inclusive varieties form a sublattice of the lattice of inclusive varieties; and (2) nonelementary inclusive varieties that form an upper subsemilattice in the lattice of inclusive varieties within the class of periodic semigroups.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let S be a semigroup. An inclusion is a formal expression of the form u ⊆ v, where u and v are words in a countable alphabet of variables; S satisfies the inclusion u ⊆ v if for every assignment of the variables to elements of S the value of u (interpreted as the singleton consisting of the resulting product) is contained in the subsemigroup generated by the value of v. A class V of semigroups is called an inclusive variety if it is the class of all semigroups satisfying some fixed set Σ of inclusions. The collection L of all inclusive varieties (within a fixed universe of semigroups) forms a complete lattice under inclusion. An inclusive variety is called elementary if it can be defined by a single inclusion u ⊆ v in which the right-hand word v consists of a single variable (equivalently, by inclusions whose right-hand side is a single letter); otherwise it is called nonelementary.

It is known that within the class of finite abelian groups the elementary inclusive varieties form a sublattice of the lattice of all inclusive varieties, and the nonelementary inclusive varieties form an upper subsemilattice (i.e. a join-subsemilattice) of that lattice.

Problem.
(1) Describe all classes K of semigroups with the property that, when the lattice of inclusive varieties is restricted to K, the elementary inclusive varieties form a sublattice of the lattice of inclusive varieties.
(2) Within the class of periodic semigroups (semigroups in which every element has finite order, i.e. some power is idempotent-generating), characterize all nonelementary inclusive varieties that together form an upper subsemilattice of the lattice of inclusive varieties.

original_question: For the main classes of mathematical structures and natural pargoids of transformations, determine: (1) the classes of structures defined up to isomorphism by these pargoids; and (2) pargoids of transformations that are determined up to isomorphism by their endomorphism semigroup or automorphism group.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a nonempty set and let T(X) denote the monoid of all self-maps X → X under composition. By a pargoid of transformations on X we mean any subset P ⊆ T(X) (typically closed under composition, so a subsemigroup of T(X), and possibly satisfying additional natural closure conditions such as containing the identity, being closed under inverses when applicable, etc.). Given a mathematical structure A on the underlying set X (for example, a partially ordered set, lattice, topological space, graph, group, ring, vector space, module, metric space, etc.), several "natural" pargoids are associated to A, such as:
 • End(A), the semigroup of all endomorphisms of A,
 • Aut(A), the group of all automorphisms of A,
 • the semigroup of all closure operators on A (when A is a poset),
 • the semigroup of all continuous self-maps (when A is a topological space),
 • the semigroup of all order-preserving self-maps (when A is a poset),
and similar canonical constructions.

Two structures A and B (of the same type) on possibly different underlying sets are said to be determined up to isomorphism by an associated pargoid construction P(·) if whenever P(A) and P(B) are isomorphic (as semigroups, or as groups in the case of automorphism groups), there exists an isomorphism A ≅ B of the structures.

Solve the following two problems for the main natural classes C of mathematical structures (posets, lattices, topological spaces, graphs, groups, rings, modules, metric spaces, etc.) and the main natural pargoid constructions P:

(1) Characterise, for each pair (C, P), the subclass of structures A ∈ C that are determined up to isomorphism by their pargoid P(A).

(2) Characterise the pargoids of transformations on a set X that are themselves determined up to isomorphism (as a pargoid) by their endomorphism semigroup End(P) or by their automorphism group Aut(P).

(A known partial result, due to E. S. Lyapin, is that every partially ordered set is determined up to isomorphism by the pargoid of its closure operators.)

While many individual instances have been resolved (e.g., classical results that distributive lattices, certain topological spaces, graphs, and modules can be recovered from their endomorphism monoids — work of Magill, McKenzie, Schein, Wiegandt, and others), the general program of classifying all natural (class, pargoid) pairs for which the determination holds remains open and is treated as a long-standing research direction rather than a single closed theorem.
